**Amended 2026-10-02: fact 5 past a guard** (`Spec.guardNames`; `plans/runtime-in-beni.md`, *The
empty page's last items*). Fact 3's guard narrows what an object chain *points to* inside a
branch; fact 5 learns the same of a local's *value* after one. A statement `if (T) â¦` whose first
arm cannot complete normally â its last statement a `throw`, a `return`, a `break` or a `continue`
â is followed by the rest of its list only when `T` was false. Then every disjunct of `T`'s
top-level `||` chain was evaluated, was false, and did not throw, so a local `X` is *nonnull* for
the rest of that list (and inside what the rest makes, closures included) when some disjunct is
`X == null`, or when some disjunct reads a property of `X` (`X.p`, `X[k]`) where it is evaluated
whenever the disjunct is â not in the right side of an `&&` or `||`, not in a conditional's arms,
not in a function. `X === null` alone proves nothing: `X` may be `undefined`. The local must be
declared once and assigned nowhere in its declaration, so the value the guard saw is the one every
later read sees, and a `function` declared in the rest sees no guard, since it is hoisted above
it. What it buys is what fact 5 already spends: a parameter every call passes such a local is
nonnull (fact 1), and so is a field every write gives it (fact 4's join). On the empty page,
`run`'s `if (d === null || d.$$root !== undefined) throw â¦` makes the body it hands `mount`
nonnull, so the slot's `p` is: `parentOf`'s `d.p === null ? d.m.parentNode : d.p` is `d.p`, and the
slot's `m`, read by nothing now, goes from its literal. Measured (release, brotli, the whole
bundle): the empty `browser` page and `Tea.sandbox` 480 â **466**, `Tea.element` 1 241 â 1 232,
with effects 5 325 â 5 316, `random` 1 992 â 1 997 (raw â33); 21 of the 52 `browser/` pages
smaller, none larger (â280 in all); the `bench/ui` app and every `run/` program byte-identical.
Fixtures: `emit/release/app/SpecGuards`, `run/SpecializeGuards` (a guard that refuses only
`undefined`, given `null`, keeps the fallback), `emit/release/split/EmptyPage`.

**Amended 2026-10-03: definite initialisation** (`Pts.definiteInit`; the empty page's study,
ledger step 13). Fact 3 learns, per object literal, the keys it lacks that no code can read before
they are written â so a read of one is never the `undefined` of a key not yet there, exactly as
for a key the literal has (*What fact 3 learns*, above). A key `k` is such a key of literal `O`
when:

- `O` is the value of a `return` of a function `F` as it is made (`return {â¦}`), so the call is
  the only way `O` leaves `F`;
- `F` does not escape and nothing but the program's calls calls it â not the entry file, not a
  `new` â and it has at least one call;
- **every** call that may call `F` (by fact 3's call graph) is the initialiser of a `const x` or
  `let x`, and the statements right after that binding begin with a run of `x.p = v`, one of which
  writes `k`, each `v` before it â and `v` itself â evaluated without running code, throwing or
  reading `x`: a literal, a name other than `x`, or a property read through objects that are all
  the program's own, none escaped (no getter) and none `null` or `undefined`.

Between the call and the write no code runs and nothing but `x` holds the new object, so no read
can see `k` missing. What a site may hold does not depend on these keys â only whether a read may
be `undefined` does â so the call graph that found them is the one they leave: the analysis is run
again with them, up to three times while it finds more. Nothing is rewritten that facts 3â6 did
not already rewrite: they now fire where an object is finished by its caller. On the empty page
`unit`'s `i.t = b.t; i.b = b` makes `t` and `b` keys of the instance the kind's `m` returns, so
fact 6 decides `patch`'s `b === i.b` (`true`): `patch` is `(a)=>a`, its two other arms go, and
with them the kind's `p`; `unit`'s two writes, read by nothing now, go too, the read `b.t` with
them â **a write fact 3 drops keeps its value as a statement only when evaluating it may do
something**, and a read through program objects (`Pts.safeChain`) does nothing. `swap` and `drop`
stay: `place`'s `else` is reached only from a branch that tested `s.i` was `null`, which no fact
sees through a call. Measured (release, brotli, the whole bundle): the empty `browser` page and
`Tea.sandbox` **605 â 557**; `Tea.element`, effects, the `bench/ui` app and every `run/` program
byte-identical. Fixtures: `emit/release/app/SpecInit` (a kind's instance finished by `unit`, and a
literal one of whose two calls writes nothing), `run/SpecializeInit` (the same, and a write whose
value reads the key it writes through a call â red when a call counts as harmless),
`emit/release/split/EmptyPage`.

**Slice 6 â a declaration's object as a constant** (*added 2026-10-03*; the empty page's study,
ledger step 20, *constant propagation through non-escaping literals*). Facts 1, 2 and 4 joined
only literals; a field that always holds `view`, a parameter every call passes the module's one
block, were â¤ or *nonnull*. The lattice gains a constant kind, **`name`**: the object or function
a top-level declaration makes â a `function`, or a `const` whose initialiser is an arrow, an object
or an array literal, which nothing assigns and which is declared once. A read of such a name is
that constant; two different declarations make two different objects, so `===` of two names is
decided, and a name is never `null`, a primitive or falsy. It flows as the literals do: a
parameter every call passes it (fact 1), a `const` or `let` it initialises (fact 2), a field every
write gives it (fact 4, with fact 4's conditions: read through a chain of program objects that
nothing unseen holds, the key present from the start). And it is spent as they are: the read, the
parameter or the field is written as the name. **Written where the module has it**: a module
names another's declaration only through an `import`, so the name is written only in a module
that already mentions it â or, when the build is one scope-hoisted file (*One scope-hoisted file
under `--release`*), anywhere, every top-level name being one binding of the one scope (Emit asks
whether it will be before specialising; specialisation only shrinks what the hand-written files
must keep, so the answer cannot change). A read `o.f(x)` written `f(x)` loses its receiver, which
nothing emitted reads: no function of the program uses `this`. Measured (release, brotli, the
whole bundle): the empty `browser` page and `Tea.sandbox` 557 â **550** (`a.view(d)` is the
page's `view` called by name, the kind's `m` called through the kind's name), `Tea.element`
1 261 â 1 253, with effects 5 412 â 5 405, the `bench/ui` app 5 723 â 5 700; `bench/size.mjs`'s
release total over `run/` â911 (`WideRecordDerivedEq` â541: its evidence records' fields are
named functions). Fixtures: `emit/release/app/SpecScalars` (`run`'s `shape.measure 3`),
`run/SpecializeScalars` (a field every construction gives one function, and one two give two),
`emit/release/app/OneLine`, `emit/release/split/EmptyPage`.

**Slice 7 â scalar replacement** (*added 2026-10-03*; ledger step 19). A local `const x = {â¦}` (or
a `let` nothing reassigns) of an object literal of plain keys â no spread, no computed key â whose
every mention in its top-level declaration is `x.k`, read or written by an assignment, for a key
`k` of its literal, and which that declaration declares once, is never made: each key is a
binding, `const` (or `let` when a write reaches it) in the literal's order, so every value is
evaluated once, where and in the order the literal evaluated it, and `x.k` is the binding. A key
never written whose value is an atom â a literal of at most 5 bytes or read once, or a name
nothing assigns and the declaration declares once â is that atom where it is read; a key nothing
reads whose value does nothing goes. Nothing but those reads and writes can see the object, so
nothing can tell; a closure that reads `x.k` reads the binding, which it shares with the function
as it shared the object. A binding lowering kept for its initialiser's effect (`effect_keep`) keeps
each key's binding whose value may have one. It runs after the facts and *A function called once*,
which is where most such objects appear: a record a helper built, now in its caller's `let`.
Measured: `run/` programs' release brotli â185 more in all; every page and the app unchanged (their
objects reach a call). Fixtures: `emit/release/app/SpecScalars` (`area`'s record, and `kept`'s,
passed to a function called twice, made), `run/SpecializeScalars` (a field a closure reads later;
in a loop, a record whose field is the loop's variable, read by closures after the loop â each
sees its turn's value, which a substitution of the reassigned variable would lose),
`emit/release/app/InlineAfter`, `emit/release/app/SpecFields`.

**Slice 8 â a small function, wherever it is called** (*added 2026-10-03*; ledger steps 12 and 17,
`plans/runtime-in-beni.md`'s *Append against Solid 1*). *A function called once* takes a body in
at one call; a function called from many places paid a call at each, an identity included
(`patch` once definite initialisation decides it, `update = Î»_ m -> m`, `Html.map`'s tagger
`identity`). Under `--release`, after the facts:

- **Which functions.** A function whose body is one `return e`, where `e` holds no function and no
  `yield`, names nothing but its parameters and whole-program names (not itself), and declares no
  parameter twice: a top-level `const f = (â¦) => e` nothing assigns, or **the one function a call
  reaches through a property** â `kind.m(â¦)`, `program.update(m, s)` â when fact 3 says the callee
  may be that one function only, and reading it does nothing (`Pts.safeChain`: no getter, no
  throw). Program functions read no `this`, so the receiver is not missed.
- **Which calls.** Each argument is an *atom* â a literal (of at most 5 bytes, or read once) or a
  name nothing assigns (`atomArgument`: such a name is the same value wherever the body reads it,
  and the body is written where the call was, in the same scope) â or an argument nothing reads
  that does nothing, or **one** argument read exactly once by `e` whose read is the first thing
  `e` evaluates that could do anything, and is evaluated whenever `e` is (`firstUse`: before it
  only names, literals and `===`; never in a branch of `?:`, `&&` or `||`, nor in a function); then
  every other argument must be a name or a literal. So each argument is evaluated once, and in the
  order it was: what an atom's evaluation could not tell moved, and the one argument that does
  something stays first.
- **The size model.** The call is replaced only when `e`, its parameters replaced, prints in no
  more bytes than the call by an estimate (short names one byte, a property its name's length,
  operators their text, brackets and commas) â an identity, a function returning a name, a wrapper
  of another call. A function every call of which is replaced is then unreferenced and goes.

The facts are then asked again (`Spec.grow` sizes their tables to the copied nodes): a constant
now passed, a field of a literal now read, folds â `scale 1 n` written in is `n`, `measure 3` is
`10`. With them, **`x.p = x.p`** on program objects â an identity written in place, `a.i =
patch(a.i, b)` â goes (no getter, no setter, no throw: `safeChain`). The passes â small
functions, functions called once, scalar replacement, then the facts â repeat at most three times
while one finds something. A name a copied body adds to a module is a property name the session's
pool already numbered (`Pts.propId` finds it in the module it came from).

*Amended 2026-10-22 (issue #781): the projection.* A read `p.k` in the body, where `p`'s argument
is an object literal that does nothing when made (`inert`) and holds `k` once among plain keys,
is written as the value of `k`. Keys are compared by property id (`Pts.propId`), because a key
JavaScript can see and a beni field may be different names with one id. The literal goes with
the rest of its values, which do nothing. Nothing can see the object between its making and the
read, so the read is that value. A key the literal lacks stays a read, since it reads the
prototype. Before, the facts asked after the pass did this as a chain (`{ k: v }.k` is `v`).
Since the passes also run before the first solve (*Where it runs*, amended 2026-10-22), a program
whose later passes find nothing is solved before such a read exists, so the copy does it itself.
`emit/release/app/ProjectLiteralField` pins it. There, `{ step: z => z + 1 }.step(1)` is `2`.

*Amended 2026-10-23 (#889): a record written in place* (`ownership-checker.md` §31.10, *The form*).
An update written in place is `(o.f = v, …, o)`, and slice 8 writes it in as any `e`. A body
whose statements are its stores and then a `return R` (`Lower.settleStores`) is `(o.f = v, …, R)`,
and a binding `const x = (o.f = v, …, o)` is its stores as statements before `const x = o` in
the tidy pass, which item 1's copy of a name then folds. A store is a write wherever it stands: its
target is no read (no fact folds it, no projection writes a value in its place, `patchStmt`
reaches only its object and its value), facts 4 and 5 join what it writes as for `o.p = v`, its
value is never a literal (`Op.effect`), and an object written in place is no scalar replacement's.
Item 1 folds a binding of a name past a write of a property of it (only a rebinding, `rebound`,
keeps it where it is), and never drops a binding that holds a store.

*Amended 2026-10-03.* Once the passes are done, **`x = x`** â a name read and written back, the
model the render loop's `update` leaves as `d = d` â goes from every list (the printer wrote it
as nothing, but it still counted as a use and an assignment, so the binding it named stayed); and
a binding lowering kept for its initialiser, whose initialiser is a read through program objects
(`safeChain`: no getter, no throw), is kept no more, as one the facts folded to an atom is. The
empty page's model, `let e=a.init`, nothing reading it now, goes: 496 â **493**. Neither runs
inside the passes, which would ask the facts again of a program that only lost an assignment.

Measured (release, brotli, the whole bundle): the empty `browser` page and `Tea.sandbox` 550 â
**503** â `first`, `last`, `patch`'s identity and `view`'s block written where they were called,
the program's `update` (the identity of its model) gone from the render loop; `Tea.element`
1 253 â 1 226, with effects 5 405 â 5 384; the `bench/ui` app 5 700 â 5 701 (raw â18); `run/`
programs â1 981 in all (`AliasChainThroughLet`, a chain of 129 aliases, 1 278 â 194). Fixtures:
`emit/release/app/SpecSmall` (an identity, a wrapper whose first argument is a call, one whose
argument is read after its own call and stays, and a function every record's field holds, called
through the field), `run/SpecializeSmall` (the same with `Debug.log` on each argument: the order
is the development build's), `emit/release/app/SpecConstants`, `SpecFacts`, `SpecNodes`,
`SpecInit`, `InlineAfter`, `emit/release/split/EmptyPage`.

*Amended: a function that assigns* (`plans/runtime-in-beni.md`, *The empty page's last items*). A
top-level function whose body is one assignment â `x = e` or `o.p = e`, optionally followed by a
unit function's `return null` â holding no function and no `yield`, naming nothing but its
parameters and whole-program names, and not assigning a parameter, is written as that assignment
at a call **made as a statement** (`f(â¦);`, its value read by nothing), its parameters the
arguments. Every argument must be an atom (as above), so each is evaluated once and before the
assignment, as in the call; a statement the lowering lists as a pure discard is left alone; and
another module's binding is assigned only in a one-scope build. **It is done at every call or at
none**: only when every mention of the function is such a call does its declaration go, and only
when the calls' growth is smaller than the declaration â the size model's, with `true`, `false`
and `null` priced as their text â is the whole smaller. The browser runtime's `stop` in a release
build is `dead = true`, called from each entry point's guard: on a page with two or three guards
it is written in (the empty page 485 â **480**, 24 of the 56 pages smaller and 4 larger
by 1â23 brotli bytes with fewer raw bytes, â207 in all), on a hosted page with eight it stays.
Fixtures: `emit/release/app/SpecStatements` (`stop` twice and gone, `set n` with a literal,
`bump` called nine times and kept, `raise` stored for the host and kept), `run/SpecializeStatements`
(the same; both builds print the same lines).

*Amended 2026-10-02: a parameter nothing reads* (`plans/runtime-in-beni.md`, *The empty page's
last items*). Fact 1 drops a parameter whose every call passes one literal; a parameter whose value
nothing uses goes the same way whatever it is passed. A parameter of a top-level function every call
of which is seen (fact 1's condition: the name is never used but as a callee, with its arity) goes
from the function and from every call when nothing in the body reads or assigns it and **every
argument for it does nothing** (`effectFree`: an inert expression â a literal, a name, a function,
an object or array of those â or a read through objects the program made that can run no getter and
throw nothing, `Pts.safeChain`); an argument that may do something keeps the parameter, so no
evaluation is lost or moved. A read that stands in the initialiser of a **dead binding** counts as no
read (`deadReads`): a `const` or `let` that nothing reads or assigns, that lowering does not keep
for an effect, and whose initialiser does nothing â `Opt` drops it whole â whose initialiser is then
written `undefined`, so no read of the parameter is left. The pass takes this in every round, but
such a drop asks for no round of its own â what it exposes the next round finds, whichever asks â
since the extra rounds it asked for cost a `--schema-library` release build a third more analyses.
The model binding of `mount` (`let e = a.init`) is dead only once its self-assignment is gone and
its read is released (*Amended 2026-10-03*, above), so when releasing a binding frees a read
through a local, the facts are asked once more after it. On the empty page `mount`'s program
parameter goes, with `run`'s `b.a` argument and the mount record's `a` (`[{}]`). Measured (release,
brotli, the whole bundle): the empty `browser` page and `Tea.sandbox` 466 â **450**, `Tea.element`
1 232 â 1 223, with effects 5 316 â 5 311, `random` 1 997 â 1 962; `bench/size.mjs` â358 over its 367
lines (38 smaller, 17 larger, the largest `run/SchemaDeclModules` +22 with fewer raw bytes, and
`run/UnitSubPattern` +13 and `run/ConstantMethodCall` +11: a call made shorter by its dropped
argument is no longer written in by slice 8's per-call size model); the 52 `browser/` pages â243
(22 smaller, 5 larger by 1â6); the `bench/ui` app byte-identical. Dropping the parameter only in a
last round, after the inlining passes, avoided those two and was measured smaller on fewer programs
(â304 and â67), so it was not taken. **Cost**: `run/SchemaDeclRecords`'s four builds, one a release
build of the whole schema engine, 0.71 â 0.72 s of user time (the least of five; asking `effectFree`
and walking for dead reads is about 45 million instructions of them). Fixtures:
`emit/release/app/SpecUnreadParams` (a parameter passed names and literals goes; one passed a call
stays), `run/SpecializeUnreadParams` (one passed `Debug.log`'s result stays, and the line is logged
where it was), `emit/release/app/OneLine`, `SpecScalars`, `emit/release/split/EmptyPage`.

*Amended 2026-10-02: unused trailing arguments* (`Spec.trimArguments`). A call whose callee is not a
function fact 1 tracks â a call through a property, `kind.m(â¦)`, or of a function passed as a value
â keeps every parameter of every function it may reach, since a call the pass cannot see may pass
them. But when fact 3 says the callee may be **only functions of the program**, none of them reads
a parameter past position *k* (a name mentioned anywhere in the body counts as a read, so a
shadowing name only keeps an argument), and every argument past *k* does nothing (`effectFree`),
those arguments go: a missing argument is `undefined`, and nothing reads it. It runs once, after
every round and the passes: slice 8 writes a call through a property in only when it passes every
argument, and trimming one first made `emit/release/app/SpecInit`'s kind call stay a call. On the
empty page the kind's `c.m(null, null)` is `c.m()`. Measured against the compiler before it
(release, brotli): the empty `browser` page and `Tea.sandbox` 450 â 450 (raw â9), `Tea.element`
1 223 â 1 222, with effects 5 311 â 5 306, `random` 1 962 â 1 955; `bench/size.mjs` â41 over its
367 lines (23 smaller, 12 larger, none by more than 16); the `browser/` pages â29 (17 smaller, 8
larger by 1â8); the `bench/ui` app byte-identical. Fixtures: `emit/release/app/SpecTrailingArguments`
(a field holding two functions that read one parameter loses the call's second argument; one that
may hold a function reading two keeps both), `run/SpecializeTrailingArguments` (an argument that
logs is kept, and logged where it was), `emit/release/split/EmptyPage`.

*Amended 2026-10-17: a trailing `undefined` to an arrow.* A call whose callee fact 3 says is only
functions the program makes as arrows (`=>`, or `arrow_method`, printed `function(){}` but
written by no code that reads `arguments`) drops the `undefined` literals that end its arguments:
no emitted code reads `arguments` to count them by, so a missing argument is `undefined` as much as a passed one, and a
literal does nothing to evaluate. `d(p,undefined)` is `d(p)`, a top-level function tracked by fact 1
included. And **the entry's callee may become the function it forwards to**
(`Spec.forwardEntry`): an entry callee `const f = (pâ, â¦, pâ) => g(pâ, â¦, pâ)` that passes its
parameters, in order, to a function declared before it in the same module, is `const f = g` when
nothing in the program names `f` and the entry passes at most `n` arguments â the hand-written entry
file calls it and compares nothing. `run`'s `e=a=>d(a)` is `e=d`
(`emit/release/inline/PushAndTimer` 599 â 589 brotli with both).

*Amended 2026-10-15: a record field's lambda* (issue #95; `plans/queue.md` row 81, found by
research 79 Â§5). `init` is a function of `â¤` since 2026-10-12 (`boundary.md` Â§9.8.16), so
`Tea.element`'s hosted `init` calls `app.init â¤` where it read a value. When a page writes its
`init` as a lambda in the record, `--release` kept the lambda, its key and the call. Before, it
folded the model into the first state. The pass knew nothing about what the lambda does: the
checker's purity bit is per whole-program function (*Calls with known results*), and a lambda in a
record is not one. Two rules now see through such a lambda. Each reads the lambda's own body, which
fact 3 finds at the call:

- **A call of functions that only make a value does nothing** (`Spec.pureCall`, `makesOnly`).
  `effectFree` is the test a drop asks: of an argument nothing reads (`trimArguments`), of a
  parameter nothing reads, of a dead binding's initialiser (`deadReads`), and of a dead write's
  value, which asked its own copy of the test until now. It holds for a call when all four of these
  hold:

  | Condition | Why |
  |---|---|
  | the callee is a chain that can neither throw nor run a getter (`Pts.safeChain`) | evaluating the callee does nothing |
  | fact 3 says the callee may be only functions of the program: never `null`, `undefined`, a primitive or a value the pass cannot see | the call cannot throw a `TypeError`, and no unseen code runs |
  | each of those functions is an arrow or a `function` whose body is empty or one `return` of an `inert` value: a function, a literal, a name, or an object, array or template of those | the body calls nothing, reads no property and writes nothing, so it cannot throw, loop, suspend, log or change a value; binding a parameter does nothing, since a `JsIr` parameter is a plain name |
  | every argument does nothing in turn, to a depth of 8 calls | the call evaluates its arguments first |

  A name the value reads cannot throw either, by the invariant every other drop of an `inert`
  value already rests on: emitted code does not read a binding before its declaration has run
  (`cyclic_value` refuses a value that needs itself). Such a call makes a new value and does nothing else, so when nothing reads that
  value nothing can tell that it was not made: `language.md` Â§6's order loses no effect, and no reachable code holds
  the object (rule 8). It goes like any other argument that does nothing: `start`'s unread
  `app.init â¤`, and `Navigation.key â¤`, whose result an application's `init` does not read.

  *Amended 2026-10-17:* the returned value may also be a *plain value* (`plainValue`): names,
  literals, `===`, `!==`, `!`, `typeof`, `&&`, `||` and conditionals of those â none of which can
  throw, run code or read a property â so `endpointOf`'s `a === 0 ? 0 : 1` is such a function.
  And a binding lowering kept for its initialiser is kept no more when that initialiser is such a
  call (`releaseKeeps`): a field of a kept schema context, left by scalar replacement as
  `const i = endpointOf(1)` that nothing reads, goes with its function
  (`emit/release/inline/PushAndTimer`, 698 â 675 brotli).
- **A function used once is written in with no size model** (`Spec.soleCalls`). Slice 8 writes a
  small function reached through a property at a call only when the body prints no longer than
  the call, which a record's lambda that makes a record never does (`{a:{}}` against `a.init()`).
  That model prices the body against the call alone. But when the call is the program's only use
  of the function, the function goes after it: nothing reads the key that holds it, so fact 3
  drops the key, and nothing reads its binding, so item 1 drops a local binding and the pass
  drops a top-level one. Each of these drops needs an `inert` value. So slice 8 does not ask the
  size model at a call through a property when, by fact 3's values over the whole program, these
  three hold: the callee of exactly one call may be that function, the function does not escape,
  and every other node that may be it only holds it (the function itself, an `inert` key's value
  in an object literal whose site neither escapes nor has every key read, or a binding's `inert`
  initialiser). A record update `{ r | â¦ }` spreads `r`, which reads every key of it, so a key of
  `r` stays whatever its call becomes: written at the call, the body would be in the output two
  times, raw bytes and brotli both larger (`emit/release/app/SpecRecordLambdaUpdate`, found by
  the PR's review). A field read (`ops.fn`) is not inert to this rule â `soleCalls` asks
  `inertOf` without field reads, though Â§9 item 1 as amended 2026-10-18 counts them inert
  where it only drops a value â and a key or a binding of one stays for the same reason (found by
  the PR's second review). `dropKeys` keeps the key `{ step = ops.fn }`
  (`emit/release/app/SpecRecordLambdaField`), and the pass keeps the top-level binding
  `picked = ops.fn` (`SpecRecordLambdaTop`). A local `f = ops.fn` that a key `{ step = f }` reads
  can go. But when a `return` that reads `f` once and first comes next,
  slice 9 writes `ops.fn` in place of `f` (*`const x = e; return R`*), and the key becomes
  `{ step = ops.fn }` (`SpecRecordLambdaLocal`). `Tea.document`'s `update = app.update` is a
  local binding of this kind that goes, because `init = app.init` is read before it. The rule
  does not count on that: five `browser/` builds of `Tea.document` give up 39â57 raw bytes
  against a rule that counts every local binding, and stay 22â68 raw bytes smaller than master.
  Issue #246 holds the wider drop, of a key or a binding of a field read that does nothing, that
  would get them back. And a call through a property
  may pass more arguments than the function has parameters, when each one past them is `inert`:
  the call evaluates it and nothing reads it. This is `app.init(null)` of a lambda lowered with no
  parameter for its `â¤`; `trimArguments` drops such an argument only after slice 8 has run. The
  rewrite is slice 8's, with slice 8's rules for the arguments that stay: atoms, or one read once
  and first. The uses are counted in one walk of the program, made at most once per pass and only
  when the size model has refused a call through a property. A body slice 8 has already written in
  during that pass is newer than the facts, so the walk cannot see the uses in it: every function
  site that fact 3 gives a node of a copied body is marked, and a marked function is not used
  once. This is a guard, not an exact count: a node of that body newer than the facts (a copy an
  earlier call wrote into it, or what `returnExpr` makes of an `if` or a `const` body) has no fact-3
  value, and a function that only such a node may be is not marked. A wrong count only costs
  bytes â the rewrite is slice 8's, sound at any size, and a key or a binding
  goes only when nothing reads it.

Neither rule changes a development build.

**Slice 9 â constructor folding** (*added 2026-10-03*; `plans/runtime-in-beni.md`'s *Append
against Solid 1*: a page that reads a list with `List.get` then `Maybe.withDefault` made a `Just`
per read, most of the cold loop's cost). A value a small function makes, that another small
function or the rest of the caller only *inspects*, is made where it is inspected, so that its
tag test folds and its fields are read where they are written:

- **A producer** is an expression that makes an object a fold can see into: an object literal; a
  *declared object* (a top-level `const` of an object literal â a nullary constructor such as
  `Nothing`); a choice `c ? A : B` of two producers; or a call of a small function (slice 8's,
  whose body may now also be `if (t) return a; return b` and `const v = e; return R` with `v`
  read once, first â the `case` lowering's shapes, read as `t ? a : b` and `R[v := e]`) whose
  body is one. A parameter is **inspected** when the body reads it, and only as the object of a
  property read; a local is when its declaration says so of every mention.
- **`return f(â¦, P, â¦)`**, `f` small, inspecting the parameter `P` is passed to, `P` a producer: the
  arguments that are not atoms are bound first, in order, by `const`s (kept by the optimiser when
  they may do something), then `return` `f`'s body.
- **`const x = g(â¦)`**, `g` a small producer, `x` only inspected: the same, `x` bound to `g`'s
  body.
- **`const x = c ? A : B`, then one statement `R` ending the list**, `x` only inspected, `A` and
  `B` producers, `R` small with no function in it: `if (c) { const x = A; R } else { const x' = B;
  R' }`, `R'` a copy of `R` reading `x'` and declaring names of its own â `R` runs once on either
  path, as it did.
- **`const x = e; return R`**, `x` read once in its declaration, by `R`, first, and not only
  inspected: `return R[x := e]` â the field binding scalar replacement leaves behind.

Then scalar replacement makes `x = {$: "Just", a: v}` its fields, and the facts fold the tag
test: `"Just" === "Just"` is `true`; and **a constructor's tag `$`** read through a chain whose
objects are all object literals of the program with the key â escaped or not â is the literals'
one value when no code of the program writes `$` on them or on anything the pass cannot see: a
beni value is immutable, and a hand-written file writes none (`Spec.tagValue`; `Nothing.$` is
`"Nothing"` though `Nothing` is passed everywhere). `List.get xs i |> Maybe.withDefault ""` is
then `0<=i&&i<xs.length?unsafeGet(xs,i):""`; `case List.head xs of Just x -> x * 2; Nothing -> d`
is `0<xs.length?unsafeGet(xs,0)*2:d`; a read through `List.drop` still makes the view, not the
`Just`. A name a body needs that is a hand-written file's binding is written by the name a module
imports it as, which is one binding of the one scope; the import stays while any module names it.
The passes run small functions, functions called once, then this, then scalar replacement â in
that order, so a function called once is taken in before a binding here makes its argument a
call.

**5 675** â its `pick` is `{let d=N(c,b);return 0<=d&&d<a.length?R(a,d):""}`, no `Just` â and
`run/` programs â671 in all. Fixtures: `emit/release/app/SpecMaybe` (`get` then `withDefault`, a

**As built â a fold steps back** (*added 2026-10-21*, #589; `Spec.foldConstructors`,
`dropKeys`). On the research dashboard at N = 64, once the inliner wrote every function called
once in its first count (#576), `spec_passes` stayed 3 with `spec_passes_capped` 1, and the second
and third passes were constructor folding's alone. It was not an unrolling: every fold was the
rule *`const x = e; return R`*, taking one binding of a run such as `const a = p.x; const b = p.y;
â¦; return {â¦, k: a, l: b}` per pass. `foldConstructors` walked forward and, after a fold, asked
again only of what it wrote; the binding before it, now followed by a `return` that reads it once
and first, waited for the next structural pass and its analysis, and `max_passes` stopped the
third with bindings left. The two rules that read the statement after their own (this one and
*`const x = c ? A : B; R`*) can apply to the statement before a fold, and no other rule's answer
for it changes within the walk, so after each fold the walk now steps back one statement. A run
of n bindings folds in one walk, within the list's budget of 32 folds. What a later pass makes
foldable is still folded then: scalar replacement, after constructor folding in the same pass,
makes a record read only by its fields one binding per field, and the next pass folds those.

Stepping back folded bindings into a returned literal that the analysis after the pass used to
drop first, a binding nothing read whose value was a call of a function that only makes a value
(`pureCall`). As a key, it stayed: `dropKeys` dropped an unread key only when its value was
`inert`. An unread key now goes under the rule an unread binding goes under, `effectFree`: inert,
a chain that can neither throw nor run a getter, or such a call. That also drops keys master kept,
such as the schema context's `i:b(1)`.

**A variable nothing reads** (*amended 2026-10-02*). Fact 3 drops a write of a property no read

when it may do something (`inert`, `Pts.safeChain`) â when `x` is

  sweep counts (an assignment's target is not a read), and that nothing the pass cannot see reaches
  (`Input.escaping`, the entry's names: `escaped`); or

  included (`uses`).

A rewrite only takes reads away, so a count of none at the round's start is none after it. With its

**A function called where it is made** (*amended 2026-10-02*). Slice 5 writes a function called
once where it is called, with each argument in place of its parameter; when the argument is a
lambda the body calls, what is left is a call of a function where it is made. The fiber runtime's
`callback register = suspend Î»wake â â¦` was `f=(b=>{let c=a(b);return typeof c==="function"?c:
null})(d)` in `callback` once `suspend` was written there, on a page whose only waits are
`callback`'s: a wrapper made and called once per wait. Once the passes are done, one sweep of every statement list in a function (the one
*Amended 2026-10-03*'s `x = x` takes) writes such a call, of an ordinary arrow (no default, not a
`function`), as its body, two ways:

- **In an expression**, when the body is one `return e` â slice 8's shape, `smallOf` â and the
  arguments pass slice 8's rule: each an atom, or one read once and first. The call is `e`, its
  parameters the arguments. No size model applies, since the arrow's own text goes with the call,
  and the body may name what the function around it names: it is written where it was made.
- **As statements**, when the call is a `const` or `let`'s initialiser, a `return`'s value or a
  statement of its own, and the body is statements ending in `return e`: `const p = a;` for each
  parameter in order (a `let` when the body assigns it), then the body's statements, then the
  statement with `e` for its value. The arguments are evaluated once and before the body, as the
  call evaluated them; an arrow binds no `this` and no `arguments`, so its body means the same in
  the list. Taken only when nothing in the list can come to mean something else: every parameter
  and every name the body declares at its own level is declared once in the declaration
  (`declCount`) and by no `catch`, no `return` but the last leaves the body, and the body holds no
  label, which the list could already hold. A body of one `return e` is the first way's: as
  statements it is bindings and a block, larger than the call.

A call whose body reads a parameter twice and whose argument is not a name stays: writing the body

**As built â the worklist** (*added 2026-10-01*, `Spec.Pts.fixpoint`, `Spec.sweeps`). The facts are
the ones above, sweep for sweep; what changed is how much of the program a sweep walks. A release
build of a TodoMVC-sized page spent 1.3 of its 3.0 billion instructions here, most of it fact 3
sweeping the whole program about eleven times a round, from scratch every round.

- **A sweep walks only what read something that changed since it was last walked.** Every read of
  a fact records the unit that made it: for fact 3 a var (`view`), a site's escape and unknown-key
  writes (`seeSite`) and a site's list of properties (`seeProps`); for facts 1, 2, 4 and 5 a
  whole-program name's `escaped` and `assigned`, a site's `prop_lat`, `ret_lat` and spread, and a
  parameter (read by its own declaration alone). A change wakes the units that read it. A unit
  nothing woke would read what it read before, make the joins it made before â no-ops â and
  change nothing, so skipping it is exact: each sweep leaves the state a walk of everything
  would, the sweeps are as many (the caps of 64 and 24 mean what they meant), and a fixpoint is
  the same fixpoint. Facts 1, 2, 4 and 5's units are the top-level statements; fact 3's are the
  top-level statements and every function body, a body walked where the walk of what holds it
  reaches it â never alone â when it or a body inside it was woken, so the order of every walk
  is the order of a sweep of everything. **The order is kept on purpose**: fact 3 is not
  order-free. A var that is `top` still gathers `prim`, `null` and `undefined`, and which it
  gathers depends on what transient values it was joined with before it went `top`; the DOM
  node-maker fact and `appendChild` read `prim` beside `top`. Walking units in another order (a
  reversed sweep, a body alone) gave a different, equally sound fixpoint on
  `run/CallbackOrderDict`, so it is not done.
- **A node's value is its unit's last walk's.** `vals` and what they point into live across a
  fixpoint's sweeps, so the sweep of everything after the fixpoint that a whole-program pass
  needs to fill them is not taken. `rewrite` likewise takes a statement's values from its last
  sweep and only counts its names, unless it was left woken at the fixpoint or reads a
  module-level constant this rewrite has already patched (`nameValue` reads the initialiser).
- **So is a conditional fact 5 decides** (*amended 2026-10-12*, `Spec.combine`'s `.cond`). Fact
  5's second case â `x.p === null ? f : x.p` is `x.p` when the read is nonnull â is recorded in
  `decided_conds` for `rewrite`, and the facts climb from â¥: a read may be nonnull at one sweep
  and â¤ at the next, when a `null` written to it arrives a sweep later (through a recursive
  function's parameter, say). Until this amendment a decision once recorded stayed, so `rewrite`
  took the branch on a fact the fixpoint had withdrawn â a release build that printed what the
  development build did not (`run/SpecializeLateNull`). Each evaluation of a conditional now
  records its decision or removes it, so what stays is the last walk's, made from the final facts
  as `memo` is. The safety check above could not see it: both of its fixpoints kept the same stale
  entry. Every other output byte for byte (the `emit/release/` goldens, every run hash).
- **What every round asked of the whole program, it asks of what changed.** `namedIn` answers
  every whole-program name at once from one walk of the module, kept while the module's `version`
  stands; inside `rewrite`, which only takes mentions away, a name the walk did not meet is still
  not met, and an identifier of a name being written as that name's own value needs no walk
  when the module has one name for it. `inlineOne`'s mention counts are kept per module the
  same way, and `nameRead` of a whole-program name reads them.
- **Rounds still start from â¥.** A round's program is the last one rewritten â calls dropped,
  branches gone â so its least fixpoint lies below the last round's facts; starting from those
  would keep what the rewrite made false, and print a different program.
- **Checked.** A safety build computes each fixpoint of a program of at most 1 500 nodes twice â
  every unit walked every sweep, then by the worklist â and stops if any fact, node value or
  sweep count differs.

**Added 2026-10-02 â why a later pass is not incremental, and what is cut instead.** A core
written in beni (`plans/core-in-beni.md` step 3) gives the inline passes something to do in
almost every program, and each time they change something the whole of `Spec.run` repeats:
`prune`, a round of facts from â¥, `rewrite`, and every inline pass again. On `abuse_wide_test`'s
16 400-arm `case` under `--release` with research 50's `List` in beni, the first inline pass
changed one module, `List` (173 nodes, 8 statements), and the second pass that followed cost
about 765 million instructions. Nearly all of it went on re-walking the untouched 16 400-arm
function. The obvious cure is to redo, after the first pass, only the functions the inline
passes changed, with their callers and callees. **That cannot print what a full pass prints:**

- *Facts must be able to fall.* Writing a call in removes a call site, so a parameter that was
  â¤ may now be a constant. Keeping a clean function's contributions from the last round cannot
  take that back. This is the worklist note's *rounds still start from â¥*.
- *Facts travel further than callers and callees.* They run down call chains (fact 1), through
  properties and returns (facts 4 and 5) and through fact 3. In the case above, the callback
  that calls the 16 400-arm function is called from `List`'s loop, so that function's argument
  is a fact-3 value of the very code the inline pass changed. Any exact delete-and-recompute
  closure contains it, so even a perfect dirty set saves nothing there.
- *Fact 3 depends on walk order*, as the worklist note shows on `run/CallbackOrderDict`, and
  allocates its sites and variables in walk order. Re-walking a subset, starting from the old
  state, reaches a different, equally sound fixpoint.
- *The rewriting passes read whole-program facts too*: `dropKeys` and `appendChild` read fact
  3, and the inline passes read the small-function table, `assigned` and `decl`. A statement
  whose text did not change can still be rewritten differently.

An exact incremental pass would replay a unit's walk only when every value it reads is
unchanged. That means recording each walk's reads, writes and allocated ids, for fact 3, the
sweeps, `rewrite` and each inline pass. It is a re-architecture with a cost on every build, and
it is not taken. What is taken instead is exact by construction: work that cannot change the
program is not done, on any pass.

- **A statement list the list sweeps cannot act on is left uncopied** (`Spec.listActs`). The
  three sweeps that walk every statement list â scalar replacement, constructor folding and
  `x = x` â copied every list and examined each statement. Each acts only on a `const` or `let`
  (of an object literal, for scalar replacement), a `return` of a call, or an assignment. A list
  holding none of these is now walked through for the lists below it and left as it was, in
  place. `--self-profile`'s `spec_lists_examined` counts the lists still copied, and
  `build_test`'s *list sweeps do not grow* holds it constant between a 64-arm and a 1 024-arm
  `case`.
- **A walk's cost per statement is cut where it was spent doing nothing.** The literals' table
  is sized to the literals the program spells before it is filled, and is probed once per
  literal, by the literal itself, with `KeyMap`'s kind of hash. Before, the key was built in a
  buffer, hashed twice with Wyhash, and the table rehashed itself as it grew. A literal without
  bytes keeps its id apart. Name counting, fact 3's walk and the sweeps' evaluation take an
  expression that is a leaf without their stacks. `rewrite` no longer walks the program for
  calls to cut when no parameter went. None of this changes an id, an order or a fact. On the
  16 400-arm build, one round's sweeps fell from 320 to 158 million instructions, fact 3 from 73
  to 53, `rewrite` from 231 to 159.

Measured with `abuse_wide_test`'s *16 400 literal branches â¦ under `--release`*, in millions of
instructions against the 4 300 budget, test harness included:

| step | master | `List` in beni (research 50's prototype) |
|---|--:|--:|
| before | 3 846 | 4 782 |
| lists left uncopied | 3 702 | 4 526 |
| cheaper walks per statement | 3 456 | **4 139** |

With `List` in beni the case now fits the budget, 161 million under it, with no re-architecture.

Each step's output is byte for byte as before: every file `bench/size.mjs` builds, in both
builds, and every release run hash.

**As built â the structural passes keep their walks per statement** (*added 2026-10-20*, #492;
`Mod.kept`, `Spec.within`, `Spec.NameScan`, `retract`, `extend`). *The combined solver*, below,
leaves the structural passes as they are, so their walks need an incremental form of their own.
A page's `update` holds every widget's call in **one** top-level statement, and its `view` holds
every widget's view. Several walks went over that whole statement again after each function
written into it: `inlineScan` (each candidate's mentions), `occurrences` (`namedIn`),
`assignedIn`, and each binding `replaceScalars`, `onlyInspected` or `declCount` asked about.
With the points-to sets small (`max_sites` at 48), they were 65% of `specialise` on the research
dashboard at N = 64. The plan proposed caching `preorder` per statement and `Mod.version`. That
cache already existed. It could not help, because every write in the module moved
`Mod.version`, and the writes all land in the same statement. What is built instead is exact by
construction, as the note above asks:

- **A change is the statement's it is made in.** A pass that writes inside one top-level
  statement says so (`within` â¦ `leave`): `inlineAt`, each list sweep (`eachFunctionList`), each
  of `inlineSmallPass`'s calls and each list `fuseAt` rewrites. Each `Mod.changed()` made while
  a statement is named is that statement's. Any other change is the whole module's. A walk of
  one statement, kept at the `epoch` it was made at, holds while neither moved past it
  (`Mod.kept`). A name added to the module and made global changes no walk
  (`Mod.namesChanged`). `preorder`, `scanOf` and `placeKept` (`fuseAt`'s places) keep their
  walks this way.
- **One scan answers every name.** `NameScan` holds, per name a statement names, its
  declarations, `ident`s, assignments, the reads `x.k` (and `x.k.j`), writes `x.k = â¦`, method
  calls `x.k(â¦)` and calls of it. It also keeps the whole-program names in the order the walk
  first meets each. `inlineScan`, `occurrences`, `declCount`, `onlyInspected`, `atomArgument`,
  `soleInit`, `foldAt` and `replaceScalars` read it instead of walking the statement. Names are
  found by a sorted index, with no hash map keyed by a dense id.
- **A change of subtrees updates the scan.** `retract` takes out what the replaced subtrees
  counted, before the change. `extend` adds what the new ones count, after it. This covers a
  call written as an expression or a statement (`inlineAt`, `inlineSmallAt`), the reads of a
  scalar-replaced object, and the lists scalar replacement and `fuseAt` rewrite. A node's part
  reads its children: a read `x.k` reads its object, an assignment its target, a call its
  callee. So the update is refused, and the statement counted again, wherever a parent's part
  would change too:
  - a call written as a name or a member read where its parent reads it (`h(x).k`);
  - a scalar-replaced object written to, called through or read two deep;
  - a call the scan no longer counts. `inlineSmallPass` lists a statement's calls before it
    writes any, and a copy of a call's root (`Copy.atom`) shares that call's callee.
- **Checked.** A safety build checks every scan it updates, and every one it keeps across a
  change, in a module of at most 3 000 nodes. It walks the statement again and compares the sum
  of each node's `contribution` (its operands and what it reads of its child), the first name of
  each whole-program name, and, for a statement of at most 32 nodes, every name. The whole corpus
  passed with the checks unbounded.

Measured on dagon, ReleaseFast, `build --release --no-cache --jobs=1`, master at `c5956dba9`
before; output byte for byte the same in every row:

| `specialise` (ms) | `max_sites` 48, before | after | 1 000, before | after |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| dashboard N = 16 | 58 | **43** | 92 | 75 |
| dashboard N = 64 | 387 | **146** | 5 553 | 5 336 |
| N = 64 without `withDefault` | 401 | **150** | 999 | 773 |

At N = 64 with small sets, the structural passes went from 65% of `specialise` to about 30%
(`inlineOnce` 18% of the whole build, the list sweeps and `fuseCalls` under 2% each). What remains is the facts (`rounds`), the points-to
analysis's own track. `test-perf`'s *specialisation writes n calls of one statement in time
linear in n* holds it: ratio 3.3 before, 2.1 after.

*Added 2026-10-21 (issue #608) â `Copy` finds a name through an index.* When a body is copied
across modules, each property name is replaced by the destination module's name with the same
text (`Copy.property`). It used to be found by a walk of all the destination's names, for every
property copied. That walk was 38% of `inlineAt` and 2.2% of the whole build at N = 64
(`plans/build-profile-2026-10-21b.md`, cause 5). `Mod.name_index` now maps each name to its
first index, as the walk found it. It is built on the first lookup. Names are only ever
appended, never rewritten, so each later lookup only adds the names appended since the last
one, whichever pass appended them (`Mod.findName`). In `perf record`, `Copy`'s own samples fell
from 2.3% of the N = 64 build to too few to see. `specialise` fell from 137.6 to 132.0 ms
at N = 64 and from 118.9 to 114.4 ms on `nowd` (`--jobs=1`, medians of 11 interleaved runs). The
output is the same.

**Slice 10 â a value read once at start-up** (*added 2026-10-15*; research 102 Â§6.1 item 2,
`Spec.inlineReads`). A top-level binding whose value is made at start-up and read once, also at
start-up, is written where it is read and not declared at all: direct's patch functions and
template protocol rows, each a `const` read once by the consumer table of its module, are the
case it exists for â `Qf(Vt,Wt,null)` becomes `Qf([â¦],(a,b)=>{â¦},null)`. It runs last, after
`trimArguments`, because a copy's nodes are in no fact, and `prune` then drops each declaration
nothing names any more. **A binding qualifies only when every one of these holds**, and each is
there for the guarantee beside it:

| Condition | Why |
|---|---|
| it is a top-level `const` of the program's own lowering (no hand-written file's binding, no `let`, no `function`) | a `let` may be assigned; a `function` is hoisted, and may be called before its statement |
| its initialiser is **inert** (`Spec.inert`): a function, a literal, a name, or an array, object or template of those | making it calls nothing, reads no property and so cannot fail, suspend, log or see a change: moving it moves no effect and no evaluation that can fail (`language.md` Â§6). `Debug.log`, `Debug.todo` and anything else are calls: never moved |
| every name it reads as it is made (outside a function in it) is assigned nowhere in the program (`immutableNames`) | made later, it reads what it read: the name was initialised at the binding (its statement came first) and holds one value from then on. A name a function in it reads is a binding the closure keeps whatever the moment it is made |
| the whole program mentions its name exactly once, and nothing the pass cannot see names it (`Input.escaping`, the entry's call; a library's exports) | that mention is the only way to the value, so whoever saw the object before sees the same one object now (rule 8): field identity is untouched, and nothing between the binding and the read can tell it was not made yet |
| the mention stands in a **later top-level statement of the same module** | the read runs after the binding, in the order the module runs its statements; across modules the order of two module bodies is the import graph's, a question this slice does not open: of the 436 reads research 102's prototype took in Conduit, 31 map to two sources, several of them the shared constant constructors no source owns, and none is a patch |
| the mention runs **exactly once** while the module starts: under no function (an arrow, a `function`), no loop (`while`, `forâ¦of`), not an assignment's target, not a statement of its own, and not a callee | a read inside a function would make the value on every call â a new object, a new closure each time, and identity per call (rule 8); in a loop, once per iteration. A callee would become a function called where it is made: measured on Conduit, that wrote 35 more brotli bytes on direct and 2 on tea, so it stays a call of the name |

**How it is written.** The value is copied to the read (`Spec.Copy`) and the read node becomes the
copy's root; every local the value declares gets a new name, since a local's `NameIndex` is
shared by every top-level declaration of the module (`localName` restarts per declaration, Â§9 item
1) and the value now stands in another one. The tables lowering handed the optimiser follow the
copy. The read keeps the value's own position, so a release map (Â§11.2) sends the written
function to its definition. A development build is unchanged, since this pass runs under
`--release` only.

Measured (release, brotli, the one file): Conduit **31 745 â 31 471** on `browser-tea`
(â274; research 102's prototype â180) and **38 243 â 36 456** on `browser-direct` (â1 787;
prototype â1 577), its three corpus scripts identical on both; `bench/size.mjs`'s release total
723 980 â **723 908** â 61 programs smaller, 39 larger, 382 equal, no program's raw bytes larger:
every larger brotli figure is a renaming of fewer raw bytes, mostly a function written into a

(`run/SchemaDeclKeys` +87, the most); `bench/corpus` (`--library`) 19 092 â 19 054; development
output byte for byte as before. Speed: nothing that runs after start-up changes; every value is

written into a list, the list into a call; a list read once inside a function and one read twice
stay), `emit/release/direct/MapKind` (`Html.map`'s kind, whose two functions are written into it,

once by a third still log in their order, before the value read between them â red with the

`emit/release/split/HolesPage`, `app/DeadArms`, `SpecFieldNames`, `SpecTrailingArguments`,

**Amended 2026-10-02 â fact 3 is order-free** (research 52 Â§3.3 and Â§4.5, slices 0â2; this
corrects the worklist note's *the order is kept on purpose* and its *Checked* bullet).

- **A value never borrows a var's storage.** A var's set of sites is a sorted slice that is
  never changed in place: a join that adds a site makes a new slice and leaves the old one. A
  walk holds the values of an expression's earlier operands while it evaluates the later ones,
  and a call among those can join a site into the very parameter an earlier operand read; the
  set used to grow in place under the earlier value, which then read shifted memory or, once
  the list moved, freed memory (research 52's E5: four `browser/tea` pages read `0xAAAAAAAA` as
  a site with the passes' cap raised). The unit test *a value read from a var keeps its sites
  when a later join adds one* is the smallest input that reaches it.
- **`top` implies the other three components.** A value is TAJS's product (`Pts.Val`): `top`,
  `prim`, `null`, `undefined` and a set of sites, each joined on its own, and `top` â what the
  program did not make or cannot follow â may be a primitive, `null` or `undefined` too. So a
  read through a value that went `top` (a host value, an escaped object, an unknown key) gives
  at least what the same read gave before it did, where it used to give `top` alone and drop
  the other bits. With that, every transfer function of fact 3 is monotone, and it has one
  least fixpoint whatever order its units are walked in: the bits a `top` var gathered no
  longer depend on what transient values it was joined with first. The two consumers that read
  `prim` beside `top` now ask only that the receiver is no object of the program: the
  node-maker fact (a primitive, `null` or `undefined` receiver has no such method and throws)
  and `appendChild` (both calls throw the same `TypeError` there, as they already did for
  `null`).
- **An escaped site is â¤.** Which of its properties a read marked, which calls it recorded,
  what it was written under â those depend on how much was walked before it escaped, and no
  fact is read of them (definite initialisation, `neverRead`, `keyUnread` and the call graph
  all refuse an escaped site; its tag is refused through `unknown_props` whichever way a write
  was recorded). They are not facts, and the check below does not compare them.
- **Checked by another order.** A safety build computes each fact-3 fixpoint of a program of at
  most 1 500 nodes twice: walking every unit every sweep with the top-level statements in a
  shuffled order (a fixed seed), then by the worklist in program order; the two must agree on
  every fact, each site taken for the one its node made (the numbering follows the walk).
  That tests rule 5's property itself, and still tests that the worklist skips only walks that
  change nothing. Put back the old `top`, and 18 `run/` and `emit/` programs stop at it. Facts
  1, 2, 4 and 5 keep the worklist-against-every-unit check until they move into the same
  solver.

**Amended 2026-10-22 â compare facts independently of their storage** (issues #657, #658).
The monotonicity premise above is unchanged. Two defects in its shuffled-order check compared
representation choices instead of facts:

- A `top` value's live sites are a **set** after mapping each site to the one made by the same
  node. Site numbers follow the walk, so that map need not preserve their numeric order.
  The check compares live-set cardinality and mapped membership, as it already does for a
  value without `top`; it still checks every component flag and each site's escape state.
- A site's property table is **sparse**. A missing entry means no values, no read, no definite
  initialisation and no per-key write. Reading a missing property makes an empty entry; a
  site is no longer marked once it escapes. A spread may therefore copy an empty key marked
  before its source escaped in only one order. That copy marks the key written, but the
  source's `any_written`, also copied, already subsumes the per-key written bit
  (`neverWritten` checks it first). An empty, unread, uninitialised entry under `any_written`
  is the same fact as its absence. The check compares the union of keys with those defaults,
  retaining every read/initialisation bit and every write not covered by
  `any_written`. It does not require equal numbers of storage entries.
- A property read includes the site's unknown-key value (`any`). When `any` is top in
  both runs, its component flags and the escaped sites retained by a transient spread
  subsume the raw property's. The check compares the effective value, with top's flags
  and the property's live sites. Every differing live site is still an error. Without
  top in `any`, it compares the raw property values exactly as before.

These corrections change no transfer, consumer, check limit or emitted JavaScript. They
state the equivalence the safety check must test: live sites, initialised keys and every
value or flag not subsumed by top remain facts that must agree.

Every output is byte for byte as before â the `emit/release/` goldens, every release run hash,
and all 411 release builds of research 52's E3 set compared file by file â so nothing in the
corpus depended on the order the bits were gathered in. **`--self-profile`** counts the pass's
work and every cap it hits (`spec_analyses`, `spec_sweeps`, `spec_points_to_runs`,
`spec_points_to_sweeps`, `spec_passes`, and `spec_analyses_declined`,
`spec_points_to_declined`, `spec_rounds_capped`, `spec_passes_capped`, `spec_init_capped`,
`spec_inline_capped`), so that a size regression is traced to the cap behind it;
`build_test`'s *counts a call chain deeper than its sweeps as a declined analysis* pins the
first. `emit/release/app/SpecDeepChain` (24 levels of pass-through: nothing specialised) and
`SpecSelfGuard` (a flag a dead branch hides from itself) pin what rounds cannot do, and move
when the combined solver lands (research 52 Â§4).

**Amended 2026-10-02 â truthiness, and what follows a jump** (research 52 Â§3.4, Â§3.6 and Â§4.5,
slice 3). Facts 1, 2, 4 and 5 fold a test only when it is a literal; `x || true` was â¤, though
every value it can take is truthy, and E4 counted the cost: `platforms/browser/Rt.beni`'s
`sameInputs` and `sameInputsBut`, specialised with `b = null`, kept
`if(a===null||true||a.length!==null.length)return false;` and the loop after it on every page
that has rows.

- **The value carries its truthiness** (`Spec.Lat`): â¥, always truthy, always falsy, or either,
  beside the value and joined on its own â Click's combined lattice for conditions. A literal's
  is its literal's; an object, an array, a function, a `new` and a DOM node-maker's result are
  truthy; `!x` is the opposite of `x`; `typeof x` is truthy; `a || b` is truthy when `a` is
  wherever it ends the operator and `b` is wherever it goes on, `a && b` the other way round; a
  conditional whose test is decided is its taken branch; a call is what its callees return,
  and a field what its writes give. `a || b` whose `a` is always truthy has `a`'s value, exactly.
  A value is a literal only where the expression's evaluation does nothing the literal could
  lose, as before: truthiness never makes one. `yield x` is now â¤, what the generator is
  resumed with; it was `x`'s value, which a comparison of the two could have folded.
- **The rewrite spends it where what it skips does nothing** (`Spec.effectFreeTest`): a
  literal, a name, a function, a read through the program's own objects (`effectFree`), `===`,
  `!==`, `!` and `typeof` of such, an arithmetic or relational operator on values fact 3 says
  are primitives the program made (no `valueOf` can run), and `&&`, `||` and `?:` whose parts
  that are evaluated are such â `y` in `x || true || y` is never reached and is not asked
  about. `a || b` whose `a` is always truthy is `a`; whose `a` is always falsy and does nothing,
  `b` (and `&&` the other way round). A conditional with such a test is its branch. An `if`
  with a decided test keeps its arm; when the test may do something it stays, as a statement
  before the arm (`T; â¦arm`), in the `if`'s own node.
- **What follows a statement that cannot complete normally goes** (`Spec.deadTail`): a
  `return`, `throw`, `break` or `continue`, an `if` neither arm of which completes, or an
  unlabelled block that does not â when nothing outside the dead statements, in the top-level
  declaration, declares or names what they declare, so no earlier statement, closure or
  hoisted `function` can reach it. A module's body is left whole. Each list is cut before the
  list around it asks whether its last statement completes, so that question reads the last
  statement only.

lose 30â69 bytes each (`sameInputs` is `a=>a===null?true:false`, and `sameInputsBut` loses its

`switch` after a folded `?` and a derived `compare`; `run/ReleaseFieldsAcrossJs` â65, a derived

**Amended 2026-10-12 â fact 3 by its constraints** (`Pts.byConstraints`; a step toward slice 5
of *The combined solver*, below, not slice 5 itself). Measured on `browser/tea/ApiItems`, a
schema-reading `Tea.element` page whose release build was 2.03 billion instructions of the
ReleaseSafe compiler: specialisation was 1.36 billion of it, eight analyses (three rounds before
the inlining passes, three after the first, one after each of the other two â the passes' cap is
reached) each taking fact 3 to its fixpoint from â¥ in about twelve sweeps, 560 million in all.
Nothing about schemas makes it so: the page is the `browser-tea` runtime, `core/Task` and `Http`
around a small program, about 23 000 nodes, and a sweep re-walked every unit that read anything
that changed. Of the 386 000 node evaluations of the eight fixpoints, 88 000 were the first
sweeps'; of the rest, five in six gave the value the node already had â a unit (a function body)
was walked again whole for one changed read in it.

- **The first sweep is the walk it was, and records constraints.** Every evaluation it makes â
  of an expression node, or of a statement's own transfer (a binding's join, an assignment's
  write, a `return`, `forâ¦of`, `throw`: `Pts.effect`) â is a constraint, numbered in walk order:
  its node and context (the top-level statement, which keys locals; for a `return`, its
  function), and the constraints whose values it read (`inputsOf`: a node's operands, an
  object's property values, a call's arguments and the object whose method it calls). A node
  lowering shares between two expressions (`a.b` in `a.b.c` and `a.b.d`) is evaluated twice
  and is two constraints; once the fixpoint is reached a node holds its last evaluation's value,
  as a walk leaves it. A node whose value its tag alone makes (an operator but `&&` and `||`, a
  template) is no constraint. Every read of a var, a site's escape or its properties registers
  the constraint making it, as it registered the unit.
- **A guard's death is recorded, not replayed.** A read is narrowed by a guard in view (fact 5,
  *What fact 3 learns*) while nothing between the guard's push and the read killed it. A call,
  an assignment, a declaration or a loop's next turn kills whatever the values are; such a guard
  is never recorded for the read. A read through a host value kills only once its object is
  `top`: the walk records, per guard a read may be narrowed by, the reads between them, and the
  read is evaluated again when one of their objects changes. An object no constraint makes
  (`this`, an operator) has its one value and kills, or not, for good.
- **After the walk, a change wakes constraints, not units.** A constraint is evaluated again
  alone, by the walk's own transfer function, with its inputs' values; one whose value changed
  wakes those that read it. A sweep is the constraints waiting, in walk order, then what the
  files the pass cannot see read, the entry's call and `propagate`; `max_pts_sweeps` caps them
  as before.

Every transfer function is the walk's and monotone, so this reaches the one least fixpoint the
sweeps reached (research 52 Â§2.3), and sites are numbered by the same first walk. **Checked**:
the safety build's comparison (*Amended 2026-10-02 â fact 3 is order-free*) now runs a sweep of
everything in a shuffled order against the constraints, on programs of at most 1 500 nodes; run
for this change on every program of the corpus whatever its size, it agreed everywhere (it
found one disagreement while the change was built, a guard killed through `this`, the last
bullet's case). Every output is byte for byte as before: all 519 `run/` and `browser/tea/`
programs built `--release` by both compilers, every `emit/release/` golden and every release
run hash.

Two smaller cuts of the same kind, each exact. **A round's first sweep of facts 1, 2, 4 and 5
counts from the record**: `countTop`'s record of a statement, kept while its module's version
stands, holds the whole-program names it read too, so the first sweep, which counts each read
once for the substitution rule, replays it as the later sweeps did. **`rewrite` drops dropped
parameters' arguments only in modules that name a function that lost one** (`rewriteCalls`):
a call of one names it.

**Another module's function, in one file** (*amended 2026-10-17*). *A function called once is
written where it is called* takes in another module's function only when the caller's module
already names every whole-program name the body names, "in the one scope-hoisted file and in the
multi-file layout alike". In a one-file build no module imports anything â every top-level name is
one binding of the one scope (`nameIn`) â so there the condition is dropped: the caller's module
names the body's names by their own `Name`, as slice 6 already does for a field read. The
multi-file layout keeps it. What it unlocked first: `Schema.validRun`, called once from the
program's `read`, named `endpointOf`, which the program's module did not, so the `Result` it
