**A body whose returns all end it, at a call statement** (*amended 2026-10-18*, the review of
`browser-inline`'s S1). A function of `â¤` written in beni with an `if` and no `else` â the runtime's
`text`, `if not (same â¦) then set â¦` â is lowered as `if (c) { â¦; return null } else { return null }`:
two valued `return`s, which no form above takes at a call statement, so a helper called once
stayed a call. Now, at a call statement, a body whose every `return` ends it â the last statement,
or the last of each branch of an `if`, or of an unlabelled block, that is the last â is written in
place with each such `return v` written as `v`, a statement, or as nothing when `v` is inert: the
call's value was never read, and control leaves the body there either way. An early `return`, or
one inside a loop, a `switch` or a `try`, keeps the call. A branch with no `return` is accepted too: control
falls off its end to the statement after the call, as it would have returned there. A function
that may suspend never meets the rule: its call is never a statement of the suspendable form, which
hands its value to `Task$andThen` (`emit/release/SuspendTailStatement`). Measured (release, brotli 11, every golden
it moved): `inline/CounterLocal` 529 â 523, `inline/FormLocal` 1 020 â 1 017,
`inline/PushAndTimer` 583 (the helper fused; it was 598 without `browser-inline`'s former special
case), `tea/HttpSendTracked` 6 784 â 6 771, `tea/HttpSendUntracked` 4 829 â 4 818,
`direct/ListScripts` 4 117 â 4 144 and `direct/TableSwap` 2 799 â 2 811. *Corrected 2026-10-18 (the
review of #350):* those two grow after brotli only. Their raw bytes shrink, 11 222 â 11 136 and
6 968 â 6 946, so the copy itself, `if`s included, is smaller than the call and the function
it replaces. The growth is compression context: the copied body (ListScripts' swap, 10 to 13
statements; TableSwap's, 28) leaves the runtime's run of similar code, where it compressed
against its neighbours, and every later top-level name shifts by one letter. One attempt at a
cost model that sees it, at most five statements copied, left ListScripts at 4 116 and TableSwap
at 2 799 but undid HttpSendTracked's and HttpSendUntracked's gains (6 783, 4 830): a statement count
does not predict brotli, so the rule stays as it is.
**Slice 9 across a call: a `case` on what a function returns** (*added 2026-10-17*, the owner's
decision for `browser-inline`'s first slice: a case of a known constructor fused across a call,
general, in this pass, for every platform). Slice 9 folds a constructor made by a *small* function.
A function of statements â a schema validator's worker, whose every `return` is a constructor, a
declared constructor or its failure mark â is not small, and its caller builds what it returns
only to test its tag and read its fields. The rule:

- **The site**: `const x = f(aâ, â¦, aâ)` in a function, and `R`, the statements after it in its
  list â a `return Râ²`, or the `switch` a `case` lowers to â where every argument is an atom (a
  literal or a name nothing assigns), `x` is mentioned nowhere but in `R`, and every mention of
  `x` in `R` is the object of a property read (`x.$`, `x.a.b`) or an operand of `===` or `!==`.
  `R` â one statement or several â holds no function, no loop, no `try` and no `continue`, is
  at most 96 units of slice 8's size model (`nodeCount`, statements 4 each), and cannot run off
  its end (the function's rule below, a `break` counting as a jump), so a copy of it may stand
  where `f` returned. An unlabelled `break` of `R` that leaves `R` refuses the site
  (`leavingBreak`): copied in place of a `return` inside a `switch` of `f`, it would leave that
  `switch` instead. A labelled one names its target and is the same jump in every copy.
- **The function**: a top-level `const f = (â¦) => {â¦}` of the program that nothing the pass cannot
  see names (`Input.escaping`), nothing assigns, whose every mention is the callee of such a site;
  some `return` of which gives a constructor (an object literal, a declared object, or a choice of
  them â slice 9's *producer*), whose body holds no function, no loop, no `try` and no
  `continue`, and whose every path ends in a jump â a list whose last statement is a `return`, a
  `throw` or a `break`, an `if` both of whose branches are such lists, an unlabelled block whose
  list is, or a `switch` with a `default`, holding no `break`, every case body of which is. A
  `break` inside the body leaves a statement of the body; one that leaves the site's rest is the
  same jump in every copy.
- **The rewrite**, at every site of `f` at once: `f`'s body is written in place of the two
  statements, its locals named fresh and each parameter its argument (*A function called once is
  written where it is called*), and each of its `return P` becomes `R[x := P]`, with what the value
  is known to be applied as the copy is made:
  - `x.k` of an object literal `P` is `P`'s value at `k`, and a chain reads on through nested
    literals; of a name or a member chain, `P.k`;
  - `x === y` (`!==`) of an object literal `P` is `false` (`true`) when `y` is a name or a member
    chain on one â a literal makes an object nothing else holds â and of a `P` that is the same
    member chain as `y` â a *stable chain*: on a local made by an object literal that nothing
    writes, mentions only through property reads and hands to no call but the site's (to a
    parameter `f` only reads properties of), ending at a value that is itself an object or array
    literal, or a `const` of one (never `NaN`) â `true` (`false`);
  - a conditional, `&&` or `||` whose test is then a literal, or `===`/`!==` of two literals, is the
    branch it chooses, and the other branch is not written;
  - a declared object's `$` is its literal's, by slice 9's test for a tag (`tagValue`: no code
    writes `$` on it); and `x === y` (`!==`) of a `P` that is a primitive literal or a declared
    object, with `y` a stable chain (above, an object made in the site's function), is `false`
    (`true`): neither can be that object;
  - an `if` the copy decides is the branch it takes, and a `switch` on a literal the case it
    takes, when that case holds no `break`; an unlabelled block of the rest is its statements,
    its declarations named afresh in each copy.

  A `P` that is a conditional `t ? A : B` is `if (t) { â¦A } else { â¦B }`, each branch the rest
  knowing its own value. A `P` that is none of these â a call's result, say â is bound once,
  `const xâ² = P; R[x := xâ²]`. `P` is an object literal read in place only when it is `inert` and
  names nothing the site's function assigns or the program reassigns (`immutableNames`), so no
  evaluation is dropped or moved past a write: reading its fields where `R` reads them evaluates
  names and literals, which cannot change between the `return` and `R`, because the function has
  no closure to write its locals. A value the literal holds that is itself made (an object, an
  array, a function) is read in place only when `R` reads it once in the copy; otherwise `P` is
  bound.
- **Gated by a size proxy**, like slice 8: the rewrite is made when the copies are smaller than
  what they replace by `Spec.stmtSize`, a count of nodes that stands in for bytes, not bytes â
  each expression's `nodeCount` (a literal or a property name its text, an operator its spelling,
  any other node a small constant) and 4 for each statement around them; Î£ over the sites of the
  copy's count, against `f`'s declaration plus Î£ over the sites of the replaced statements. Printed
  and compressed bytes can disagree with it: the proxy is what is asked, and the goldens pin what
  it chose. It is all or nothing: a function some site of which does not fit, or whose copies are not
  smaller, stays shared, so a kind's shared code (`browser-inline.md`, S5's sharing by kind) is
  never undone for a gain smaller than the function. Slice 5's single-call rule, which runs first,
  is unchanged: a body of one `return` called once is written there without being priced.

**A `switch` on a literal is the case it takes**, wherever it stands (`chosenCase`, the facts'
`if` folding extended): its discriminant a literal, every case test a literal, the first test
`===` it â else the `default` â chosen, when that case's body holds no `break` and cannot run off
its end into the next. A schema primitive's worker switches on its kind, which the program
passes as a literal: `run/` programs that read a `Schema.value` kept every kind's arm.

Measured (release, brotli 11): `emit/release/inline/PushAndTimer` 756 â **709** (the worker
written into the program's `read`, its `Set` and `Ok` never built), `app/ValidatorRun` 963 â
**691** (the literal `switch` of `Schema.value`'s worker, and what only its other arms reached);
every other golden unchanged. The compiler pays for asking: on `browser/direct/ApiLogin`,
where nothing fuses, the release builds count 1 639 â 1 658 and 1 449 â 1 467 million
instructions, most of it the walk over every function some `return` of which makes a
constructor.

Soundness is the `case`'s: `language.md` Â§6's order is the call's â the arguments (atoms), then the
body, then `R` â and the only values dropped are constructors nothing else could see (`x` reaches
nothing but `R`'s reads and comparisons). Fixtures: `emit/release/app/CaseAcrossCall` (one function
fused at its one site; one called from three sites that stays shared; a site that reads `x` whole,
which keeps the call), `emit/release/inline/PushAndTimer` (the validator's worker fused into the
program's `read`: no `Set` and no `Ok` is built), and `run/CaseAcrossCall`, the same program run in
both builds.

*Amended 2026-10-24 (#934, the S1 hand-minify pass's S2): a validator fused into the decode-or-keep
that calls it.* A schema validator run whose value its function returns,
`Result.withDefault (Json.decodeValue v) d`, is lowered `const c = validContext(); const x = W(c,
…, v); return x === c.fail ? d : x`. The rule above refused it twice: the rest reads `x` whole,
and `c` is made by a call, not by an object literal. So every route's `replace` kept a wrapper
round its worker, and a context, and the comparison. Three extensions take it, each exact:
- **`x` read whole, only as what a `return` gives.** A mention of `x` that is the value of a
  `return` of the rest, or a branch of a conditional that is (`returnedWhole`), is allowed beside
  the property reads and comparisons. Such a read is the last thing done with `x`, so nothing has
  stored `x` before a comparison reads it, and `x === y` of an object literal stays `false`: the
  literal makes an object nothing else holds. In a copy it is `P`; an object literal `P` is made
  there, at most once per copy (`projectsToAtoms`), so no object is made twice, and making an
  `inert` literal later than the `return` cannot be seen. Any other whole read — an argument of a
  call, a field of a record — refuses the site, as before.
- **An alias of `x` is `x`.** A `const z = x` of the rest, `z` declared once and never assigned —
  what slice 9 leaves of a `case` on the run, its `Ok new` pattern bound to the value — is held to
  every rule `x` is held to, and so is an alias of an alias. A comparison of `x` with one of its
  aliases, which an object literal `P` would decide `false`, refuses the site.
- **A stable chain through a call that makes a fresh object.** `y`'s initialiser may be a call,
  with no arguments, of a top-level `const f = () => {…}` that nothing assigns and nothing the
  pass cannot see names, whose body is `const`s of object and array literals of atoms and then a
  `return` of an object literal whose value at `k` is an object or array literal or one of those
  `const`s (`makesFreshAt`). Each call makes its own object and its own value at `k`, which only
  `y` holds, so two reads of `y.k` give one object, never `NaN`, and `y.k === y.k` is `true` —
  the same rule as an object literal's, under the same conditions on every other mention of `y`.
  `validContext` is such a function once specialisation has folded it to `() => ({a: []})`.
- **A parameter handed on is still only inspected.** A parameter that `f`'s body passes to a
  top-level function (one nothing assigns and nothing the pass cannot see names, called with all
  its arguments) counts as a property read when that function only reads properties of the
  parameter it takes, by the same rule, taken to be true while it is being asked (`inspectedIn`).
  A worker hands its context to the worker of a nested record, which only reads `c.fail` and
  passes it on.

Order is the rule's: the arguments, then `f`'s body, then the rest written at each `return`. The
rest is evaluated where it was, after everything `f` did on that path, and nothing of it is moved
before anything `f` does that could throw. Then `x === c.fail` is decided at each `return`, the
default is what each failure returns, and the context is read by nothing, so the optimiser drops
it. S1's N = 1 wrapper `x=(a,b)=>{let c=u(),d=w(c,a);return d===c.a?b:d}` and its worker become
`v=(a,b)=>{if(typeof a!=="object"||a===null||Array.isArray(a))return b;…;return{d:c,a:d,c:e,b:f}}`,
the route row holds `v`, and `u` goes from the page. Pinned by `Spec`'s unit tests *a call's
object is fresh, with its own value at a key, only for a function of literals* (a number, a
parameter, a value a call made and a missing key refuse) and *a fused site's binding may be read
whole only as what a return gives*; by `emit/release/app/ValidatorFused` (one function fused, one
whose run a record holds kept); and by `run/ValidatorFused`. Measured (release, brotli 11, against
the goldens before): `app/ValidatorRun` 591 → 537, `app/ValidatorWorker` 637 → 588,
`app/ValidatorNoPath` 635 → 599, `app/PayloadUnreadField` 689 → 635, `inline/ValidatedLoader`
1 218 → 1 195, `inline/CaseLoader` 1 409 → 1 367, `inline/ErrorUnreadWidgets` 1 167 → 1 117;
`inline/NestedStableLoad` 1 272 → 1 282 grows after brotli only, its raw bytes 3 352 → 3 256 (the
copied worker leaves the run of similar workers it compressed against, as `direct/ListScripts` did
above). S1 `unique-components`, one file, seeds 1–3: N = 1 1 482 / 1 424 / 1 655 → 1 461 / 1 410 /
1 643, N = 16 6 107 / 6 135 / 5 910 → 6 042 / 6 049 / 5 851; N = 64 and 256 are on the shapes side
and do not move. The event decoder is not fused into the push's dispatcher: the rest there makes
a function (the snapshot's `a => g[a[2]]`), which the rule does not copy.

**A function that only calls a function is that function** (*added 2026-10-17*; `Spec.etaIn`, in
the last sweep). `() => g()` is `g` where `g` is a local an earlier statement of the same list
declares, once, as an arrow of no parameters, and nothing assigns it. Neither function takes a
parameter or reads `this`, so a call of either, with any arguments, runs `g`'s body and answers
what it answers; and `g` is bound by then, since its declaration ran before. Arguments of the
inner call that are literals (`null`, the `â¤` a lowering passes) take no parameter and do
nothing, so they go. `setInterval(()=>r(),1000)` is `setInterval(r,1000)`, and then the single-use
rule of item 1 makes `r` there.

**A short `switch` is its `if`s** (*added 2026-10-17*; `Spec.switchAsIfs`, the last sweep of every
statement list). `switch (k)` on a name, with at most three cases besides a `default` that comes
last, every
case's test a literal, and every body holding no `break` and unable to run off its end, is
`if (k === t) { body }` for each case in order, then the `default`'s statements. A literal test
does nothing and a body that cannot complete never falls into the next case, so the cases are tried,
and one is run, exactly as the `switch` tries and runs them. A body that is one unlabelled block is
the block's statements (an `if`'s body is a scope of its own); the `default`'s join the list where
the `switch` stood when they declare nothing, or when no other statement of the list names what
they declare. `switch(k){case"set":{â¦}case"reset":{return R}default:{return F}}` is
`if(k==="set"){â¦}if(k==="reset")return R;return F`. Measured (brotli 11):
`emit/release/inline/PushAndTimer` 628 â 611, `app/ValidatorRun` 655 â 643; no other golden moved.

### The combined solver

*Specified 2026-10-02, normative for `src/js/Spec.zig`'s analysis from slice 4 of research 52
Â§4.5 on; the owner adopted the architecture that day (research 52 Â§0.3). The review it rests on
is research 52 Â§8, whose findings G1âG11 this section cites. Nothing here is built yet: where the
code and this section disagree before a slice lands, the code is the old design.* It replaces
*Whole-program specialisation*'s rounds of analyse â rewrite â prune (and the worklist note's
sweeps) with **one optimistic, combined, sparse fixpoint per structural pass, read once by one
rewrite**. The facts are the ones above â constants and truthiness, points-to, fields, returns,
the allocated-once fact, guards, definite initialisation â plus two the rounds approximated by
repetition: which code is executable, and which local binding is live. What the rewrite does
with a fact is unchanged unless a slice below says so.

#### Where it runs

Per structural pass of `Spec.run`, in this order:

1. **Extract** (workers, one task per module): walk the module's `JsIr` once and emit its
   constraints, its cells' local numbering and its statements' name counts (*Extraction*). A
   module whose `Mod.version` did not change since the last extraction keeps its arrays.
2. **Merge** (calling thread): number every module's cells and constraints by prefix sums in
   module order, intern the literals in that order, build the readers index.
3. **Solve** (calling thread): the worklist to its fixpoint (*The worklist*).
4. **Read off** (calling thread): executability, reachability and liveness (*Reading off*).
5. **Rewrite** (workers, one task per module): patch each module from the final facts, which no
   step of the rewrite changes (*The rewrite*).
6. **Structural passes** (calling thread, unchanged): small functions, functions called once,
   constructor folding, scalar replacement, then the `iife` and `self_assign` list modes â moved
   into this loop (research 52 Â§8.3, G9) â and, when one changed the program, back to step 1, at
   most `max_passes` = 3 times, counted (`spec_passes`, `spec_passes_capped`).

`trimArguments`, `releaseKeeps` and the solve after it disappear into steps 4â5 (G9). The
pipeline around `Spec.run` (`backend.md` Â§9's *One scope-hoisted file*, `Opt`, `Fields`) is
unchanged.

*Amended 2026-10-22 (issue #781): the structural passes first.* Before step 1 of the first pass,
`Spec.run` runs step 6's passes once on the program as lowering left it (`structureFirst`): small
functions, functions called once, constructor folding, scalar replacement and the `tidy` list
modes. No fact exists yet. `Mod.memo` is â¤, and fact 3 has not solved, so `pts.ok` is false.
Every question a pass asks of the facts is therefore answered as for a value nothing is known
of. So a small function is written in only where it is called by its name, because no fact 3
resolves a callee. A whole-program name counts as assigned when any `assign_stmt` of the program,
live or not, names it. That is what the solve would conclude, or more. The declarations are
numbered as `analyse` numbers them (`declTable`). When a pass changed the program, `prune` and
`grow` follow, and then the loop runs as before.

What is written in is solved once, in the context of its call site. If the passes after that
solve find nothing more, the program is solved once instead of twice. N = 64, the variant without
`withDefault` and the 100 000 lines are such programs: their second solve, about 12% of their
build's instructions, is gone, and their output does not change.

The order costs only where a pass, run without facts, leaves a shape the one solve folds less
well than the old order did. Before, the solve that followed the structural pass also absorbed
the first rewrite's cascades: a key, parameter or binding that only became unread when the
rewrite and `prune` took its last read. When the pass after the solve now finds nothing, no solve
comes to take those. The As built note below lists the programs this costs bytes, and names an
issue for each cause.

#### Cells

A **cell** is a `u32`. Every cell holds a value of the product lattice (*Values*); a cell's id
is fixed before solving, by its module's extraction and the prefix sums of the merge, so ids
follow module order and IR order whatever the threads did (rule 5). The kinds, each a dense
range:

| Kind | One per | Replaces |
|---|---|---|
| node | value-producing `JsIr` node of a module (the cell id is the module's base plus the node index) | `Mod.memo`, `Pts.vals` (D1) |
| name | whole-program name (`Input.globals`, and `addGlobal`'s) | `Pts.globals`, `nameValue`'s module-level reads |
| local | local binding: (top-level statement, name) in the order extraction meets them; a parameter is its function's local | `Mod.value`, `Spec.params`, `Pts.locals` (D7) |
| return | function node (arrow, `function`, generator) | `ret_lat`, `Pts.Site.ret` (D2) |
| site | object, array and function node (allocation site) | `Pts.sites`; its facets are columns: `escaped`, `all_read`, `any_written`, `once`, `prog_any`, `odd_caller` |
| field | (site, property id), made when a load or store first reaches it, in a pool; per site a sorted run of (property, cell) found by binary search | `prop_lat`, `Pts.Prop` (D2, D3) |
| exec | function body, and arm: an `if`'s two, a `?:`'s two, a `&&`'s or `||`'s right side, each `case` | â (new, slice 6) |

Values live in **columns indexed by cell**, sized at the merge: `lat: []Lat` (four bytes: state,
truthiness, literal), `pts: []u8` (the four bits `top`, `prim`, `nul`, `undef`), `set: []SetId` and
`done: []SetId` (the site set, and the part of it already propagated), and the `exec` bitset.
A **site set** is an immutable sorted `[]u32` held in a hash-consed set table (content-addressed,
so its id is the same whichever cell made it first); a cell's set is replaced, never grown in
place (G2). Field cells, made during the solve, number in solve order; no answer depends on their
numbering, since every consumer finds one by (site, property).

#### Values

The product of `Spec.Lat` â â¥ < literal | `name` < *nonnull* < â¤, with truthiness â¥ < truthy |
falsy < either beside it (slice 3) â and fact 3's `Pts.Val` â `top`, `prim`, `nul`, `undef` and a
site set capped at `max_sites` = 48, past which it is `top` and its sites escape; `top` implies the
other three bits (slice 2). Each component joins on its own. **Every transfer function is
monotone, component by component**, and is written as a join over what its operands may be:
never "a constant while some fact is still false, something else after". The rule bites where
today's code special-cases: a read `x.p` through objects all of which are the program's own is
â¨ over `x`'s sites of (the field cell, â `undefined` where the literal lacks `p` and definite
initialisation did not find it) â which is `undefined` exactly while nothing is written, as
`neverWritten` says today, and grows from there â not "`undefined` if never written, else the
field". Each transfer function has a property test over small lattices (research 52 Â§4.3), and
the safety build's order check (*Determinism*) catches any that slips.

#### Extraction

One walk of a module's `JsIr` per extraction, on a worker, reading nothing but the module and
`Input` (its `global` and `prop` columns): it emits the module's constraints as flat arrays â
`op: []Op` (a `u8`), `exec: []u32` (the exec cell gating it), `a`, `b`, `out: []u32`, `node: []u32` â
with variable-length operands (a call's arguments, an object's keys) in a `u32` pool, and per
top-level statement the names it declares, reads and assigns (the counts `countTop`, `inlineScan`,
`declCount` and `nameUses` each make today, G7), its guards' Ï-copies with their kills, its
definite-initialisation candidates, and the literal nodes to intern. The kinds, each a `switch`
arm of the solver:

| Constraint | Meaning | From |
|---|---|---|
| `lit n â c` | the literal | literal nodes |
| `copy a â c` | `c â a` | a binding's initialiser, an assignment to a name, an argument to a known function's parameter, a `return` to its function's return cell |
| `op a, b â c` | `unary`, `binary`, `templateValue`, `identity` over the operand cells; `&&`/`||` and `?:` with their truthiness rules | operators, conditionals, templates |
| `Ï a â c` | `a` narrowed by a guard (not `null`, not `undefined`) while every listed kill is a read through program objects | `Pts.narrowed` with `kill`, `guardNames` (G9) |
| `alloc s â c` | the site, with its literal keys as stores | object, array and function nodes |
| `load o, p â c`; `store o, p â v`; `loadAll`; `storeAny`; `spread` | fact 3's reads and writes, on every site `o` holds, through the field cells | member reads and writes, computed ones, `forâ¦of`, spreads |
| `call f, args â c` | for every function site in `f`: arguments to parameters, return to `c`, the call recorded as a caller, the body made executable; for anything else: the arguments escape, `c` is â¤ | calls; the entry file's call (`Input.entry`) |
| `escape v` | `v`'s sites escape | `throw`, a host call's arguments, `Input.escaping`, a value written to â¤ |
| `branch t â then, else` | an arm is executable when its parent is and `t`'s truthiness allows it | `if`, `?:`, `&&`, `||`; each `case` arm whenever the `switch` is |

The `escaped`, `assigned` and `reads` columns of today's sweeps are extraction facts (they are
syntactic). The literals are interned at the merge, in module order, so their ids do not depend
on the workers.

#### Executability

An exec cell is a bit, false until something makes it true. The roots: every module's top-level
code; every name `Input.escaping` lists and the entry's call; every function whose site escapes
(IPSCCP's rule: address-taken means executable, and its parameters are â¤). A function body becomes
executable when an executable `call` reaches its site; an arm when its `branch` allows it. **A
constraint whose exec cell is false contributes nothing** â no argument, no write, no allocation,
no escape, no caller (Click's mixed functions). A callee that may be â¤ (a host value) reaches every
escaped function, which is already executable. Exec bits only become true, and an arm's rule is
monotone in its test's truthiness, so executability is one more monotone component. Until slice 6
every exec cell is true from the start, which is today's analysis: both arms of every `if` and
every body.

*Amended 2026-10-22 (issue #685).* **Every function body is a root, for now.** Fact 3's call graph
misses calls the program makes: in `run/TaskRootScope`, a function that runs, the bracket's use
function, has one recorded caller, and that caller is in a body the graph never reaches from a root,
though Task runs that function through its fibers' frames. A body the solve leaves false contributes no
argument to the functions it calls, so a parameter every other call passes the same literal would
be dropped under a call that passes another. Until the graph is complete, every body is
executable and only arms are decided. Arms are decided by the test's truthiness, which does not rest
on the graph. Research 52's E2 (`SpecSelfGuard`) and `SpecDeadArm` are arms, and no `emit/release`
golden moves.

*Amended 2026-10-22 (issue #685): a check.* A hidden, test-only `--check-call-graph` runs the
call graph on its own after every fact-3 solve (`Spec.checkCallGraph`). The roots are those
executability had before the amendment above: a function site that escaped, one with
`odd_caller`, and one held in a site's `any` or under an implicit host key. A call reaches the
function sites its callee may be when it stands at a module's top level or in a reached body.
Arms are not asked. Every function body that some solve leaves unreached is then written as
`throw "beni: --check-call-graph: â¦"` (`poisonMissed`). The corpus's release passes build with the
flag: `run/`, the `--schema-library` pass, the `browser/` pages and the value-fuzz pages. So a
program that calls a body the graph missed fails a gate loudly, instead of printing something
else. When the check landed it found no such body in the corpus. Without it, nothing tests the
graph's completeness, which the revert of this amendment needs.

*Amended 2026-10-22 (issue #685): the call graph is complete, and a body runs only when it is
reached.* A function body is again a root only when it is reached as follows. Every way the
emitted JavaScript can run a beni function body is one of the following, and each is covered by a
root or an edge:
1. **A call node of the program** (`f(x)`, `o.m(x)`, `o[k](x)`, `new C(x)`). An executable `call`
   turns on the body of every function site its callee may be (`Solver.calls`, fact 3's `vals` of
   the callee). The callee's value is exact: a member read is the read's load cell, and a computed
   read `o[k]` is `readAll` of `o`, every property, marked `all_read`. A `new` sets `odd_caller`,
   which is a root.
2. **A call through a value held in a site.** A site's property holds its value in a var (or a
   field summary), and a read gives it, so the call is case 1. A value under a key the pass does
   not know is in the site's `any`, which is a root. This covers an array's elements and an
   unknown-key write.
3. **Escape to the host or to foreign code**, including core's JavaScript siblings, the fiber
   runtime's frames and the markup runtime. A value passed to a callee fact 3 does not know (an
   import of a hand-written file is â¤), returned to it, or written into an object it cannot see
   (â¤, or an escaped site) escapes. An escaped site escapes everything it holds (`propagate`),
   and an escaped function is a root. A call of an unknown callee escapes its arguments and its
   receiver, so `stack.pop()` on the fiber runtime's array escapes the frames in it. A var that
   becomes â¤ escapes every site it held or later holds (`makeTop`). `Js.method` makes a function
   JavaScript calls with a receiver, and writing one escapes it and its object (`holdsMethod`).
4. **A key the host reads unasked** (`toJSON`, `toString`, `valueOf`): a function held under one
   is a root.
5. **`any`**: as in case 2.
6. **Getters and setters.** The IR makes none. An object literal has plain properties and
   spreads only, so no read or write runs code beyond case 4.
7. **The platform's entry.** The entry file's `start`, `flush`, `main` and `run`, and what the
   markup runtime imports from the runtime module, are `Input.escaping` and escape. The entry's
   `run(main)` is a call that sets `odd_caller` (`entryCall`).
8. **The markup lowering's handlers.** A handler is handed to the markup runtime through a call,
   either a call of an imported runtime function (case 3) or of the program's own runtime (case
   1). The DOM then calls it through `addEventListener`, an unknown callee, so it escapes in
   either case.

Two classes stay conservative, because fact 3 has nothing precise to say about them: a body fact
3 made no site for is a root, and when fact 3 did not reach its fixpoint (`pts.ok` false) every
body is a root. A call that stands in an arm facts 1, 2 and 5 decide is never taken does not
count. Those facts do not rest on the call graph. `--check-call-graph` (above) tests the graph,
without arms, on the whole corpus. `run/CallGraphComputedMethod` (a function kept in a JavaScript
array and taken out by a method named at run time) and `run/CallGraphComputedKey` (a record's
function field read by a key made at run time) pin cases 2 and 3 under it. Taking back the "every
body is a root" rule recovers the 92 bytes it cost: `run/MainParkedForever` and
`run/MainParkedOnNever` −40 each, `run/MutualDispatchMethods` −12, no other program and no golden. It
costs 0.3–0.5% instructions on N = 16, N = 64 and nowd (the solve turns bodies on as calls
reach them, and evaluates what they open), and 0.02% on the 100 000 lines. A computed method's
receiver now escapes as a named one's does (`o[k](x)`, case 3).

#### The worklist

Two queues, rings of `u32` with a bitset of what is queued: changed cells and newly executable
exec cells. A changed cell wakes the constraints that read it: the static readers, a CSR index
(offsets and constraint ids) built at the merge by counting sort, and the dynamic ones a `load`,
`store` or `call` registers on a field cell or a function's parameters as its operand's site set
grows, in a pool of linked `u32` pairs (today's `Pts.deps`). An exec cell becoming true queues the
constraints it gates (a CSR index of its own). **Site sets propagate their difference**: a cell's
`set \ done` is what its `copy` successors and the `load`s, `store`s and `call`s reading it act
on, and `done` becomes `set` once they have (Pereira & Berlin's wave, SVF's `AndersenWaveDiff`);
a `lat` change re-evaluates the reader whole, which is a few instructions. The queues are seeded in
cell order and drained first in, first out; any other fair order reaches the same fixpoint.

**Termination** is the lattice's: a cell's `lat` changes at most 6 times, its bits 4, its set at
most 48 times before it is `top`, an exec bit once. There is no sweep cap and no round cap. A work
budget â 64 evaluations per constraint and cell â is an assertion: a safety build that exceeds it
panics, naming a cell still changing; a release build sets every cell still queued, and every exec
cell, to â¤ and drains (â¤ is a fixpoint above any other, so the facts stay sound), and counts it
(`spec_budget_hit`). Never "rewrite nothing" (research 52 Â§2.1, *Stopping early*).

#### Calls with known results

*Decision 3 of research 52, approved by the owner 2026-10-02 with four constraints, built as a
mixed function of the `call` constraint, not as a pass of its own (slice 8a).* When a call's callee
cell holds exactly one function site, that function is **pure by the checker's inference**
(`Input` carries the checker's purity bit per whole-program function, `checker-v2.md` Â§26), and
every argument cell is a literal, the call is **evaluated**: the function's body is interpreted
with those literals bound, by the folds the facts already make â integers that are safe, booleans,
string concatenation and ASCII comparison, `===`, truthiness; nothing else, so no transcendental
`Math` and no float-to-string, only what the compiler computes exactly as V8 does â following a
call it makes when that call qualifies in turn. The evaluation is **bounded** (a step budget and a
depth, both counted when hit): one that finishes yields a literal; one that runs out, meets an
operation outside the list, or would throw yields nothing, so a call that does not terminate or
that crashes is never hidden. Results are memoised by (function, arguments). A literal so found is
the call cell's value â joined, like every value, so a call whose arguments later stop being
literals is the function's return as before â and the rewrite writes the call as the literal
**only when the literal prints no longer than the call**. Because the call is pure and was
evaluated to completion, an expression around it that folds to a literal may drop it, which keeps
the invariant every fold rests on: a node whose value is a literal does nothing when evaluated.
The parked prototype (`constantCall`, `foldsTo` on the branch `spec-call-results-parked`) is the
reference for the evaluator, not code to merge. Cloning (decision 4) is not part of this.

#### Reading off

After the solve, three read-offs, each a function of the final cells:

- **Executability.** An arm whose exec cell is false is not printed; a function body that is not
  executable belongs to a function nothing live calls (slice 6). The rewrite keeps the arm an
  `if` takes, as `foldList` does today; a test that may do something stays, before it (slice 3's
  `T; â¦arm`).
- **Reachability** (`prune`, now a read-off): a top-level declaration is live when it is a root
  (a statement whose evaluation may do something, `Input.escaping`, the entry's call) or an
  executable read of a live binding names it.
- **Liveness of bindings**: a local binding is live when an executable read reads it or lowering
  keeps it for its initialiser's effect (`effect_keep`); only a live binding's initialiser
  references anything, and a write to a binding nothing live reads goes (master's `unreadName`).
  This is what `Opt` will conclude, known before `Spec` decides (G8): `deadReads`, `releaseKeeps`
  and `unreadName` go.

#### The rewrite

One rewrite per solve, on the workers, one module per task: every step reads the final cells and
the read-offs, and none writes them, so the order modules or statements are patched in cannot
change the output (G4 â `stale`, `declined`, `folded_reads` and the `now_literal` round go). What
it does is today's: a node whose value is a literal is written as the literal under the
substitution rule (5 bytes, or read once â by the extracted read counts, executable reads only); a
parameter every call passes the same literal, or that nothing reads and no argument for it does
anything, goes with its arguments; a key nothing reads goes from its literal and a write of it
from the program; `appendChild`; trailing arguments nothing reads (`trimArguments`); a test decided
by its truthiness where skipping it loses nothing (`effectFreeTest`, the one purity test the
rewrite asks, G7); what follows a statement that cannot complete. A name written in a module that
lacks it is added to that module only, so the tasks share nothing they write.

#### Determinism

By construction: ids come from extraction and the merge in module order; every transfer function
is monotone, so the fixpoint is the least one whatever order the queues take; the rewrite reads
only final facts. **Checked** in safety builds on programs of at most `max_checked_nodes` = 1 500
nodes: the solve is run twice â first in first out, then last in first out from the reversed
seeding â and every cell's value, every exec bit and every field (by site and property) must agree
(today's shuffled-order check of fact 3, slice 2, extended to every cell). The determinism test
(`--jobs=1` against `--jobs=8`, twice each) covers the workers.

#### Memory

Per node about 60 bytes at most for the life of one structural pass: 13 per cell (`lat`, the bits,
`set`, `done`) for its node cell and its share of the others, 21 per constraint, 8 per reader
edge; site sets hash-consed, so cells that hold the same set hold one copy. Three arenas: the
extraction arrays (kept per module across the passes while its version stands), the solve's
columns and pools (reset after the rewrite), the set table (reset with them). Today every analysis
allocates new per-node arrays into one arena that lives for the whole pass (D4): a `--release`
build of `bench --generate=100000` as a library peaks at 377 MB. Each slice reports peak RSS on
TodoMVC, that build and `abuse_wide_test`, and none may raise it by more than 5%.

**As built 2026-10-21 â the solve's memory reused between runs** (issue #574, part of #464). A
release build solves fact 3 up to six times (one fewer where an analysis keeps it, #575). Every
run took its per-node and per-name columns (`vals`, `site_of`, `name_var`/`name_top`,
`node_var`/`node_top`, `ones`, `globals`), its vars, sites, locals and statement list anew
from the compilation's arena, which kept each run's copy until the build ended.
The fixpoint's own arena, a `std.heap.ArenaAllocator`, was reset with `.retain_capacity`, which
in Zig 0.17 frees every chunk but the last and reallocates that one, so a run that outgrew it
faulted a fresh mapping the next time. `inlineOne` and `fuseOne` took three
arrays as long as the program's names on each of their hundreds of calls, and `inlineScan` took
every module's counts anew whenever a body written at the top added a name. Page faults were a
quarter of the N = 64 dashboard's wall time. Now:

- **One run arena** (`Pts.tmp`, `src/Arena.zig`) holds everything of one run: those columns, the
  vars, sites, locals, constraints, edges, summaries, load cells, the set table, and `Spec`'s
  arrays of one analysis (`spread_sites`, the sweeps' dependency lists). The solve's columns and
  pools and the set table are reset together, as above, in one arena.
- **It is emptied with `Arena.ResetMode.keep_all`** at the start of each run. That frees no chunk
  and opens them again in the order the run before opened them, so a run that repeats its
  predecessor's allocations lands on the same pages, already mapped. The columns come first and
  are filled again where the last run left them, grown in place when a pass added nodes.
- **The safety build's reference run** fills an arena of its own, swapped in as before, which
  `expectSame` reads after the build's run has refilled `tmp`.
- **The inliner's scratch is kept** across calls, and `inlineScan`'s counts across an added name
  (`Spec.scratchOf`, grown by half again past the need).
- **The compilation's arena keeps only what outlives a run**: `extra_init`, the walk's stacks,
  the modules' property columns. A unit test pins it: a second fixpoint takes nothing from that
  arena and no new chunk, and its columns are the first's memory.

No fact moved: every `emit/release/` golden and run hash is byte for byte the same, and the
shuffled-order check is unchanged. ReleaseFast, `build --release --no-cache --jobs=1` on dagon
(Ryzen 9 5950X), against master with #575, before â after. Faults and peak RSS are medians of 5 or
7 runs; the times are the minima of 11 interleaved runs, on a quiet host:

| program | minor faults | peak RSS | sys | wall |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| research dashboard N = 16 | 13 600 â 8 700 | 56 â 40 MB | 0.02 â 0.01 s | 0.07 â 0.07 s |
| research dashboard N = 64 | 56 300 â 31 100 | 180 â 115 MB | 0.08 â 0.04 s | 0.33 â 0.29 s |
| N = 64 without `withDefault` | 46 300 â 28 000 | 163 â 103 MB | 0.07 â 0.04 s | 0.29 â 0.26 s |
| `bench --generate=100000`, `--library`, names migrated | 92 000 â 68 000 | 348 â 273 MB | 0.15 â 0.12 s | 0.56 â 0.52 s |
| `browser/tea/TodoMVC` | 9 800 â 5 700 | 44 â 31 MB | | |
| `abuse_wide_test`'s 16 400 arms | 11 600 â 10 800 | 33 â 30 MB | | |

What is left of the faults:

- **Run 1** touches its arena once: 38 MB at N = 64, about half of it lists that grew and left
  their old copy behind, which a bump arena cannot reuse within a run.
- **A run that outgrows every earlier one** faults its growth: at N = 64, the solve after the second
  inlining pass takes the arena to 77 MB.
- **`Spec`'s own caches** still go to the compilation's arena between the runs: `nameScan`'s
  per-statement uses, `preorder`, `inlineSmall`'s copies.

There is no extraction yet to keep per module while `Mod.version` stands: `Pts` still makes every
constraint from its walk (slice 5).

**As built 2026-10-21 â the hot columns grow in place, scratch stays mapped, huge pages on Linux**
(issue #606, part of #464; `plans/build-profile-2026-10-21b.md`, cause 2). After #574 page faults
were still about a quarter of the N = 64 dashboard's wall time. A throwaway stack trace of every
large free the run arena could not take back put 44 MB of the four runs' garbage on eight lists:
`vars`, `cold`, `links_of` (`newVar`), `field_outs` (`copyField`), `edges` (`copy`), `sites`,
`deps` and `summaries`, each grown by copying past the others. Now:

- **Each of those eight is a column** with an arena of its own (`Spec.RunArena`, reset, swapped and
  freed as one with the rest of the run's memory). A column is its arena's only allocation, so it
  grows in place (`Arena.resize`), and its first chunk is a 256 MiB reservation
  (`Arena.initColumn`) on 64-bit Linux and macOS, where untouched memory costs only address space:
  a column is never copied, and leaves nothing behind. Elsewhere â Windows, which commits what it
  maps, and the playground's `wasm32-wasi` â and where the backing allocator refuses the
  reservation, the arena opens what the request needs and the column grows in ordinary chunks.
- **The per-module and per-item scratch is emptied with `keep_all`**: check's worker arenas and
  its patterns arena (per `case`), the frontend's per-file worker arenas, the emit workers'
  per-item arena (lowering, printing), and ownership's per-depth walk arenas, which were
  `std.heap.ArenaAllocator`s and are now `Arena`s.
- **On Linux a chunk of 2 MiB or more is whole 2 MiB pages, aligned to one, and advised
  `MADV_HUGEPAGE`**; a column's chunk is advised past its first huge page, so a short column costs
  the small pages it fills. Advice only: a kernel without transparent huge pages ignores it. Every
  other target opens chunks as before.

Only where memory lives moved: every `emit/release/` golden and run hash is byte for byte the same,
`--jobs=1` and `--jobs=8` write the same files, and `zig build test-playground` passes. Unit tests
pin a huge chunk's placement, a column that grows to megabytes without moving or a second

5950X, THP `madvise`/`madvise`, load 1.8â2.5), medians of 11 interleaved runs, master â this
change (â the same without huge pages, which is what macOS gets):

| program | `--jobs` | minor faults | sys | wall | peak RSS |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| dashboard N = 16 | 1 | 8 200 â 5 000 (7 300) | 18 â 15 ms (18) | 62 â 56 ms (61) | 37.1 â 37.8 MB (34.0) |
| dashboard N = 16 | 8 | 10 600 â 7 400 (9 600) | 31 â 25 ms (28) | 59 â 53 ms (57) | 36.6 â 37.0 MB (33.2) |
| dashboard N = 64 | 1 | 29 000 â 11 300 (23 300) | 55 â 32 ms (46) | 201 â 169 ms (185) | 104.3 â 95.7 MB (86.2) |
| dashboard N = 64 | 8 | 31 500 â 13 900 (25 900) | 71 â 53 ms (62) | 186 â 156 ms (171) | 103.9 â 94.8 MB (85.3) |
