**Huge pages are a bet on the host.** With `defrag` at `madvise`, a fault in an advised range
compacts memory synchronously to find a free 2 MiB page. On dagon, whose free memory is fragmented
(few order-9 blocks, 97% of its compaction attempts fail), one interleaved run under another
agent's load gave a build with huge pages alone *twice* master's sys time at N = 64 (121 against 57 ms);
the three runs at low load gave the gains above. The columns and `keep_all` win on every host and lower
peak RSS; huge pages win most of the faults and pay up to 2 MiB of RSS per large chunk.

What is left (11.3k faults at N = 64): first touches of live data, spread thin â the columns
themselves, check's type stores (one per module, kept for ownership and the backend), lowering's
name maps, the frontend's artifacts, and `Spec.analyse`'s per-analysis arrays, which still go to
the compilation's arena once per analysis.

#### Building it â research 52 Â§4.5's slices 4â8

Each slice is gates-green, measured (instructions of the ReleaseSafe compiler and peak RSS on
`browser/tea/TodoMVC`, `bench --generate=100000` as a `--library` release build with its names
migrated, and `abuse_wide_test`'s 16 400 arms; `zig build bench`), and compared build by build with
the compiler before over every `run/` and `browser/` fixture and the `bench/todomvc` app.

4. **Extraction, the merge and the solver, for facts 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 and truthiness, every exec cell
   true; fact 3 still `Pts`, read as input.** In safety builds on programs of at most 1 500 nodes,
   the sweeps run too and must agree with the solver on every node value they computed, every
   parameter, field, return and decided conditional, and the `escaped`, `assigned` and `reads`
   columns; the panic names the node. Byte-identical. Then the sweeps, `checkedSweeps`,
   `count_logs` and `max_sweeps` go, with the check.
5. **Fact 3 into the same cells and constraints**; `prop_lat`, `ret_lat`, `decided_conds` and
   `Pts`' walker go. The same double run against `Pts` (each site taken for the one its node made,
   as slice 2's check does). Byte-identical. `max_pts_sweeps` goes.
6. **Executability, the read-offs and the rewrite once**; rounds go (`max_rounds`), `prune`,
   `deadReads`, `releaseKeeps`, `unreadName` and `trimArguments` become read-offs, and the `iife`
   and `self_assign` modes join the pass loop. `emit/release/app/SpecDeepChain` and
   `SpecSelfGuard` move (research 52's E1 and E2 fold), and so does `run/DerivedPartTypedLater`
   (G8); every other move is listed and justified. `spec_analyses` becomes `spec_solves`.
7. **Definite initialisation as a may-fact** in the solver (research 52 Â§3.5); `max_init_runs` and
   the restarts go. Byte-identical or smaller.
8. **Calls with known results** (8a, above, approved); **cloning** (8b) is **dropped** (the owner,
   2026-10-04): no mainstream JavaScript compiler clones, and the engine specialises hot code itself.

*Amended 2026-10-22 (issue #637).* **E1's cliff goes with slice 4, not slice 6.** It was
`max_sweeps`, and the solver has no sweep to run out of, so `emit/release/app/SpecDeepChain` moves
in slice 4: every `x` is `7`, every test folds, and the program prints what it printed. `build_test`'s
*solves a call chain deeper than the sweeps' old cap* asserts that 22 levels and 24 converge alike
with no analysis declined. Every other output of slice 4 is byte for byte the same. E2
(`SpecSelfGuard`) and `run/DerivedPartTypedLater` wait for slice 6's executability, as written.
And *Where it runs*' "a module whose `Mod.version` did not change keeps its arrays" is per
statement since slice 4 (*As built 2026-10-22*, below): the rewrite patches nearly every module,
so whole modules were never kept.

*Amended 2026-10-22 (issue #649).* Slice 5's double run against `Pts` survives `Pts`' walker as a
shuffled replay: a safety build of a small program replays fact 3's extracted statements in a
shuffled order and compares every fact with the replay in program order. That is the check
*Determinism* specifies, and what goes is the recording walk and `byUnits`, not the order check.

**As built 2026-10-19 â copy edges, field summaries and load cells inside `Pts`** (issue #464; a
step toward slice 5, not slice 5). A release build of the research dashboard with 64 widgets
allocated tens of GiB and never finished: `Pts` evaluated a spread `{...model, w: v}` as one
constraint that re-walked every source site and every property on every change, found a property
by a linear scan, and built a union it then discarded; a member read `x.p` likewise re-unioned the
property of every site whenever any one of them changed; and `browser-inline` emits one handler
per widget message, each with its own `const $before = $model` copy of the whole model and one
spread of it, so the work was (sites Ã properties Ã spreads) and the sites, properties and spreads
all grow with the program. What `Pts` now does, with the facts the same least fixpoint â every
`emit/release/` golden and release run hash byte for byte, the safety build's shuffled-order check
on every program of the corpus â is *The worklist*'s difference propagation, built on the existing
constraint walk:

- **Copy edges** (`Pts.copy`, the `copy` constraint): a binding, a call argument or a `return`
  whose value is a name no guard narrows is an edge between the two vars, and what joins the
  source later joins the target as it arrives â one batch of new sites at a time, on a worklist,
  never by recursion (`joinNow`); a var's set is still an immutable sorted slice, now one new slice
  per batch in the fixpoint's arena, not one per site in the compilation's.
- **Field summaries** (`Pts.Summary`, the `spread` constraint): a spread of a name copies through
  the var's summary, one var per property fed by copy edges from the sites' property vars; a var
  that is a copy of another takes the other's summary through one edge per property, since a
  summary is a homomorphism of the union. Every record update of one record shares one summary. A
  capped var that is `top` has a dead summary: its sites are escaped, nothing more is folded. An
  uncapped `top` var still holds its sites, and a spread of it folds them.
- **Load cells** (`Pts.Load`, the `load` constraint): a member read's value is its own var, fed by
  one copy edge from the property's var of each site, shared by every read of one property of
  one var (by node for any other object expression) and read by the reference sweep too. The var
  is never `top` by `max_sites` and keeps its sites beside `top`, as the value a read gives does.
  The sites it linked through an object that later escaped are kept and are escaped, so the
  order check compares a `top` value on its live sites alone, and a `top` local the same way.
  *Amended 2026-10-20.* A local bound to that read is uncapped too (`VSet.limited` still applies
  `max_sites`). Joining the cell's `top` into a capped local escaped every object the read named,
  so an unread field of a variant payload stayed in the literal. The slot is shared with `Result`'s
  `Err` list and the read is `top`.   The binding keeps the objects beside `top`. The read sets `top`
  before the set can grow. The cap calls `makeTop`, which returns only when the var is already
  `top` and holds no sites. A member binding that is already `top` still has its sites escaped,
  the other three flags of `top` set, its summary marked dead, and `top` joined into every
  successor and every load cell of those sites (`escapeSite`). A use that cannot name a field
  still escapes the sites. Fact 3 does not
  split those payloads by the tag test, so a field read on any variant the binding may hold stays
  on each of them (issue #507). A later assignment joins the same local, and a field read after
  that assignment stays on the new record. Passing the binding to a host function escapes it the
  same way, and the field that function reads stays. Fixtures: `emit/release/app/PayloadUnreadField`,
  `run/PayloadUnreadField`, `emit/release/app/PayloadReassign`, `run/PayloadReassign`,
  `run/PayloadPassed`.
- Properties are sorted by id and found by binary search (`Pts.prop`).

Measured, ReleaseFast, `--release --no-cache --jobs=1`, the research `unique-components`
dashboard and its standalone spread reduction, dagon: N=16 0.55 â **0.12 s**; the reduction at
N=64 1.35 â **0.09 s**; N=64 itself, which no compiler had finished (killed at 21 GiB, then at
3.3 GiB under a 6 GiB guard), **6.5 s at 1.1 GiB**. The corpus case
`emit/release/inline/SpreadWide` (48 children) cost 32 070M instructions before and 2 051M after.
**What is left is the degenerate case, not this machinery**: in that program `Result.withDefault`
is called with every widget's model and is not inlined (its first argument is a call, not an
atom), so every widget model flows into one var; the host JSON value then makes every one of them
escape, yet before they escape 448 arm parameters each hold the merged set of 270 sites with 78
property names, and summaries of them are folded one by one. Under this section's cap of 48 sites
(`max_sites`, today the interim 1 000 that #442 tracks) the same build takes **0.49 s at 219 MiB**
with byte-identical output, and `specialise` is then the structural passes (`pushChildren`,
`srList`, `placeExpr`, `inlineScan`), not fact 3. The cap, context sensitivity for small pure
helpers, or binding a non-atom argument to a local so the inliner may inline, are the owner's
decisions (#464).

**As built 2026-10-20 â the set table inside `Pts`** (issue #496, part of #464). The site sets of
*Cells* are now what `Pts` stores: `Pts.Sets` holds every set a var takes and every union and
difference `Pts` makes, once, content-addressed, with ids in solve order that no fact reads. A
var's `sites` is an entry's own storage and a `Val`'s stays a slice, so every reader outside
`Pts` is unchanged and a value read before a join keeps the set it was read as. `joinNow`'s batch
is an entry, and each operation on two ids is made once (`Sets.ops`), so a var that holds what
another held and takes the same batch takes the same grown set with no work; a filter of a set by
a declared key, below, is one more such operation. Measured, ReleaseFast, `--release --no-cache
--jobs=1`, dagon, every output byte-identical: `spec_pts_set_words` on the dashboard N=16
1 764 840 â 89 023, N=64 175.6M â 1.50M, N=64 without `withDefault` 57.7M â 1.25M; peak RSS at
N=64 1.13 GB â 0.96 GB and without `withDefault` 386 MB â 317 MB; time at N=64 about â10% and
otherwise within noise. The words are no longer the cost: what is left of fact 3's time is the
copy edges' worklist, one pending join per var per batch. `emit/release/inline/SpreadArms`
(29 children of six messages) costs 4 537M instructions before and 3 843M after, `SpreadWide`
2 038M â 1 928M.

**As built 2026-10-20 â a member read of a name reads its field summary** (issue #498, part of
#464). A load cell of a name's property (var `v`, property `p`) no longer takes a copy edge from
`p`'s var and from `any` of every site `v` may hold: it takes one from the var of `p` in `v`'s field
summary and one from the summary's `any`, two edges per cell whatever `v` holds. A read of any
other object expression keeps its cell per node, linked per site. What the per-site cell also did
is now a mark on the summary, applied to the sites it folded, to the sites it folds later, and to
the summaries that feed it, whose sites are a subset of `v`'s (`Pts.markRead`, a walk over the
summaries' new `preds`): the read marks `p` read on each site (`Prop.read`), made when the site
lacks it, as `load` made it; a site without the key, or with it uninitialised, sets the mark's
`lacks`, which runs along `succs` and joins `undefined` into the cell; a folded site that escapes
or is no object sets the summary's `escaped` or `unknown`, which make the cell `top`. **A summary
holds only what is asked of it**: every property when a spread reads it whole (`Summary.whole`,
which now carries what `foldSite` did to every site â `all_read` â and passes to the feeding
summaries the same way), and otherwise only the properties a read marked (`Pts.demands`). Without
that, a summary made for a read joined every field of every site and the dashboard N=64 build took
14.1 s against 6.3 s; with it a read of one field of a wide record costs one edge per site in the
one summary, and the marking costs nothing in facts â a read never marks a field it does not read,
so the release build still drops unread fields. A summary's vars are `uncapped`, as a cell's is,
since a summary now feeds reads as well as spreads and a cap there would escape sites no
consumer's own var escapes. The links a summary takes across a copy edge are unchanged, so
*Declared-type filtering of fact 3*'s rule holds as written: where it links no summary, the
target's summary folds its sites one by one and the marks reach them there. Every `emit/release/`
golden and release run hash is byte for byte the same; the safety build's shuffled-order check is
green on the corpus with one change: a site written under an unknown key is not compared on its
per-key `written` flags, which `neverWritten` never reads past `any_written`. A spread copies the
keys its sources have, and the keys of a source that escaped are no fact; a read through a summary
marks a site as it is folded, which in one order is before it escapes and in another after
(`run/MarkupFieldIdentity`). Measured, ReleaseFast, `--release --no-cache --jobs=1`, dagon, every
output byte-identical, before â after: `spec_pts_edges` per fact-3 run on the dashboard N=16
29 196 â 11 519 (7 runs), N=64 4.52M â 4.37M (6 runs), N=64 without `withDefault` 418 837 â 91 818
(6 runs); time and peak RSS N=16 0.15 s / 62 MB â 0.14 s / 61 MB, N=64 6.27 s / 961 MB â 6.05 s /
961 MB, without `withDefault` 1.21 s / 317 MB â 0.82 s / 274 MB. Instructions of the gates' build:
`emit/release/inline/SpreadArms` 3 846M â 2 613M, `SpreadWide` 1 927M â 1 593M, and the new
`MemberReadsWide` (SpreadArms with 34 children) 5 124M â 3 445M. At N=64 with `withDefault` the
edges are the merged sets of the degenerate case the 2026-10-19 note describes, not reads.

#### Declared-type filtering of fact 3

*Specified 2026-10-20 (issue #488, part of #464; the owner's decisions D1 and D2 in its safe form,
`plans/type-directed-points-to.md` Â§2âÂ§3). Normative for that plan's slices 2â4; nothing here is
built. It extends `Pts` as the* As built 2026-10-19 *note describes it (copy edges, field summaries,
load cells, `Pts.joinNow`), and carries over unchanged into the cells of* Building it*'s slice 5.*
Fact 3 is context-insensitive, so a helper every widget calls with its own model
(`Result.withDefault`) holds every model in one parameter and one return, and the merged set travels
from there into every caller's bindings, arms and record updates: the work grows as (callers Ã
sites) at every consumer. The type system already says which of those flows can happen. **A var
whose declared type is closed holds only the sites of that type**, and the filter that says so is
one intersection at the one place sites join a var.

**The representation key.** `Lower` maps each type key of the artifact (Â§3) to the key of what the
value is at run time in a release build. A type of one constructor with one field is its field's
key, with the type's arguments substituted (*A type of one constructor with one field is its field*,
`CtorRep.unboxed`), so a site of `R` held at `Wrap` is held at `R`. `Bool`, the primitives, `Int32`,
strings and a type all of whose constructors are nullary make no site and need no key. Lowering
writes the result into `JsIr.name_key`, filled where a Bir local becomes a name (`Lower.localName`;
`Lift` gives a lifted arm's parameter its local's key), and `JsIr.node_key`, on object, array and
arrow nodes; an arrow's key is its function type's, whose result key is its return's filter. In
`Spec`, `Mod.setNode`, `copyNode` and `foldTo` clear a node's key, `addName` and `freshLocal` make
wild names, and `Copy` keeps the keys of a body only when its declaration's type holds no type
variable. A safety build asserts that a keyed node is still an object, array or arrow when the
filter reads it.

**The wild set** is assembled at the merge, in module order, from every module's artifact, and a key
in it is wild wherever it occurs, as a site's key or as a var's filter:

- **unboxing's boundary set** (*A type of one constructor with one field is its field*): every type
  a live `foreign`'s annotation names, and every closed type a `Js.from` or a `Js.to` is
  instantiated at, transitively through fields, payloads and arguments;
- **every type that crosses into JavaScript at a `Js.from`**, followed through quantifiers: a
  quantifier of a declaration *crosses* when its body instantiates `Js.from` at a type that mentions
  it, or instantiates a crossing quantifier of a callee at one. The checker computes the bit per
  declaration to a fixpoint over the module's own calls and publishes it as a flag of
  `Interface.Quantified` (an `iface_bytes` format bump; dependants see it through the interface
  firewall like any change of a scheme). A module that instantiates a crossing quantifier at a
  closed type lists that type, and the types it holds transitively, in its artifact. `core` and the
  platforms compute and publish the bit although their own keys are wild;
- **the subject type of every `?`** (Â§4, *`?` is a test and a `return`*), whose failure is returned
  unchanged at the enclosing function's result type;
- and, as sites rather than keys, **the one constant object of a nullary constructor of a type with
  parameters** (Â§4, *A nullary constructor is one object*), which is the same object at every
  instantiation.

*Amended 2026-10-20 (issue #489):* **"mentions" means "occurs in the representation".** For a
`Js.from` at type `T`, a quantifier `q` crosses exactly when `q` occurs in what a value of `T` is at
run time: through an alias's expansion, a record's fields, a tuple's elements, a function type's
parameters and result (a closure can hand an `a` out or take one in), and a named type's
constructor payloads, transitively, by the parameters its payloads hold
(`Interface.Type.payload_params`). A phantom parameter does not occur. A `foreign type` holds
nothing JavaScript can reach through it, except `List`, an array of its elements, and `Js.Ref`, a
cell holding one. The closed types the walk meets join the wild set by the same rule. It is
sound because the filter only has to account for objects that reach JavaScript through the cast
and come back at another type. An object of type `a` reaches JavaScript through a value of `T`
only if the representation of `T` holds an `a`, and a phantom `a` holds none. So `Schema e a`,
which is a host value, crosses at neither `e` nor `a`. Every other part of the rule is unchanged,
the propagation through callees' crossing quantifiers included.

**The rule.** Every var of `Pts` has a filter, `allow`. A local's and a parameter's is its name's
`name_key`; a function's return var's is the result key of its arrow's `node_key`; every other var
is wild: a site's property vars, `any`, summaries, load cells, the globals and every name the
compiler made. Every site takes its `node_key` at `siteOf`, and a site of a node with no key is
wild. A var with a closed filter `K` holds only sites whose key is `K` or wild; a wild var holds
everything it did before. **Only the site set is filtered**: `top`, `prim`, `nul` and `undef` pass
unchanged, so a host value is a host value at every type and a var that holds one still turns `top`.
`max_sites` counts what is left after the filter, and a var that goes `top` escapes the sites it
holds, which are all the sites it can hold.

**Where it applies.** In `Pts.joinNow`, where every join, copy and drain lands: the batch of new
sites is intersected with the var's filter before its difference with what the var holds. That is
the whole mechanism. No transfer function, no consumer of a value and no rewrite changes, and no
call needs to know an instantiation.

**Why it keeps the least fixpoint.** A var's filter is fixed before the solve, since keys are
inputs. Intersection with a fixed set is monotone and distributes over union, so every transfer
function followed by it is still monotone and the system has one least fixpoint, which no order of
the worklist changes. Since (S âª Î) â© A = (S â© A) âª (Î â© A), *The worklist*'s difference propagation
is unchanged: filtering each batch is filtering the set. The safety build's shuffled-order check
needs no change, and *Building it*'s slice 5 applies the same intersection to the local and return
cells' site sets.

**Summaries across a filter.** A field summary is linked along a copy edge because Î£(A âª B) = Î£(A) âª
Î£(B), which holds when the target holds every site of the source. Across a filter it does not. **A
copy edge from `u` to `v` links `v`'s summary to `u`'s only when `allow[v]` is wild or equal to
`allow[u]`**; otherwise `v`'s summary is folded from the sites `v` holds, one by one. Linking past a
stricter filter would be sound, since it over-approximates, but it would carry every filtered-out
site's properties into `v`'s summary and undo the filter; folding costs work, not soundness.

**Why it is sound.** Without the filter, fact 3 is a may-analysis of the JavaScript and reads no
type. The filter removes a site `s` from a var `v` only when both keys are closed and differ. That
is sound when no execution puts an object made at `s` in `v`, and beni's type system says so for
checked code. It has no subtyping, a value has one closed type up to aliases, and a value held by a
name of closed type `T` is a `T`. The key is canonical, with aliases expanded and records by their
fields, so equal types have equal keys, and it is a representation key, so it follows unboxing. A
poisoned type (`<error>`) is wild. What remains are the places
where the JavaScript does not follow the types, and each is made wild:

| Where the JavaScript is not the type | What keeps the filter sound |
|---|---|
| `Js.to` and `Js.from`, unchecked and compiled to nothing (`boundary.md` Â§4.2) | the boundary set, plus every type that crosses at a `Js.from` through quantifiers. A `Js.to` needs no rule of its own: it yields either a value JavaScript made, which is `top` and no site, or an object that went in at a `Js.from`, whose key is wild. Nothing relies on "the caller answers for the type" |
| a hand-written sibling, a host call, an escaped function | a host call's arguments escape and its result is `top`; an escaped function's parameters are `top`; a host value is `top`, which is no site and passes every filter. The types a `foreign` names are in the boundary set |
| `Js.Value`, `Js.Ref`, every `foreign type`, the schema `Value` | wild keys |
| type variables and row variables: generic code, extensible records, a polymorphic `let` | wild keys |
| `?` returns its subject at another type | the subject's type is in the wild set |
| a nullary constructor of a parameterised type is one object | its site is wild |
| a type of one constructor with one field is its field | the representation key |
| records are structural and aliases transparent | the canonical key |
| evidence parameters, derived `eq` and `compare`, compiled schema parsers and printers, port codecs, markup lowerings, the entry's call, constructor and placeholder wrappers, tail-call accumulators and scalar views | no Bir local or instruction, so no key: wild |
| `Spec`'s own rewrites: inlined copies, folds, new names | keys cleared on every mutated node, wild new names, `Copy`'s rule |
| `core` and the platforms (`List.js`, `Record.copy`, the fiber runtime) | wild in the first version; what their hand-written files return is `top` |
| `Debug` | refused under `--release`; under the corpus's `--allow-debug` it is `core`, wild |

A source of objects that is not in this table is a defect of this subsection. A wrong key is a
silent miscompile, not a failed check, which is why the table is generous and the fixtures run.

**Fixtures.** `run/` programs, built in both builds and compared with one golden, each of which
miscompiles in the release build if a live flow is filtered away (fact 3 then drops a key it
believes unread or folds a read to `undefined`): `run/UnboxedTypes` extended with an unboxed type
through a generic function; a model taken through `Js.from` and `Js.to` at a type variable in
`tests/platforms/toy` and read back at another closed type; an extensible-record function updating
two record types; a `where a.compare` helper over two records; `Debug.log` of a model under
`--allow-debug`; an alias and its structure on the two sides of a binding; a `?` returning an `Err`
built at `Result E A` from a function answering `Result E B`, whose caller reads the error; a
nullary constructor of a parameterised type of the program at two instantiations; a generic body the
inliner copies into concrete code; and the dashboard's `withDefault (Json.decodeValue s) m` with two
models, one field of which only the host's JSON supplies. Precision:
`emit/release/inline/TypedMerge`, two models through one helper that is not inlined, a field read
only on the first, which the filter lets the second's literal drop; red before, green after. Every
`emit/release/` golden that moves is listed in the PR, and each is smaller or the same size.

**What it does not do.** Records of the same shape share a key, so two widgets whose models have the
same fields still merge. A generic function's own vars still merge: `withDefault`'s parameter and
return hold every caller's model and its host result still makes them escape; what changes is that
the merge stops at the first binder of a closed type, so `replace`'s return holds its own model and
nothing past it sees the others. There is no context sensitivity, no filter at a member read's or a
call's node and none at a site's property var (the plan's slice 5), and `top` keeps its meaning (D4
is not taken). Neither `max_sites` (#442) nor the inliner changes: the owner declined a cap and the
inliner shortcut on 2026-10-20. `core` and the platforms are wild until a later version keys them.

*Amended 2026-10-22 (issue #722): the filter at a site's property var.* **A site's own var of a
property holds only sites of that field's key.** A record's key is canonical, with its fields
ordered, so the key of each field follows from the site's own key. `Emit` lists, for every record
representation, the key of each field under its property id (`Spec.Input.field_keys`), and
`Pts.ownField` gives the var it makes that filter (`Pts.fieldFilter`). The var is wild in three
cases: the site is wild, the field's key is in the wild set, or the field's type is a function,
since an arrow is keyed by what it returns and not by its type. A field shared by a spread
(`shareField`) keeps its wild var, because one shared var serves the fields of every site that
spreads one record. The summary-link rule applies as for any var: a copy into a stricter filter
folds. It is sound for the reason a binder's filter is: a value of a closed record type holds in
each field a value of that field's type, and the type's parts are wild wherever the JavaScript does
not follow the type. **Two key losses went with it.** `Mod.copyNode`, and so `foldTo`, keeps an
allocation's key on the node it moves into, which is now that allocation. And `Copy` keeps every
key, of a node and of a name made afresh: a key is a closed type, the same at every instantiation of
the body it is in, so the rule *Copy keeps the keys of a body only when its declaration's type holds
no type variable* buys nothing. As built it was stricter still, since it read whether the checker
had keyed the declaration, so a declaration with a host-typed parameter (`step : Msg, Model â
Model`, with `Value` inside `Msg`) lost every key. `JsIr.closed_decls` is gone. On the N = 64
dashboard the solve after the structural pass no longer merges every widget's model into each field
of `Main.Model`: it makes 1 623 folds where it made 10 569, 124 973 copies where it made 348 518,
and 18 124 edges where it made 110 018. Its output goes from 104 494 to 103 200 bytes, and the build from 1.102 to 0.997 billion instructions. Fixtures:
`run/TypedFilterField*`, which cover a function field, an unboxed field, a `Js.from`/`Js.to` cast
into a field and the dashboard's `withDefault` into fields; `TypedFilterFieldFunctions` fails when
a function field is filtered. Precision: `emit/release/app/FieldKeyFilter`. There is still no filter
at a member read's or a call's node.

*Amended 2026-10-22 (issue #796): a `const` copy is its source's var.* Take `const x = y` where
`x` is declared nowhere else in its module: no other binding, parameter, loop or catch of the
name, counting every node, live or not (`Pts.aliasSources`). The read of `y` is not narrowed
(`maybeNarrowed`), and `x`'s filter is wild or equal to `y`'s. Then the copy edge would make
`x`'s set exactly `y`'s, flags and all, and nothing else writes `x`. So `localVar` gives `x` the
source's var (`aliasOf`) and makes no var, no edge and no load cell of its own. The facts are
those of the copy edge. On the N = 64 dashboard, after the structural passes first,
`structureFirst` writes the TEA runtime into `main`, and 288 such copies of one local each held
all 349 sites. With the alias, joins go 67 007 â 22 596, edges 17 374 â 13 426, load cells 1 252
â 970, and instructions fall 2.8%. The output does not change.

**In a `browser-tea` page the filter changes nothing, in either direction.** The hosted runtime
keeps the program's model in a `Js.ref` and reads it back with `Js.to`
(`platforms/browser/Browser.beni`, `model = Js.ref (Js.to Js.null)` and `Js.write model (p.update
self (Js.to msg) (Js.read model))`), so the model is already `top` at every `update` call. The
message types cross at a `Js.from` in both platforms (`Js.from msg` in
`platforms/browser-inline/Inline.beni`'s `commands`, `Js.from apply` in `Browser.beni`) and are
wild. The `browser-inline` lowering keeps the model in a JavaScript binding, which is why the filter
applies to the dashboard. Lifting the TEA model out of the `Js.ref` is separate work and not part of
this subsection.

*As built 2026-10-20 (issue #490): the columns,
which nothing reads yet.* Under `--release` (an application or a `--library` build),
`js/RepKeys.zig` merges every module's artifact into one table on the calling thread, after the
boundary is closed and before any module is lowered: nodes in module order, each module's in its
artifact's order, and every node the walk makes after them in the order it meets them. `rep` follows
`CtorRep.unboxed` through the field's written type in its declaring module's `Bir`, the type's
arguments substituted, canonicalised as the checker's keys are (an alias expanded, a record's fields
by text, `{ r | â¦ }` under a closed `r` its whole row, a host type wild); a type that is its own field
through unboxing is wild. **`node_key` is sparse**: `JsIr.node_keys` holds a row (node, key) per
keyed allocation, ascending, since only objects, arrays and arrows carry one, and a dense column was
23 % of `JsIr`'s bytes on `bench/corpus`; `name_key` stays a dense column. **A key is the
representation key itself**, wild for a type that makes no site and for a function type: **an
arrow is keyed by what it returns**, its return var's filter and the one thing its key is for, so a
function with a host-typed parameter and a closed result (a widget's `replace`, taking
`Schema.Value`) still filters its return, and a var of function type holds arrows of every key.
`RepKeys.isWild` answers for the wild set where the filter reads. The wild set is as specified, the
boundary's named types being every named type of constructors without integer tags. **A schema
declaration adds its own `Type` and `Encoded` and its tagged variants' payloads, inline records
included, and nothing else** (their values come from compiled code and `Js.to`); the checker lists
them in the artifact's wild set (checker-v2.md Â§36), and the merge closes them as any wild type. A
record endpoint a written type names is canonicalised from its plan's term, as the checker expands
it. Where the closure would have to go through a type this file cannot canonicalise as the checker
does, every key is wild (`all_wild`), since a key no checker key equals would be a filter that drops
a site of its own type. Three things the specification did not
foresee:

- **A name is a `NameIndex`, not a local.** Lowering numbers a local's disambiguator within its
  top-level declaration, so two declarations' `p$1` are one name. A name keeps a key while every
  local it names has that key, and is wild once two disagree. Fact 3 keys a local's var by its
  top-level statement, so a per-statement key would recover what this loses, if the filter finds it
  matters. A local with no source name is not keyed: its `$p` name is one compiler-made parameters
  take too.
- **A declaration's arrow is keyed by what it returns.** The artifact keys each value declaration by
  its scheme when closed (checker-v2.md Â§36); its arrow takes that scheme's result, or, when a
  parameter makes the scheme wild, the result its annotation writes. Not a suspendable twin, an arrow
  evidence parameters lead, nor any function that may suspend, whose return is a parked fiber. A
  lambda's arrow takes the artifact's `result`. `Copy`'s rule reads the declaration's own key:
  lowering lists the statements of closed declarations in `JsIr.closed_decls`, a statement leaving
  the list when it is rewritten, and `Spec.keepsKeys` keeps a body's keys only from one of these.
- The release peephole's two in-place rewrites clear a key as `Mod.setNode` does, though they run
  after the filter. The safety assertion is `JsIr.nodeKey`, which `Pts.siteOf` calls in a safety
  build.

The hidden `build --rep-keys` prints the table and every key lowering wrote, which
`tests/corpus/repkeys/` pins (an unboxed type, a type that crosses, a lambda, a spread, and a lifted
arm under `browser-inline`), and `cache_test.zig` asserts that a build from a warm cache prints what
a cold one does.

*As built 2026-10-20 (issue #491): the filter.* As specified, in `Pts` alone: `VSet.allow` is set in
`localVar` from the name's key and in `funcSite` from `RepKeys.result` of the arrow's key, `Site.key`
in `siteOf`, both through `Pts.closedKey`, which maps a key in the wild set (or every key, under
`all_wild`) to `wild` once, so the filter compares two keys and never asks the table. `joinNow`
intersects the batch with the var's filter first (`filterSites`, the set table's third cached
operation, keyed by set and key, which answers with the batch's own entry when every site passes),
and a `top` var escapes only the sites that passed. The summary-link rule is `Pts.linksAcross`, read
in `copy`, in `joinNow`'s propagation (the `folded` flag of each successor's batch is the rule, so
a target that does not link folds what arrives), in `summaryOf`'s walk (a summary is made only for
the sources it will link) and in `feedSummary`'s cover. `expectSame` is unchanged. The fixtures are
`emit/release/inline/TypedMerge` (blessed on the base: the second model's literals lose `shown`,
1 127 â 1 119 bytes), `run/UnboxedTypes` extended and nine `run/TypedFilter*` programs, one per
item of *Fixtures*; the model through `Js.from` and `Js.to` is `run/TypedFilterJsCast` with its own
platform, since `tests/platforms/toy` is built only by `external_platform_test`. Two broken builds
showed what they guard: one that ignores the wild set miscompiles `TypedFilterJsCast` and
`TypedFilterQuestion`; one that drops wild sites from a closed var miscompiles those two and
`TypedFilterExtensible`, `TypedFilterInlinedGeneric` and `TypedFilterNullary`. `Alias`, `Compare`,
`DebugLog` and `WithDefault` fail only if two keys of one type differ, which neither break reaches.
No other `emit/release/` golden and no other run hash moved; `bench/corpus` is 19 280 release
brotli bytes before and after. Instructions of one release build (the safety compiler):
`SpreadWide` 1 449M â 1 463M, `SpreadArms` 2 464M â 2 501M, `MemberReadsWide` 3 248M â 3 287M â
the folding a stricter filter asks for, with no fact changed.

**The dashboard does not move.** N=16, N=64 and N=64 without `withDefault` keep their
`spec_pts_edges` (80 632, 26 222 539, 550 910 over 7, 6 and 6 runs), `spec_pts_max_set` (103, 415,
415), output bytes and times (N=64 5.2â5.9 s either way), because nothing in it is keyed:
`build --rep-keys` prints `every key wild`, since `Main` declares schemas and the wild set closes
through their endpoints (`all_wild`). With `all_wild` ignored, as a measurement only, it still does
not move (edges 90 077, 26 355 990, 684 361, more folding and the same output): `Main.Model` and
`step`'s locals and result are keyed, but 12 of the 16 widget models are in the wild set â each
`replace` decodes the model itself with `Json.decodeValue`, whose `a.codec` reaches `Schema`'s
`toHost = Js.from` at `Codec a`, so `a` crosses (D2) â and `replace`'s arrow has no key in any
widget, since its parameter `Schema.Value` is a host type and a function type with one wild part
is wild. The merged set leaves `withDefault` into the property vars of `Main.Model`'s records,
which no filter reads (slice 5). So the filter as specified cannot meet the plan's N=64 target;
what would let it is a choice for the owner, not this slice: keys through schema endpoints, a
function's result key independent of its parameters', a narrower D2 for `Schema`'s own `toHost`,
and slice 5's property filters.

**As built 2026-10-21 â a binding or an argument that is a member read is a copy of its load
cell** (issue #562, part of #464). In the dashboard N=64, 609 field summaries folded 182â202
sites each, one by one. They are not copies of `$model`: those take its summary through one edge
per property, as the 2026-10-19 note says. They are the parameters of the `inline` lowering's
bind wrappers (`const $bind$72 = ($p$73, $p$74) => { Widget$W1$view$$bind$0$0($p$73, $p$74); }`),
which every handler that changes the widget calls with a read of the model
(`$bind$72($elements$8, $model$5.w1)`), and the locals a handler binds to a read of a field
(`const $t$345 = $model$5.w4`, `const $t = $before.w1`). An argument or a binding whose value was
a member read was joined with the read's value. Its var then held the field's records as a set
of its own, every widget's at N=64 (`withDefault` merges them: the 2026-10-19 note's degenerate
case), and its summary folded each record. The sites are records made in `Main`, where the
inliner copied the widgets' arms, so "`Main.Model` sites" in the issue was a misreading. The
parameters go `top` when the host's JSON escapes them, so most of that folding was for summaries
that die. What `Pts` does now, every `emit/release/` golden and release run hash byte for byte
and the safety build's shuffled-order check green on the corpus:

- **A member read nothing narrows is a copy source** (`Pts.copySource`), as a name already was:
  a binding, a call argument or a `return` of it is a copy edge from the read's load cell, found
  as `load` found it (by the object's var and the property for a name, by the node for any other
  object). The cell's var is `uncapped`, so `top` arrives as a flag. A capped target
  (`makeTop`) escapes its sites as the join did, whether the cell turns `top` before the edge is
  made or after, and a member binding (`uncapped`, `limited`) holds the objects beside `top`.
  Every name that copies one read of one property of one var then shares the cell's summary.
- **A summary is not linked across a site's own var, nor across a var two summaries deep**
  (`VSet.site_var`, `VSet.depth`, `Pts.linksAcross`). Once a cell can have a summary, a summary
  can be made of the summary var that a read's cell copies, and linking went on from there: to the
  property's var of every site those summaries folded, and to every var feeding those. The first
  build, which linked them all (and copied assignments), made 7 796 summaries for N=16 against
  388, and N=64 took 3.13 s against 1.89 s. The summary at the summaries' vars now folds the
  sites the field holds, once per field, and every cell and name that copies the field links it.
  Depth stops a regress that the corpus found (`run/UrlParser` ran out of memory): where a
  function passes a field of its parameter back to itself, each summary's var of `next` would
  feed a summary one level deeper, without end. So every summary is of a name's var, a cell, or
  one of their summaries' vars, and there are as many as the program has names, reads and
  properties. Linking or folding is cost alone and no fact.
- **An assignment stays a join.** `$model = $result.a` reads a cell no other read shares, since
  each handler has its own `$result`. As a copy, the model's summary would be linked to 349
  cells' summaries, so each field summary of the model, which the reads of `$model.wK` link,
  would be fed by 349 per-handler field summaries, and each of those folds the field's records
  again. Measured with it, every other rule the same: `spec_pts_edges` at N=16 79 000 â 346 880,
  at N=64 1.36M â 99.7M (28.7 s, 6.1 GB), without `withDefault` 663 029 â 4.48M. Folding each
  record into the model's summary once, as the join does, is the cheap side.
- **Nothing is built for a binding under a guard.** No binding, argument or `return` of the three
  programs is refused a copy because a guard narrows it: the diagnostic counted no fold from one.
  A copy that narrowed would carry `nul` and `undef` only while the guard lives. A guard dies once
  a read between its push and the read goes `top` (`Narrow.kills`), so the edge would have to
  start passing them then. Nothing measured asks for that.
- *Summaries across a filter* holds as written: a cell is wild, so it links only into a wild
  target. `Main$pushed`'s model parameter, keyed `Main.Model`, still folds the 349 records
  `$before`, a wild compiler-made name, passes it.

Measured, ReleaseFast, `--release --no-cache --jobs=1`, dagon, median of five, every output
byte-identical, before â after: `spec_pts_edges` (over 7, 6 and 6 runs) on the dashboard N=16
89 482 â 79 000, N=64 7.54M â 1.36M, N=64 without `withDefault` 680 243 â 663 029; time and peak
RSS N=16 0.09 s / 56 MB either way, N=64 2.03 s / 623 MB â **0.69 s / 247 MB**, without
`withDefault` 0.54 s / 198 MB â 0.52 s / 198 MB. Instructions of the gates' build: the new
`emit/release/inline/MergedChildren` (14 child modules of their own fields, merged by
`Maybe.withDefault`) 5 077M â 3 417M; `SpreadWide` 1 470M â 1 486M, `SpreadArms` 2 508M â
2 536M and `MemberReadsWide` 3 294M â 3 339M, which bind reads of seven records each, where a
chain of linked summaries costs a little more than folding seven sites.

**As built 2026-10-21 â a spread target's untouched field shares one var** (issue #564, part of
#464). A record update `{...$before, wK: v}` gave its site a var per field, fed by one copy edge
from the spread's summary var of that field, and every summary that folded the site took one
edge per field from each. Those fields hold nothing but the summary's set, so `Pts` now keeps
them in one var (copy equivalence, as in Hardekopf and Lin's HVN): a property of a site is in
one of three states (`Pts.Prop`).

- **No var.** A property nothing has written (one a read made) holds nothing and has no var.
  What it would have fed â a summary that folds the site, a load cell that reads it â is listed
  on the property (`Prop.outs`, `copyField`), with no edge.
- **Shared.** A property that a spread of a name writes and nothing else does, and that the
  literal does not write, takes the shared var of its summary var `x` (`spreadSummary`,
  `shareField`). The issue named the wrong source: in `browser-inline` every handler spreads
  its own `const $before = $model`, so the 349 updates spread 349 summaries and no two of them
  have the same `x`. Each such summary is linked to the model's, so its var of a property has
  one source, the model summary's var of it, and holds what that var holds. The field shares the
  var of the root of that chain of copies (`VSet.shared`), and the field is listed on every var
  in the chain (`VSet.sharers`). The shared var is a site's own var (`site_var`, capped, depth
  0, wild), so it holds what each field's own var held, `top` and `max_sites` included, and links
  no summary (`linksAcross`).
- **Own.** A write of anything else gives the property a var of its own (`ownField`): a
  literal's key, `write`, a non-name spread, a second spread from another var, an array's
  elements, or a var in its chain gaining a second source (`unshare`, called from `copy`). The
  new var is fed by `x` and feeds everything the property listed, and the constraints that read
  the property through the site are evaluated again (`wakeReaders`). The shared var keeps the
  edges it made. They carry a subset of what the new var carries, except when the new var goes
  `top` and the shared one does not. Then a `top` consumer also holds the escaped sites the
  shared var still passes on, which *an escaped site is â¤* already makes no fact.

The facts read of a property (`written`, `read`, `init`, its value and so `undefined` for a
key the literal lacks) are kept per site and property as before, so `neverWritten`,
`neverRead`, `keyUnread` and `expectSame` read them unchanged. `expectSame` takes a property
with no var as â¥. Every `emit/release/` golden and release run hash is byte for byte the same,
and the safety build's shuffled-order check is green on the corpus. Measured, ReleaseFast,
`--release --no-cache --jobs=1`, dagon, median of five, every output byte-identical, before â
after: `spec_pts_edges` (7, 6 and 6 runs) on the dashboard N=16 79 000 â 52 747, N=64 1.36M â
0.51M, N=64 without `withDefault` 663 029 â 269 424 (first run: 59.6k vars and 102k edges â
41.9k and 49.4k). `specialise` 64 â 56 ms, 561 â 370 ms and 411 â 288 ms. Time and peak RSS
N=16 0.09 s / 55 MB either way, N=64 0.65 s / 248 MB â **0.45 s / 209 MB**, without
`withDefault` 0.50 s / 198 MB â **0.37 s / 181 MB**. Instructions of the gates' build: the
new `emit/release/inline/SpreadCopies` (SpreadArms with 42 children) 4 751M â 4 103M,
`SpreadArms` 2 537M â 2 237M, `MemberReadsWide` 3 336M â 2 925M, `MergedChildren` 3 417M â
3 122M and `SpreadWide` 1 484M â 1 370M. The first build looked each property up by id at every
copy, which the self-hosted backend does not inline, and it put `MergedChildren` up 3%.
Passing the property's index removed that. What is left of these edges is the links themselves:
each handler's summary of `$before` still has a var per property, fed by the model's, which
carries the model's sets once per handler (about 22k of the 49k edges of a `nowd` run). A
summary that is a copy of another's would remove them. That is a separate change.

**As built 2026-10-21 â a var that copies one var has that var's summary** (issue #568, part
of #464). Each `browser-inline` handler's `const $before = $model` had a field summary of its
own, linked to the model's, with one var per property it was asked for, each fed by one edge
from the model summary's and holding what that one holds: 349 such copies at N=64. The summary
of a var with one source and nothing of its own is the source's, Î£ of a union of one, so `Pts`
no longer makes it (`Pts.aliasSummary`, the same move #564 made for a spread target's fields,
one level up). A var shares its source `u`'s summary when it has exactly one copy edge in, the
edge links summaries (`linksAcross`, so *Summaries across a filter* is the condition here too:
its filter is wild or `u`'s, and it holds every site `u` holds), every site it holds is one `u`
holds, it is not a capped `top` var, `u`'s summary is not dead, and `u` is at its depth, so the
summary's vars link as its own would. `summaryOf` decides such a var after its source, through a
chain of them, and answers the root's summary (`resolve`, cached until the next split); a var
that can never share one (no source, several, or a capped `top`) is given its own when the walk
finds it, so a cycle of copies is fed as before. **It splits into its own summary** (`split`)
when a second copy edge reaches it (`copy`), when sites the edge did not bring join it
(`joinNow`: a join from a constraint, or an edge that does not link), or when it is about to be
`top` (`makeTop`): its own is made as `summaryOf` makes one, linked from each source's and
folding what none of them holds. A var whose summary is about to die splits each var sharing it
first (`splitKids`), since an uncapped copy keeps its sites beside `top` and its summary alive.

**What held the shared summary is listed, not redirected.** A summary id is held in many places
(a site's `summaries`, the summaries' `succs` and `preds`, a constraint's local while it spreads),
so every read through an aliased var is recorded on it as it is made (`Alias`): a load cell of
it (`nameLoad`), a summary it feeds (`linkFrom`), and the constraints that spread it
(`seeAlias`, a dependency list). At a split each of those of the var, and of every var sharing
its summary through it, is applied to the new summary â the cell reads it (`summaryLoad`), the
link is made, and the spread is evaluated again, so that its untouched fields take vars fed by
the new summary (`ownField`) â and each keeps what it took from the old one. That is a subset of
what the new one holds, since the var held every site of its source, so no consumer holds more
than it would have had the var never shared a summary. A forwarding id read on every access
would have put a lookup in every hot path and still needed the spread woken. A mark's load
cell became a list (`Mark.load`, `mark_loads`), since one summary now has the cells of every
var sharing it. Every `emit/release/` golden and release run hash is byte for byte the same,
and the safety build's shuffled-order check is green on the corpus. Measured, ReleaseFast,
`--release --no-cache --jobs=1`, dagon, median of five, every output byte-identical, before â
after: `spec_pts_edges` (7, 6 and 6 runs) on the dashboard N=16 52 747 â 40 509, N=64 509 708
â 360 868, N=64 without `withDefault` 269 424 â 151 994; `specialise` 55 â 50 ms, 369 â 284 ms
and 289 â 229 ms; time and peak RSS N=16 0.08 s / 56 MB â 0.08 s / 55 MB, N=64 0.45 s / 209 MB
â **0.37 s / 179 MB**, without `withDefault` 0.37 s / 181 MB â **0.31 s / 159 MB**. Instructions
of the gates' build: the new `emit/release/inline/SpreadCopiesWide` (SpreadCopies with 46
children) 4 750M â 3 852M, `SpreadCopies` 4 108M â 3 355M, `MemberReadsWide` 2 924M â 2 438M,
`SpreadArms` 2 236M â 1 890M, `MergedChildren` 3 125M â 2 973M and `SpreadWide` 1 370M â
1 202M. The 2026-10-21 note above on a spread target's fields describes the chain of copies
`shareField` follows; with this change a handler's spread reads the model's summary itself, so
the chain is the summary's own var unless a copy has split.

**As built 2026-10-21 â the worklist batches per var, and a value carries its set's id** (issue
#563, part of #464; the profile behind it is `plans/pts-per-run-profile.md`, causes 2 and 3).
*The worklist* specified a queue of cells with their difference, first in, first out; `Pts` kept a
stack of `(var, batch)` pairs, drained inside every join, so each site a constraint made went
through the whole copy graph before the next was made, and a var with k paths to it took k
batches. **A var now waits with one batch** (`VSet.queued`, `q_*`): `join` merges what it joins
into that batch â its flags, the union of its sites, and the part of those sites no linking
edge brought, which the var's field summary folds â and queues the var once; `pending` is a FIFO
of vars. **The queue drains at the end of a constraint's evaluation** (`combine`, `effect`, and a
read's `load` before it reads its cell), at the end of `copy` and `makeTop`, after each
top-level statement, a function declaration's binding and a body's fall-through, and after
`propagate`, the entry's call and the escaping globals; never inside a join, and empty whenever a
sweep asks whether the fixpoint is reached. A read made before the drain registered its
dependency and is woken when the var changes, and every transfer is monotone, so the order is
one more fair order and the fixpoint the same. A batch the var holds already â its own set, a
subset of it, flags it has â is no batch (`enqueue`), and a one-site batch is searched for and is
its own difference. **`VSet` and `Val` carry the set's id beside the slice** (`set`, *Cells*'
`set: []SetId`): `view` and `unionOf` hand it on, `setOf` of such a value is the field,
`difference`, `filterSites` and a load cell's `done` work on ids, a one-site set's id is found by
site (`Sets.single`), and `Sets.by_slice`, which hashed a slice's address to recover an id the
caller had held, is gone. A value built from any other slice (`no_set`: a test's, a node's
`ones`) is looked up by its content; ids compare as their sets do, since the table is
content-addressed. Two counters say how much of the worklist is no-op: `spec_pts_joins` (the
batches vars took) and `spec_pts_joins_empty` (those that added nothing). Every `emit/release/`
golden and release run hash is byte for byte the same, and the safety build's shuffled-order check
is green on the corpus. Measured, ReleaseFast, `--release --no-cache --jobs=1`, dagon, median of
five, every output byte-identical, before â after (the before build is master with the two
counters added; 7, 6 and 6 runs): joins N=16 160 661 â 89 024, N=64 1 007 444 â 522 270, N=64
without `withDefault` 737 237 â 479 852, of which empty 67 216 â 22, 463 964 â 42 and 239 827 â
27; `spec_pts_edges` unchanged (40 509, 360 868, 151 994); `specialise` 48 â 46 ms, 281 â 266 ms
and 225 â 204 ms; time and peak RSS N=16 0.07 s / 55 MB â 0.07 s / 56 MB, N=64 0.36 s / 179 MB â
0.35 s / 185 MB, without `withDefault` 0.31 s / 159 MB â **0.29 s / 163 MB** (the queue's fields
make a var 28 bytes larger). The profile's estimate of fact 3 halving was made before #562, #564
and #568 cut the edges by 4.5Ã; on today's master the join machinery is about 15% of the build
without `withDefault` (`drain`, `enqueue`, `unionSets`, `copy`), the structural passes
(`inlineScan`) and `summaryProp`/`propAt` about as much. Instructions of the gates' build:
`emit/release/inline/SpreadCopiesWide` 3 855M â 3 385M, `SpreadCopies` 3 363M â 2 951M,
`MemberReadsWide` 2 440M â 2 168M, `SpreadArms` 1 892M â 1 689M, `MergedChildren` 2 975M â 2 871M,
`SpreadWide` 1 201M â 1 148M, and the new `SpreadCopiesBatched` (51 children) 4 556M, over the
budget, â 3 988M.

**As built 2026-10-21 â a site waits to be folded until the end of the sweep** (issue #565, part
of #464). The issue, written from `plans/pts-per-run-profile.md` before #562, #564, #568 and #563
landed, asked for two things: a batch that makes a var `top` taken before its site batches, and
summaries that link a property only when a reader asks for it. Measured again on master (an
instrumented ReleaseFast build, not committed), both already hold, and neither is where the
waste is. **`top` first holds by construction since #563**: a var waits with one batch, and
`joinNow` applies the batch's `top` before its sites, so a site queued with a `top`, whichever
was joined first, is escaped and never folded. A `makeTop` that reaches a var whose site batch
waits leaves the batch to a `top` var, which escapes what joins it. **Laziness holds since
#500**: a summary holds a property only when a spread reads it whole or a read marked it
(`demands`). The summaries that die are read whole, by spreads. On the dashboard N=64, runs 5
and 6 still make most of the edges (138 080 and 108 719 of 360 868), and 87% and 85% of theirs
end in a summary whose owner var is `top`. Of those, 67 244 and 26 882 are in summaries that
die (a capped owner). The rest, 53 109 and 65 673, are in the live, escaped summaries of
uncapped `top` owners: cells and member bindings that keep their sites beside `top`. Those edges
carry facts (a read through such a value still marks the sites it holds), so they stay. Of the
edges into dead summaries, 3 in each run were made in the same drain as the `top` that killed
the summary, and every other one a drain or more before it: no order of `pending` can save
them. **What changed is when a fold happens.** `joinNow` no longer folds a site that came by no
linking edge into the var's summary there and then. It queues it (`Pts.folds`), and
`foldWaiting` folds every queued site at the end of the sweep, after the constraints that wait,
the escaping globals, the entry's call and `propagate`. It does so inside one drain, as the
fold at the join was, so that what the folds' copy edges join is one batch per var.
`feedSummary`'s folds, made when a summary is created, stay immediate: deferred too, they tripled
the edges of N=64's first three runs. A fold that waits is one more step of a fair order, and the
sweep asks whether the fixpoint is reached only after it, so the least fixpoint is the same. Every
`emit/release/` golden and release run hash is byte for byte the same, `zig build
test-run-hashes` changes nothing, and the safety build's shuffled-order check is green on the
corpus. Measured, ReleaseFast, `--release --no-cache --jobs=1`, dagon, median of seven, every
output byte-identical, before â after: `spec_pts_edges` per run on N=64 29 984, 28 764, 28 764,
26 557, 138 080, 108 719 â 29 995, 28 775, 28 775, 26 614, 83 351, 87 002 (360 868 â 284 512;
the edges into dead summaries in runs 5 and 6 94 126 â 22 272); N=64 without `withDefault`
151 994 â 131 968; N=16 40 509 either way. `spec_pts_joins` 89 024 â 83 336, 522 270 â 493 331
and 479 852 â 462 748. `specialise` 49.7 â 47.3 ms, 274.8 â 248.7 ms and 212.8 â 207.2 ms; time
and peak RSS N=16 0.08 s / 56 MB â 0.07 s / 56 MB, N=64 0.36 s / 185 MB â **0.33 s / 179 MB**,
without `withDefault` 0.30 s / 163 MB â 0.29 s / 163 MB. The issue's estimate (N=64 from 2 s to
0.55 s with #562) was met before this change by #562, #564 and #568. Instructions of the gates'
build move by under 1%: `SpreadCopiesBatched` 3 987M â 3 970M, `SpreadCopiesWide` 3 385M â
3 371M, `SpreadCopies` 2 951M â 2 938M, `MemberReadsWide` 2 169M â 2 156M, `SpreadArms` 1 689M â
1 680M, `MergedChildren` 2 871M â 2 880M. No corpus case crosses the budget either way, so none
was added: the edges saved are those of summaries that die after they folded, which the
dashboard's escaped JSON makes and no corpus case does at a size that matters. The first build
drained after each fold, outside a drain, so each copy edge's join was a batch of its own; it put
the inline cases up 1â2%.

**As built 2026-10-21 â an analysis keeps fact 3 when nothing it reads changed** (issue #575,
part of #499). *Whole-program specialisation*'s rounds solve fact 3 from â¥ at every analysis,
and the worklist note's *rounds still start from â¥* is why: a rewrite takes constraints away.
A rewrite that takes none away and adds none leaves the least fixpoint where it was, so the
analysis after it keeps the last solve's state (`Pts`' vars, sites, cells, summaries and per-node
values) and solves nothing; the sweeps of facts 1, 2, 4 and 5 run as before. The rule is exact
by construction, and conservative:

- **Every change asks for a solve** (`Mod.fact3`). `Mod.changed` and `Mod.namesChanged` set the
  flag, so every rewrite, prune and structural pass that writes a node, a list, a parameter list,
  a module body or a name does: an object, array or arrow, a call, a member read or write, a
  binding or assignment, a `return`, a dropped parameter and its arguments, a pruned declaration,
  an `import` trimmed. The analysis keeps the state only when no module set the flag since the
  last solve and no module grew a node or a name (`Spec.fact3Kept`), the solve reached its
  fixpoint, and definite initialisation was not capped.
- **One write does not** (`Spec.fact3Neutral`): an identifier written as a number, a string,
  `true` or `false` (`patchLiteral`), when fact 3's value of the read was the primitive alone (no
  site, not `top`, not `null` or `undefined`), the read is not the object of another read, the
  string is not `__proto__`, and lowering keyed no type on the node. Fact 3 makes of the literal
  what it made of the read; a guard takes only `null` and `undefined` off a read, so none on that
  name narrowed anything; and what else a read of a name gives fact 3 (a copy edge where a join
  would do, a dependency) is cost, not a fact. A folded test is not neutral: an `if` that keeps
  one arm drops the other's constraints, and the fold of a guard's test drops the guard.
- **Checked.** A safety build solves again whenever an analysis of a program of at most 1 500
  nodes keeps the state, and every fact of that solve must be the kept one's, each site with the
  same number (`Pts.checkKept`, `expectSame`); the build then reads the kept state, so the
  corpus's outputs are the skip's. With the flag never set, the check stops builds of
  `-Dcorpus=run/Specialize`. `--self-profile`'s `spec_points_to_reused` counts the analyses
  that kept the state; `spec_points_to_runs` still counts the solves.

**What it does not reach: the case #575 measured.** On today's master the rewrite between
analyses 2 and 3 of the dashboard N = 64 writes one identifier as `"root"` â neutral â and drops
the parameter that read it, with the argument of its one call, in the same module; `prune` also
trims an `import`. The dropped parameter asks for the solve, as this rule says it must: the
parameter's var, its position in the site's `params` and the argument's copy edge are fact-3
state, and keeping them is exact only with that state patched. Measured, ReleaseFast, `--release
--no-cache --jobs=1`, dagon, median of five, outputs byte for byte the same, before â after:
`spec_points_to_runs`/`spec_points_to_reused` on N = 16 7/â â 7/0, N = 64 6/â â 6/0, N = 64
without `withDefault` 6/â â 6/0; time 89 â 89 ms, 405 â 407 ms and 339 â 337 ms. Of the 453
`run/` programs built under `--release`, 3 keep a state (`PayloadReassign`, `PayloadPassed`,
`ReleaseReadAcrossWrite`), each at the analysis after `releaseKeeps`, which writes no node. Of 123
analyses inside `rounds` after its first, in a sample of 86 of those programs, none kept it: each
had a change before it that asks for a solve, and a dropped parameter with its calls was the
commonest (in 79), alone in 24. A parameter drop that kept fact 3 would remove the parameter from
its site's `params`, give the dropped arguments' nodes the value of a node no walk reaches, and
drop the parameter's local; that is a separate change, with its own check. `build_test`'s *keeps
fact 3 for an analysis after a change fact 3 does not read* pins the counter on
`run/ReleaseReadAcrossWrite`.

**As built 2026-10-21 â a dropped parameter keeps fact 3** (issue #582, part of #499; this
amends the note above, whose *every change asks for a solve* named a dropped parameter). A
parameter every call passes the same literal, or that nothing reads, goes with its arguments
(`rewrite`, `rewriteCalls`). Fact 3's state takes that drop without a solve when a solve of the
program without the parameter would differ from the kept state only in what the parameter
held, and nothing read that:

- **The parameter** (`Spec.keepDrop`): its var holds no object of the program and is not `top`,
  so no site escaped, was linked or was folded through it; it is the parameter's local of the
  declaration's statement; and no identifier of the statement names it any more (each read was
  written as its literal, `fact3Neutral`, or there was none). `rewrite` drops only a parameter
  declared once in its statement, so no other function shares the local.
- **The arguments** (`Spec.keepArgs`): each dropped one is a literal or a name, a leaf whose
  value only joined the parameter. Anything else â a member read marks its property read, an
  object makes a site â asks for a solve, as before.
- **What changes in the state** (`Spec.applyKeptDrops`, only when the next analysis keeps it,
  so every pass between the rewrite and that analysis reads the state it read before): the
  function site's `params` lose the parameter, its local goes from `locals` and the name cache,
  and each dropped argument's node takes `Val.top_val`, the value `Pts.reset` gives a node no
  walk reaches. The parameter's var stays, fed by edges no fact reads.

The safety build's re-solve and compare (`Pts.checkKept`) holds on every corpus program of at
most 1 500 nodes that keeps a state. **The identifier-to-literal exception now admits a node with
a type key**: fact 3 reads a node's key only where the node makes a site (`siteOf`,
`funcSite`), and `JsIr.nodeKey` asserts a keyed node is an object, an array or an arrow, so an
identifier's row is `wild` if it has one; `Mod.setNode` making it `wild` moves nothing fact 3
reads.

`run/` programs built under `--release`, 81 now keep a state at least once (3 before), 87

**As built 2026-10-21 â fact 3's lookups start where the last one ended** (issue #577, part of
#464; cause 5 of `plans/build-profile-2026-10-21.md`). A frame-pointer profile of the N = 64
dashboard and its no-`withDefault` variant put a third of fact 3 in finding things: a binary
search of a site's properties, a summary's properties or its marks for every property a fold, a
spread or a mark touched (`foldSite`, `markSite`, `spreadSummary`, `markWhole`, `linkNow`), a
list walk or a probe of `edge_set` for every copy (`hasEdge`, 10% of fact 3 at N = 64), and the
generic searches' order function, which a release build calls once per step. Nothing in what
`Pts` stores changed, only how it is found, so every operation happens in the same order as
before: every `emit/release/` golden and release run hash is byte for byte the same, `zig build
test-run-hashes` changes nothing, and `spec_pts_edges`, `spec_pts_joins` and
`spec_pts_set_words` are equal on the three programs. What changed:

- **A walk over one sorted list finds each id in another where the last one was** (`indexAt`,
  `summaryPropAt`, `propAtHint`, `findMarkAt`, `markSiteAt`): the place it expects or the one
  after, and a search only past a gap. A fold of a record of 64 fields searches nothing; the
  answer is always the binary search's, which a unit test checks from every hint.
- **`copy` remembers the last edge each end made or found** (`VCold.last_to`, `last_from`): an
  edge is never taken away, so either is an edge that exists. A fold copies one shared field var
  into the same summary var site after site, and this catches it with no walk. `hasEdge` then
  walks whichever list is shorter by the counts, before the table.
- **A one-site batch past a var's last site is not searched for** (`holdsSite`), and the `u32`
  searches have no order call (`lowerU32`).
- **`VSet` is 64 bytes**: what `linksAcross` and the filter read (`VLink`: `allow`, `site_var`,
  `depth`) and what only an edge, a summary or a shared field reads (`VCold`) are columns of
  their own.

**As built 2026-10-22 â slice 4: facts 1, 2, 4 and 5 by the solver** (issue #637, part of #464).
`Spec.analyse` takes facts 1, 2, 4 and 5 and truthiness from one solve (`Spec.solve`) where the
sweeps were: fact 3 is `Pts`, read as input, and every exec cell is true. What the rewrite reads
is where it was (`memo`, `params`, `prop_lat`, `ret_lat`, `decided_conds`, the `escaped`,
`assigned`, `reads`, `spread_sites` and `arg_effect` columns), so the rewrite and everything after
it are unchanged. Where the code departs from the sections above:

- **A constraint is a node's evaluation** (`Op`, `Extractor`). Extraction is one walk that does
  what a sweep's walk does (`count`, then `evalStmt`) and, in place of each evaluation, emits the
  constraint it would evaluate, in that order: one per node with its `combine`, plus a `store` per
  `o.p = v` and a `ret` per `return` and per body that may run off its end. The *Extraction*
  table's kinds are folded into them: `copy` is a `local` or `param` read, `Ï` is that read's
  flag (the guard is syntactic, `guardNames`), `op` is `unary`, `binary`, `cond` and `template`,
  `alloc` and the literal's keys are `object`, `load` is `member`, and a `call`'s arguments join
  the parameters of the function it names. Each transfer function is the one the walk used
  (`unary`, `binary`, `identity`, `condValue`, `templateValue`, `memberValue`, `callValue`), its
  operands read from cells, so the two agree by construction. A read of a local before its
  declaration in the walk is â¤, as the walk's `m.value` was.
- **Cells.** A node's cell is its occurrence: its own index the first time the walk meets it,
  `nodes + k` for a repeat (a node two parents share), and `memo` keeps the last, as the walk
  left it. Then one cell per tracked parameter. Fields and returns are made as a write or a read
  first reaches them, keyed by (site, property) and (module, function node) (`Solver.dynOf`), and
  a field exists from its first write whatever the value, as `prop_lat`'s entries did, since
  `tagValue` reads existence.
- **The merge** numbers cells and constraints by prefix sums in module order, sums every module's
  counts into `reads`, `escaped` and `assigned`, escapes a tracked function called with another
  arity, writes every value fixed for the solve (literals interned in module order, names'
  `globalValue`, a node's kind), finds each `param` read's cell, asks `effectFree` of each tracked
  call's arguments (`arg_effect`) and marks spreads; then the parameters' readers index. A
  module's own readers index is built with its extraction (`Extract.rd`).
- **The worklist** is one first pass over every constraint in module and walk order, then a
  first-in-first-out queue of the constraints the pass has passed whose reads changed. A field's
  and a return's readers are registered as they read them. The work budget is the specified one
  (64 evaluations per constraint and cell, `spec_solve_budget_hit`); no corpus program reaches it.
- **The rewrite's dependency lists are the solve's**: `g_deps` from each statement's reads of
  names, `site_deps` from `readsSite` as the transfers call it, `w_dirty` empty. The rewrite still
  walks a statement again (`walkTop`) when a patch before it changed what it reads; that, `stale`
  and the rounds go in slice 6.
- **Extraction is kept per statement, not per module.** Measured on the dashboard, nearly every
  module changed between analyses: the rewrite and `prune` changed modules wholesale. Their
  changes are now made in the statement they touch (`within`), a new list of statements counts as
  no change to any statement's nodes (`Mod.bodyChanged`, `Mod.keptNodes`), and an extraction
  copies the constraints of each statement whose nodes stand (`Extractor.reuse`). On N = 64, 1 561
  of 3 684 statement extractions are copies. The statements that change are the large ones (each
  widget's handlers), so the time saved is small.
- **Memory.** An extraction keeps 9 bytes a constraint (the kind and a flag in one byte, a cell or
  node, an operand) and the pool, in an arena of the module's own. A solve's columns live in an
  arena of their own (`Spec.solve_tmp`, emptied with `.keep_all`): in `Pts.tmp` they piled up
  across the analyses that keep fact 3. Extraction runs on the emit workers, as many as its nodes
  call for (`nodes_per_extractor`): one thread per module kept a scratch of the largest module in
  each worker, and TodoMVC's safety build peaked 13% higher at 32 threads.
- **Checked.** In a safety build of a program of at most `max_solve_checked_nodes` (1 500) nodes,
  the sweeps run first (`checkedSweeps`), then the solver, which must agree on every node's value,
  every parameter, field, return and decided conditional, and on the `escaped`, `assigned`,
  `reads`, `spread_sites` and `arg_effect` columns; the panic names the node. A statement's copied
  constraints are checked against a fresh extraction on the same programs (`Extract.expectSame`).
  Both checks passed on the whole corpus run with no node limit (and no instruction budget), as a
  measurement.
