**Slice 4 alone is slower, not faster.** At N = 64 and one thread the solve is about 4.4 ms of extraction,
1.4 ms of merge and 6 ms of solving (one timed run), where the sweeps took 10.1 ms in all: the walk
the sweeps made once per analysis is now an extraction and an evaluation, and the rewrite still
re-extracts the large statements at every analysis. The solve itself is about one walk's worth of
transfers (0.85 evaluations per constraint), since every transfer reads fact 3 as the walk did.
What pays is slice 6: one solve per structural pass in place of 4 to 6 analyses.
`spec_solve_extracted`, `spec_solve_kept`, `spec_solve_stmts_walked`, `spec_solve_stmts_kept`,
`spec_solve_constraints`, `spec_solve_evaluations` and `spec_solve_budget_hit` count it.
`check/rules_test`'s scan of `src/js` now searches a file for a bit's name before its lines: it
read every line five times and reached its instruction budget as `Spec.zig` grew.

*Added 2026-10-22, the same issue â the sweeps go.* `sweeps`, `walkAll`, `checkedSweeps`,
`checkedSolve`, `count_logs` and `max_sweeps` are deleted, with the check against them and the
`spec_sweeps` and `spec_analyses_declined` counters: no analysis is declined any more. The
rewrite's per-statement walk (`walkTop`, `evalStmt`, `combine`) stays for its walks of statements
a patch made stale, until slice 6. Its count of a statement (`countTop`) now walks the statement
each time, where `count_logs` replayed a count kept while the module's version stood; the
analysis's counts are the extraction's. The check of copied statement constraints against a fresh
extraction stays (`max_solve_checked_nodes`). Outputs are byte for byte as with the check. In
instructions of the ReleaseSafe compiler against the solver with the check: TodoMVC 1 385M â
1 394M, the 16 400 arms 2 892M â 2 918M (the rewrite's counts), the 100 000 lines 15 761M â
15 704M; ReleaseFast times and peak RSS within noise.

**As built 2026-10-22 â slice 5, part 1: `prop_lat`, `ret_lat` and `decided_conds` go** (issue
#649). What facts 4 and 5 know of a property is a column of fact 3's own cell of it
(`Pts.Prop.lat`, with `lat_made` for "a write reached it" and `lat_readers` for the solver's
readers), and what a function returns is one of its site (`Pts.Site.ret_lat`). The two maps and
the solver's own table of fields and returns are gone. A write to a property fact 3 has no `Prop`
for has nowhere to go and needs none: `propValue` and `tagValue` find the `Prop` before they read
the field. Likewise no call reads the return of a function fact 3 made no site for. The cells
start again from â¥ at every solve, since fact 3's state may be the last analysis's
(`fact3Kept`). A conditional fact 5 decides is read off the final values when the rewrite patches
it (`decidedBranch`, the test of `nullTestTaken` on `memo`), which is what the map recorded at the
last evaluation. Outputs are byte for byte the same. Measured as in slice 4, before â after
(slice 4 with its sweeps gone): `specialise` on the dashboard N = 16 24.1 â 24.1 ms, N = 64
85.9 â 82.4 ms, without `withDefault` 72.0 â 71.6 ms, peak RSS within 1%; ReleaseSafe
instructions TodoMVC 1 394M â 1 400M, the 16 400 arms 2 918M â 2 908M, the 100 000 lines
15 704M â 15 642M (peak RSS 339 â 334 MB).

**As built 2026-10-22 â slice 5, part 2: fact 3's constraints from the extraction** (issue #649).
`Pts`' first sweep by constraints no longer walks the program to record its constraints
(`walkStatements` with `recording`). Each module's are extracted from its IR (`PtsExtract`,
`PtsExtractor`) and replayed (`Pts.replayWalk`). The extraction follows the recording walk's own
order, which is not the solver's: an assignment's value comes before its target's object, and a
`try`'s `catch` before its `finally`. It also follows the walk's flow-sensitive guards exactly. A
read's candidate guards are the ones in view whose chain it reads and that no unconditional kill
(a call, a `new`, a `yield`, a declaration, an assignment, a loop's turn, a `try`'s part) has
killed. Each carries its kill list, the reads through an object between its push and this read,
and a read through a constant `top` object kills outright. Beside the constraints the extraction
keeps the script of what the walk did between them, in its order. That is: a function's site and,
for a declaration, its name holding it; a body's begin and end, with `undefined` returned when it
may run off its end; the drains; the context a site is made in (`once`); `fresh_fn`; and every
`const x = f(â¦)` (`decl_call`).

**One choice the walk made at run time**, kept as it was. It noted a member read's guards only when
the read's object was not `top` at its first evaluation (`narrowed` returns first otherwise), and
whether a read has a guard decides whether a binding of it is a copy or a join (`copySource`). So
the replay holds each read's candidate guards open (`Cons.narrow_open`) and decides at its first
evaluation under the same test. It links a constraint's inputs and its guards' killers then, as
the walk did.

Replayed in this order, the first sweep makes the sites and vars the walk made, numbered alike, and
reaches the state the walk reached. **Checked**: a safety build of a program of at most 1 500 nodes
runs fact 3 three times. They are the shuffled-order sweeps (`byUnits`, as before), the recording
walk, and the replay, which must equal the walk exactly, every site numbered as it was
(`expectSame` numbered). With the node limit lifted and no instruction budget, the replay equals
the recording walk on every corpus program, as a measurement. The shuffled-order comparison with
the limit lifted fails on four programs on master before this change (`browser/tea/MapLambda` and
three of Conduit's, a site's property entries): issue #657, which this check rests on and which is
not this slice's. A statement's fact-3 constraints read only its own, so one whose nodes stand is
copied into the next extraction with its ids shifted (`PtsExtractor.reuse`), checked against a
fresh walk in the same small programs. Every output is byte for byte the same.
Measured on dagon, master at `b271a9704` before, under a load of 5 to 19 from other work (so the
instructions are the figures to read): instructions of the ReleaseFast compiler on the dashboard
N = 16 340M â 348M, N = 64 1 440M â 1 465M, without `withDefault` 1 326M â 1 350M (+1.7 to
+2.2%); of the ReleaseSafe compiler TodoMVC 1 399M â 1 431M, the 16 400 arms 2 908M â 2 937M, the
100 000 lines 15 645M â 16 009M (+1.0 to +2.3%); peak RSS within 2%. The replay itself costs less
than the recording walk it replaces. What is added is the extraction of the statements that
changed since the last analysis, and copying each run's constraints out of the extractions. What
is left of the walker, the recording path and `byUnits`, goes in the next part with
`max_pts_sweeps`.

**As built 2026-10-22 â slice 5, part 3: `Pts`' walker and `max_pts_sweeps` go** (issue #649).
The first sweep by constraints always replays the extractions (part 2). So the recording walk
(`walkStatements` and the `stmt`, `list`, `branch`, `body` and `expr` it walked with), the guard
and kill bookkeeping it carried at run time (`Guard`, `guards`, `reads`, `kill`, `killRead`, the
recording branch of `narrowed`), `byUnits` (the sweep of everything a safety build compared
against) and the cap of 64 sweeps are gone, with `spec_points_to_declined`, which counted fixpoints

shuffled replay, which with the node limit lifted and no instruction budget passes on the whole
corpus (#657's fix, comparing effective facts, is on master). Every output is byte for byte the
same.

**As built 2026-10-22 â slice 6, part 1: executability** (issue #676). The extraction gives every
constraint the innermost exec cell it lies in: its module's top level, a function body (`func`),
or an arm. An arm is the `then` or `else` of an `if` or `?:`, or the right side of `&&` or `||`.
Its test is the cell of the test's node. `switch` cases, loops and `try` parts share their parent's
cell. The cells, and the indexes from a cell to the constraints it gates, from a cell to the arms
below it and from a test cell to the arms it decides, are built by counting sort with the rest
(`Extract.execs`, `ec`, `ek`, `et`). A statement that is kept is renumbered with its cells, and
the safety build's check of what was kept compares them too. The solver starts with every top
level true. A body starts true when fact 3 made no site for it, or when its site escaped or has
`odd_caller` (`new`, the entry file). It also starts true when its function is held under a key in
`implicit_host_keys` or under a key the pass does not know, which the host may call with no call in
the program. An executable `call` makes true the bodies of the function sites in its callee.
An arm becomes true when its parent is true and its test's truthiness allows it, which is checked
when either changes. A constraint whose cell is false is not evaluated, and a woken one is skipped
until its cell is true. Past the budget, every cell is true. Fact 3 still analyses every body
and both arms; its sets are a superset of what runs, which is sound. Two things follow from the
facts holding only of what runs. **The rewrite's walks join nothing** (`Spec.frozen`): a walk of
a statement already patched reads the solved parameters, fields and returns, and no longer widens
them with what a dead arm passes. **An arm of a `?:` whose test may do something, and is always
truthy or always falsy, is written as `0`** (`writeDead`), because its nodes have no values and
nothing evaluates it. A tag read (`tagValue`) treats a literal with no write, which never ran, as
holding nothing. `SpecSelfGuard` folds `go` as it folds `quiet` (371 â 341 bytes).
`PayloadReassign` loses a dead object with its message (4 791 â 4 683). `SpecDeadArm` is new
(473), and is 558 bytes before this part. No other golden moves. Development output is byte for
byte the same, and 34 `run/` and `browser/` release outputs changed with the same results.
Measured on dagon against master at `2a362f6e7`, load below 3: the measurement programs' outputs
are byte for byte the same. Instructions of the ReleaseFast compiler are N = 16 355M â 365M,
N = 64 1 504M â 1 534M, and without `withDefault` 1 390M â 1 419M (+2 to +3%). `spec_analyses`
is unchanged (5, 4, 4), and the minimum `specialise` (27/135/107 ms â 29/130/98 ms) and wall are
within noise. The ReleaseSafe compiler takes TodoMVC 1 440M â 1 488M, the 16 400 arms 2 958M â
3 117M and the 100 000 lines 16 126M â 16 564M, with peak RSS within 2%. The cost is the exec
cells' extraction and indexes. Parts 2 and 3 remove the rounds this part still runs.

**As built 2026-10-22 â slice 6, part 2a: the names' cells** (issue #676). A whole-program name
whose value is its initialiser's now reads that node's cell (`Spec.nameInit`). That is a name's one
`const` or `let` with an initialiser that nothing assigns, other than a function, an arrow, or a
`const` object or array, which stay the name itself (`nameLat`). Before, a read of such a name was
`globalValue`, a function of the initialiser's tag alone, so a module-level constant was a literal
only as written. The rounds and the rewrite's `stale` walks carried what its initialiser was found
to be over to its readers, one round later. Now the solve does: a `global` read of a name with a
cell is a reader of that cell, woken with it. The readers are kept per name in an index built by
counting sort, and a bitset with a sorted list maps a cell to its name. A read before the
declaration throws, so it has no value at all. The value the solve found is kept for the
rewrite's walks (`name_solved`). Golden moves: `tea/HttpSendUntracked` 12 340 â 12 322 and
`tea/HttpSendTracked` 17 867 â 17 861, an alias of a module constant gone. `SchemaWorkers` (5 722)
and `app/ValidatorWorker` (1 324) keep their size, with a declaration ordered and named apart.
Over the `run/` corpus's release builds, 51 programs shrink and none grows: 1 988 794 â 1 987 146
bytes against master with part 1. TodoMVC is 23 620 â 23 614 bytes, and 8 762 â 8 771 after brotli
from the names it renamed. Instructions of the ReleaseSafe compiler against master
(`2a362f6e7`) are TodoMVC 1 440M â 1 492M, the 16 400 arms 2 958M â 3 121M and the 100 000 lines
16 126M â 16 605M. Of the ReleaseFast compiler they are N = 16 355M â 366M, N = 64 1 504M â 1 536M
and without `withDefault` 1 390M â 1 422M. Part 1 accounts for nearly all of it. Peak RSS is
within 2%, and the measurement programs other than TodoMVC are byte for byte the same.

**As built 2026-10-22 â slice 6, part 2b: one rewrite per solve** (issue #676). `rounds` is one
solve, one rewrite and `prune`. `max_rounds`, the rewrite's `stale` re-walks (and `Spec.frozen`),
`now_literal`, `deadReads`, and `releaseKeeps` with the solve after it are gone. `spec_analyses` is
`spec_solves` (one per structural pass), and `spec_rounds_capped` is gone. The rewrite reads only
the final facts, and every step below reads the program as the patch leaves it:
- **A statement is patched until its own counts allow nothing more.** This happens only when the
  patch refused a local read for its count (`refused_local`). A read of a module constant the
  substitution rule refused is written once the whole patch has folded enough of its reads away
  (`declined`, `folded_reads`). Dropped arguments, dead bindings and dropped keys count off what
  they read (`noteGone`).
- **Liveness of local bindings** (`liveness`). A `const` or `let`, declared once and assigned
  nowhere, is dead when every read of it stands in a dead binding's initialiser. It must also not
  be kept by lowering (`releaseKept` releases what does nothing by the facts), not be under a
  qualified name, and have an initialiser that does nothing (`effectFree`). A dead binding goes
  from its list. Lowering keeps only bindings it knew might go unread, so a `?` temporary whose
  reads the patch folded keeps its effect: `run/QuestionOrder` pins that.
- **Parameters.** A parameter literal by the solve goes by the counts the patch starts from. One
  that nothing live reads goes when no argument for it does anything, as the patch left the
  arguments (`argEffects`). Drops iterate inside the rewrite: a function that lost a parameter is
  numbered anew, and the statements the drops changed are counted again (`applyDrops`,
  `unreadParams`).
- **Keys** a fact-3 read reached, but that no read the patch left reaches, go (`dropUnreadKeys`,
  `liveKeys`), before the parameter decisions and again after `prune`.
- **Reachability before the solve** (`liveStatements`, from the extraction's per-statement name
  lists). A declaration that `prune` may drop and that nothing live refers to has its statement's
  exec cell false: its constraints, its bodies, its reads and its assignments are not in the solve.
  Every statement has an exec cell of its own.
- **A field of an object literal that does nothing when made** is read as a chain: `{a: 1}.a` is
  `1`.
- **`self_assign` and `iife` run in the pass loop**, as one sweep (`tidy`).

### Compact statements

### Compact statements

*Added 2026-10-02 (`plans/browser-decisions.md` R47-3: each step of the runtime's port must print
as the hand-written JavaScript it replaces).* Shapes a release build writes more shortly than the
lowering does, each exact wherever it applies, none in a development build. Each has its golden;
the whole `run/` and `browser/` corpus's release pass is their differential test.

1. **No `else` after an arm that jumps, and no braces around one statement** (`Print.compactIf`).
   When an `if`'s first arm always ends in a jump â its last printed statement is a `return`, a
   `throw`, a `break` or a `continue`, or an `if` both of whose arms do â the second arm is not an
   `else` but the statements after the `if`: `if(d===e)return;d=f;` for
   `if(d===e){return null;}else{d=f;}`. When only the second arm jumps, the test is negated (by
   `negatedTest`: `===` for `!==`, the operand for `!x`) and the arms swap. A body of one statement
   that JavaScript allows there â a `return`, `throw`, `break`, `continue`, expression or
   assignment, or an `if` with no `else` after it â has no braces, and an `else` whose body is an
   `if` is `else if`. What "always jumps" reads is what is PRINTED: a `continue` that ends a loop
   body and a `return` that a function whose result nothing reads writes as its value (*A result
   nothing reads*) are not jumps. An arm is not spliced when it declares a name its declaration
   declares twice (the compiler's positional names can repeat; `Opt.Plan.repeated`), nor out of an
   `if` that is itself an unbraced body, which must stay one statement. Fixture:
   `emit/release/core/CompactIf`.
3. **A flag test is its bits** (`Spec.peephole`, on every release module). In a test position â
   an `if`'s or a conditional's test, the operand of `!`, either side of `&&`/`||` in one â
   `(x & k) !== 0` is `x & k` and `(x & k) === 0` is `!(x & k)`: a bitwise operator's value is an
   integer and never `NaN`, so it is truthy exactly when it is not zero. A comparison node referred
   to from anywhere else keeps its `Bool`. Fixture: `emit/release/core/FlagTests`.
   *Amended 2026-10-15* (research 102, Â§6.1 item 7): in the same test positions, **`x && true`
   and `x || false` are `x`** â the literal decides nothing and evaluates nothing, so the operator
   is truthy exactly when `x` is â when neither node is referred to from anywhere else. It is what
   specialisation leaves where it folds `!c.all` to `true` in a compiled schema reader's
   `if (f === c.fail && !c.all)`, and an `||` arm folded to `false`. An operand of `&&`/`||` is a
   test position only when that operator itself is referred to from nowhere else, for this
   rewrite and for the flag test above. Conduit: â136 brotli tea,
   â68 direct. Fixture: `emit/release/app/SchemaReaderTest`.
2. **No result where the result is `()`**: Â§4's *A `()` result is not written*, with its fixture
   `emit/release/core/UnitResults`.
5. **An optional call** (`Print.optionalCall`). Where its value is discarded â an expression
   statement, the end of a function whose result nothing reads, or such a function's concise
   body â `x == null ? <literal> : x(a)` is `x?.(a)`, and `x.m(a)` in its place is `x?.m(a)`
   (tested either way round, and through `!`). `?.` calls exactly when `x` is neither `null` nor
   `undefined`, which is what `==` tests; `===` does not, so a platform writes the test with
   `Js.isNullish`. Fixture: `emit/release/core/StatementShapes`.
8. **A host global is its bare name, and a conditional nothing reads is an `if`.**
   `globalThis.x` is `x` for a host global of `Rename.bare_globals` (`document`, `queueMicrotask`,
   `Error`, â¦): no ordinal of either namespace ever spells one (`Rename.reserved`), and a
   scope-hoisted build keeps `globalThis.` for one a hand-written file binds at its top level as
   written or through a host `import` (`Emit.bareBlocked`; `import process from "node:process"`
   binds `process`, which is therefore not on the list). A conditional whose value is discarded
   and one of whose branches is a literal or a name is an `if` (`Print.discardedValue`):
   `if(c)f()` for `c?f():null`, and a concise body so shaped is a block, `()=>{if(g)j()}`, which is
   no longer. Fixture: `emit/release/core/StatementShapes`.

   *Amended 2026-10-24 (the owner, #936).* `window` is bare only in a build for a chain that
   says it always runs in a page (`"host": "page"`, `boundary.md` §5.2): it is
   `Rename.page_globals`, apart from the list above. Where there is no window, a bare `window`
   throws `ReferenceError` and `globalThis.window` reads `undefined`, so a build for any other
   chain keeps `globalThis.window`; the rule writes a bare name only where both read the same
   value. And `globalThis["x"]` — `Js.global`'s form when its name reaches it as a value, as
   `Listen.on "window"`'s does once its argument is inlined — is `x` on the same terms as
   `globalThis.x`, because the two are one read. Fixtures: `emit/release/inline/PushAndTimer`
   (`f=window`, on `browser-inline`), `emit/release/core/GlobalWindow` (`globalThis.window`, on
   `node`).

4. **A for-each is a `forâ¦of`.** `Js.each xs f` (`boundary.md` Â§4.2) is the statement
   `for (const x of xs) â¦` (JsIr's `for_of`): with a lambda of one parameter that cannot suspend,
   the lambda's body, discarded, is the loop's body and its parameter the loop variable â
   `for(const b of a)b()` â and with any other function the loop calls it. Recognising the
   index-loop shape instead was rejected: `forâ¦of` asks the iterator protocol, which an array-like
   without `Symbol.iterator` does not have, so the rewrite is exact only where the program says it
   iterates. And **a function called once in a discarded position is written there**: the one
   call of a function of the module, its arguments atoms, whose value nothing reads (a `let _ =`, a
   discarded lambda body) is its body discarded in turn (`Lower.discard`), statements or not â
   the extension of *A function called once â¦* that puts the port's `startOne` in `run`'s loop.
   Fixture: `emit/release/core/ForEach`.
6. **A loop whose first statement leaves it is a `while`** (`Print.whileLoop`): an unlabelled
   `for(;;){if(c)<exit>;S}`, `<exit>` a `break` or a `return` that says nothing the end of the
   function does not (the loop ends the function; no value, or one it does not write), and `S`
   one statement, is `while(!c)S`. *Measured*: the wider rule â any `S`, the `return x` written
   after the loop â cost the release corpus 415 brotli bytes (raw â401) against the `for(;;){if(`
   every other loop shares, so it is this narrow. `S` may hold no `break` of its own. Fixture:
   `emit/release/core/WhileLoops`, whose `gather` is research 47's fragment loop,
   `while(a.firstChild!==null)b.appendChild(a.firstChild)`. (*Amended 2026-10-02:* superseded by
   Â§8, *The exit test is the loop's header*, which writes every such loop as a `while` in both
   builds, the exit moved after it, for speed â and which, with the exit taken from either arm,
   is smaller than this narrow rule, not 415 bytes larger.) The runtime port's `template` is one
   function because `Rt.beni` now writes the parse in the cloner, as the hand-written runtime does
   (its cell rewritten step by step), not because of a compiler rule.
7. **`new`, and an `else if` chain as a value.** `Js.construct c [ â¦ ]` is `new c(â¦)`
   (`boundary.md` Â§4.2; JsIr's `new_call`), so an error is `throw new Error(â¦)`. Under `--release`
   a `case` whose value is wanted may have a nested `case` for an arm and still be a conditional
   (`Lower.condChainPossible`): `c?"a":d?"b":"c"`, not a temporary each arm assigns. Fixture:
   `emit/release/core/ThrowError`.
9. **An `if` with nothing left in either arm, whose test only reads, is nothing**
   (`Print.testReadsOnly`; *added 2026-10-02*). Both builds write such an `if` as its test, as a
   statement; a release build writes nothing when the test is a read (a name, a literal, a field
   of one), `!` of such a test, `===` or `!==` of two reads, or `==` of two reads one of which is
   `null` or `undefined` â none of which converts an operand, so none can run code. It is what a
   guard leaves when specialisation folds away what it guarded: `Rt`'s `stop` in a page that runs
   no fiber (`boundary.md` Â§9.8.14, the size pass). Fixture: `emit/release/core/EmptyIfTest`.
10. **What a discarded value does, and no more** (`Print.discardedParts`, `skippedOperand`,
   `flatOperands`; *added 2026-10-23*, #896). A name or a literal evaluates nothing, so a release
   build leaves it out where nothing reads it: an operand of a sequence before its last, a
   sequence's last operand and an object literal's values where the sequence or the literal is
   itself a value nothing reads (an expression statement, the end of a function whose result
   nothing reads), and a whole expression statement that is one. A sequence that is an operand of
   another before its last is written in its place, so its own last operand is before the last
   too. `c.a=4,c;` is `c.a=4;` — a record written in place (`ownership-checker.md` §31.10, *The
   form*) whose value a handler discards — `(d.a=a,d),c=b` is `d.a=a,c=b`, and `({a:K(a,f)});` is
   `K(a,f);`. An object literal with a computed key or a spread is left as it is, and a
   conditional left as the one part is not made an `if` (item 8), which the decision of an outer
   `if`'s braces does not foresee. Fixtures: `emit/release/inline/RootClosures`, `PushAndTimer`,
   `TickInPlace`, `emit/release/tea/HttpSendTracked`. A name the lowering writes is always one it
   declared before the read runs, so reading it never throws (no `ReferenceError`, no read before its
   `let`), and leaving the read out changes nothing a development build would show; that is what
   lets release drop it while it still behaves exactly as development does.

And under all of them:

- **A block's last statement has no `;`** (`Print.closeBlock`) â a `}` ends a statement as a `;`
  does.
- **An `if` both of whose arms return a value is one `return c?a:b`**, nested for an `else if`
  chain, and as a function's whole body a concise arrow, `(a)=>a<0?"minus":a===0?"zero":"plus"`
  (`Print.returnsBoth`). *Measured*: the release corpus â370 brotli, the port's empty page â13, the
  `bench/ui` app **+16** â from its only two such sites, `(a)=>{if(a.$==="Just")return a.a;return""}`
  among them; brotli shares the long form with the hand-written runtime's `if(â¦)return`s. Kept for
  the corpus and the port; the app is still below its size before this work.
- **`x = x op e` is `x op= e`** for a name, an arithmetic or bitwise `op`: both read `x`, then
  `e`, then write.
- **`!(a === b)` is `a !== b`** (and the other way round) anywhere (`Spec.peephole`).
- **A `++` of strings is `+`** (`Lower.stringy`): a `++` the checker did not solve to lists, one
  of whose operands is a string literal, an interpolation or another such `++`, is on strings â
  the two operands have one type â and `Basics.append` of two strings is `+`. With no call of it
  left, the hand-written `append`, mostly its list half, is not written. Fixture:
  `emit/release/app/StringAppend`.
- **`x = x` is not written** (`Print.skipped`): a loop assigns every variable it carries, and one
  an iteration passes unchanged is its own value. Fixture: `emit/release/ListScalarView`.
- **Adjacent `let`s join**, as adjacent `const`s do (Â§9 item 5), and a run of top-level ones keeps
  its newline after each member. Fixture: `emit/release/core/LetRuns`.

Measured on `EmptyPage`: 933 â 924 brotli for the bare globals, â 916 for items 5 and 8; with the
port's `Rt.beni` rewritten for items 5â8 (`isNullish` for the phase, the parse in the cloner, one
guarded `throw new Error`), items 6 and 7 and the shapes above, **884**, against the hand-written
runtime's 978; with `Js.each` for its two index loops and `startOne` written in `run`'s loop, **855**.

*Amended 2026-10-02 (the empty page's study, `bench/minify/empty-page/`, ledger steps 03â06): four
printer and compactor rules that need no whole-program fact, each exact, none in a development
build.*

- **No newline in the emitted half** (`Print.endLine`, `Emit.appendJoined`). Â§9 item 3 kept one
  after every top-level statement, for stack traces that name a declaration by line; the study
  priced it at 13 brotli bytes of the empty page's 838. Every statement the printer writes ends in
  `;` or a block's `}`, so no newline was ever standing in for a semicolon. The one file joins its
  pieces the same way: an emitted module's trailing newline goes, and a hand-written file's goes
  after a `;` only (its last `}` may end an expression that automatic semicolon insertion ends at
  that newline). The file ends with one newline. A declined runtime's `import{run,â¦}fromâ¦` keeps a
  line of its own, which is how `tests/browser/driver.mjs` finds it.
- **A `const` is written `let`** (`Print`), and a run of adjacent declarations joins whatever their
  keywords (Â§9 item 5 joined `const`s and `let`s apart). A `const` the compiler writes is assigned
  nowhere, so the one difference â the `TypeError` an assignment would throw â cannot arise, and a
  file of one keyword compresses better than a file of two (research 41; the study's step 03).
  `for (const x of â¦)` is `for(let x of â¦)`: a fresh binding per iteration either way.
  *Withdrawn at the top level on 2026-10-03* â it was not free at run time; the paragraph after
  this list.
- **A function's trailing parameters that its body never mentions are not written**
  (`Print.namedParams`): `m:()=>{â¦}` for a kind whose body reads neither argument, `p=()=>n` for a
  `view` that ignores its model. The caller still passes them â an argument is evaluated whatever
  the callee does with it â and an emitted function has no `arguments`, so the one difference is
  the function's `length`, which no beni program, core file or runtime reads. A mention is any
  identifier of the name in the body, nested functions and assignment targets included, so a
  shadowing binding keeps the parameter; a body past the walk's budget keeps them all. A derived
  comparison's defaulted depth parameter is never touched.
- **`const` â `let` in a hand-written file is decided over the tokens that are written**
  (`Minify.constToLet`, *Hand-written JavaScript under `--release`*): a unit elimination cut is never
  evaluated, so its `i = â¦` no longer keeps the `const`s of the units that stay. And **the newline
  after a block statement's `}` goes** (`Minify.statementBlocks`): the body of an `if`, `for`,
  `while` or `with` head, of `else`, `try`, `catch (â¦)`, `finally`, `do`, `switch (â¦)`, or of a
  function declaration at the start of a statement ends its statement, so the newline after it is
  never automatic semicolon insertion's. An arrow's or a function expression's body is not one:
  `f=()=>{}`, a newline, `g()` is two statements only because of that newline, and keeps it.

The whole `run/` and `browser/` corpus's release pass is the differential test; fixtures
`emit/release/app/OneLine` (user code: one line, `let`, a callback's unread second parameter) and
every `emit/release/` golden, now one line each; `Minify.zig`'s unit tests for a cut unit's
assignment and for each block kind. Measured (release, brotli, the whole bundle): the empty
`browser` page 802 â **776**, `Tea.sandbox` 809 â **781**, `Tea.element` 1 599 â **1 552**, with
effects 5 839 â **5 758**, the `bench/ui` app 5 998 â **5 941**.

**Amended 2026-10-03: a top-level `const` stays `const`** (`Print.topConstRun`,
`Minify.constToLet`; `plans/core-in-beni.md`, the schema engine). The rule above assumed the keyword
costs nothing at run time, and in V8 it does not hold at a module's top level: a module-level
`const` is folded into the code that reads it, while a `let` is loaded from its slot and checked on
every read, because V8 must assume something reassigns it â and a top-level function is read at
every call. A loop calling a two-line top-level function ran **2.5Ã slower** with the function
written `let` than `const` (Node 24, one process, both modules side by side); inside a function the
keyword changed nothing measurable, a captured `let` included. On `core/Schema`'s engine it was the
failure paths' gap to the hand-written JavaScript: instructions per operation of
`bench/schema-library`'s workloads, all of them warmed first as the bench does, against the
JavaScript engine â parse `wrong_type` 1.026 â **0.999**, `missing_key` 1.029 â **1.019**,
`unknown_key` 1.040 â **0.999**, read `missing_key` 1.072 â **1.000**, every valid path 0.94â1.00.
So the printer writes a top-level run of `const_decl`s `const` and a run of `let_decl`s `let` â a
run is one kind now â and the compactor never rewrites a hand-written file's top-level `const`. A
function's locals keep `let` (written `const` too, the corpus grew 97 brotli bytes more for
nothing). The price is bytes, and the owner's rule is that bytes never buy run time (the
`hand-minify` skill, Â§1.4):
`bench/size.mjs`'s release total 372 717 â **373 337** brotli (+0.17 %), the largest program +31
(`browser-tea` random, 1 987 â 2 018); the floor 202 â 184, `bench/corpus` 19 670 â 19 661 and
the `bench/ui` app 5 675 â 5 669 (a hand-written runtime's top-level `const` now matches the
emitted code around it). The release file's aliases of a sibling's exports (`Emit`, `const a=say`)
are `const` for the same reason. Fixture: `emit/release/app/TopLevelConst`.

**Amended 2026-10-02: the loops a bound loop prints as** (`Print.breakLoop`, `forHead`,
`assignmentValue`; `plans/runtime-in-beni.md`, step 4). Three printing rules, each for shapes the
loops of *A function called once is written where it is called* produce:

- **`for(;;){if(c)break;â¦}` is `while(!c){â¦}`**, and `for(;;){if(c){â¦}else break;â¦}` is
  `while(c){â¦}`: an unlabelled loop whose first statement is an `if` one arm of which is a bare
  `break` and nothing else. Unlike *item 6*'s `return` form, the rest may be any number of
  statements, and may hold other `break`s â in a `while` they leave for the same place. Only loops
  that exit by `break` are touched, so no loop printed before changes.
- **`let i=a;while(c){â¦;i=e}` is `for(let i=a;c;i=e){â¦}`** when the loop prints as such a `while`,
  its body makes no function (a `for` head's `let` is one binding per iteration), no `continue` of
  its own that prints would skip the update, the update is an assignment of `i` among the
  assignments the body ends with and none after it reads `i` nor does it read what they write, and
  nothing after the loop reads `i`. The declaration may be a member of a run of declarations if
  the members after it hold literals only; the run is written without it.
- **`x += 1` is `x++`** and `x -= 1` is `x--` (a `+` with a number literal is a number's), and
  **`!(a == b)` is `a != b`** in a test.

Fixtures: `emit/release/core/BoundLoops`, `emit/release/core/WhileLoops`, every `emit/release/`
golden with a counter, and the `run/` and `browser/` release passes.

**Amended 2026-10-01: an arrow of one parameter is `a=>â¦`** (`Print.arrowParams`;
`plans/core-in-beni.md`, step 1). An arrow whose written parameter list (after *Compact
statements*' trailing-parameter cut) is one name prints it without brackets, as a hand minifier
does â `b=>String(b)`, where it was `(b)=>String(b)`. A `function` declaration, an arrow of no
parameter or of several, and a derived comparison's `$d=0` keep theirs. It came with core's
`String` moving to beni: the hand-written siblings had the short form from `Minify`, so the same
function compiled from beni was two bytes longer. Every `emit/release/` golden with such an arrow
moved; development output does not.

**Amended 2026-10-17: an identifier-named string index is a member** (`Print.dottedKey`). Compact
printing writes `x["key"]` as `x.key` wherever `key` is an identifier name â ECMAScript reads both
as one property access, so nothing a program does can tell. Specialisation leaves
`globalThis["window"]` where the browser platforms ask for a host global, and the schema workers
spell host keys as strings. Development output does not move.

### Reachability after the optimiser

*Added 2026-10-17.* Specialisation's reachability (`Spec.prune`) runs before the per-module
release optimiser (item 1), which drops an unread binding whose initialiser does nothing. The
binding may hold the last mention of a top-level function: a schema context's `inE` field is
`endpointOf(src)`, scalar replacement leaves the read as `const t = endpointOf(src)`, nothing reads
`t`, and the optimiser drops it â but specialisation had already counted the mention, so
`endpointOf` stayed in the file with no caller. In a one-file build (*One scope-hoisted file*)
the emitter therefore walks the program once more after the optimiser (`Emit.pruneOptimised`), as
the printer will write it: a binding the plan drops is skipped, and a single use the plan
substitutes is read as its value. The roots are specialisation's â the names files the pass cannot
see read or call, and the entry's call â and every top-level statement but a declaration whose
initialiser is inert (`Spec.inert`); a name an `export` statement names is kept, and so is a name
declared twice. A declaration nothing reached is dropped from the plan. A multi-file build keeps
what it has: its modules are printed apart, and a name one module exports may be read by a file
the walk does not see. Fixtures: `emit/release/inline/PushAndTimer` (`endpointOf` and a schema
helper go), `emit/release/app/InlineReachable`, `SpecMaybe`, `emit/release/direct/ListScripts`, and
the `run/` and `browser/` release passes, which run every program the walk changed.
## 10. Chunking

**Release output is chunks; development output is not.** Â§9.5 of the design doc settles that with
"two build modes, one graph", and chunking is what makes the second half true. A chunk is a file; a
declaration's chunk is decided by which entry points reach it; and **with one entry point and no
`lazy`, a release build is exactly one file**, which is the degenerate case of everything below and
the part of this section worth the most bytes.

*Decided 2026-10-03 by the owner* (the decisions below supersede the PENDING paragraph that
follows and `plans/m3d-plan.md` Â§6; specification of the open points comes before code):
1. **Two sources of entries.** Static multi-entry â one build, several `main`s, shared code in a
   common chunk â and `lazy`. `boundary.md` Â§5.3's "ONE entry point and ONE platform" becomes "one
   platform, a set of entry points".
2. **`lazy` is a contextual word on an annotated top-level function**, as `where` is
   (`lazy adminPage : Model â Html Msg`); `lazy` stays usable as a name, and a value cannot be
   `lazy`, because a top-level constant is evaluated at load time, where nothing can suspend.
3. **A call to a `lazy` function may suspend**: no new effect type; the effects inference marks its
   callers and the fiber runtime parks on the dynamic `import()`. So it is callable from commands
   and tasks, not from `view`, which renders a loading state meanwhile.
4. **A failed load is a typed error** (rule 9). The declaration carries its real type; a CALL has
   type `Result LoadError r`, where `r` is the declared result. `LoadError` names each documented
   failure of a dynamic import; anything else crashes.
5. **The chunker is this section** â colouring, the main chunk absorbing every colour with `main`,
   merging by promoting entries, synthesised cross-chunk bindings â with the 4 096-byte / 5%
   thresholds provisional until measured on the first large app.
6. **A `--release --library` build is one file**: packages ship as source, so nobody consumes
   per-module compiled output.
7. **Acceptance is stated in entries**: a two-entry program splits and both entries run, and a
   `lazy` function is loaded and called in a page.
8. **Preloading, two forms.** A platform may write `<link rel="modulepreload">` into the page shell
   for chosen chunks (fetch and compile, not evaluate; none by default). And a core task
   `Lazy.preload f : Task LoadError â¤` starts the load from the program â after first render, on
   a link's hover â whose argument must be the NAME of a `lazy` declaration, written directly, so
   the chunk is known statically; anything else is a compile error. Evaluating a beni chunk early is
   always safe: its top level is pure constants.

*Emission sketch* (not normative): the body goes to its own chunk; the main chunk holds a stub that,
once the module has arrived, calls it synchronously (one test, no suspension), and otherwise parks
on `import(chunk).then(ok, fail)`, `fail` mapping exactly the documented failures to `LoadError`
and rethrowing the rest. Chunk names are derived from module and declaration (rule 5).

**Open research before the specification:** (a) how Chrome, Firefox and Safari report a failed
`import()` â network failure, a chunk that throws while evaluating, a parse failure â so `LoadError`
names exactly what each documents; (b) whether a failed module fetch is cached in the module map, so
that retrying the same URL fails without refetching â which decides whether `LoadError`'s network
case can be retried and whether a retry needs a different URL.

**What is PENDING an owner decision, and nothing here quietly assumes an answer.** The `lazy` marker
is specified in `fast-compiler.md` Â§9.5 as rewriting a declaration's type to `Task LoadError a`, and
that section's own block quote says the type is gone. A deferred load is asynchronous, this language
is synchronous and has no effect system yet, and there is therefore **no way to express a deferred
value in the language as it stands**. [`plans/m3d-plan.md`](../../plans/m3d-plan.md) Â§2 is the
argument and Â§6 the decisions: whether `lazy` is a keyword, a contextual word or neither; whether it
waits for `plans/effects-plan.md`'s E1âE3; whether a build may carry more than one entry point. Until
those are taken, this section specifies the chunker and **not** the trigger. Everywhere below, "an
entry" means a declaration in the seed set, and how a declaration gets there is PENDING.

### The colouring

Entry points are **the entry declarations of the build** â today `main`, and whatever Â§6's decisions
add. Each node's colour is the set of entries that reach it; nodes sharing a colour share a chunk.
**"Reaches" is Â§9's walk with more than one seed, over Â§9's graph** â the colouring adds a lattice,
not a second graph. Declaration granularity is proven in four whole-program compilers and Closure's
four safety guards for it are vacuous in a pure language (report 12 Â§3.2).

Mechanically it is Â§9's pass run once per entry and transposed: `Reach.run` already returns two
bitsets per module over input-derived node identities (`src/js/Reach.zig:103-123`), so node *n*'s
colour is the `|E|`-bit vector of which runs marked it, and **Â§9's liveness is the OR of those bits**
â one machine, both answers, no second walk. Colours are **interned**: dart2js measured 401 deferred
imports producing 2.9 million import-sets and a five-gigabyte heap without it, and GWT and Rollup
found the same late. At `|E| â¤ 64` a `u64` key into a hash map is `ImportSetLattice` at a thousandth
of the code; the trie is what is needed past that, and the cost of the walks is `|E| Ã O(nodes)`
against a pass Â§9 measures in microseconds.

**Every colour containing the main entry IS the main chunk.** dart2js's rule and its reason, quoted
in report 12 Â§3.1: code reachable from `main` is loaded "possibly synchronously", so splitting it out
buys a chunk that is always fetched. One consequence is worth stating because it removes a whole
class of bug: **the main chunk has no outgoing cross-chunk edge.**

**The chunk graph is a DAG by construction.** If `d â e` then every entry reaching `d` reaches `e`,
so `colour(e) â colour(d)` and a chunk imports only from chunks whose colour is a strict superset.
Rollup's `CIRCULAR_CHUNK`, Scala.js's `maxExcludedHopCount` and its two-of-three "(unproven)" lemmas
(report 12 Â§3.3) are all repairing a property the colour order gives here for free.

### The merge

A merge pass follows, budgeted by compression rather than by request count: four chunks cost about
6.6% of compressed bytes and sixteen about 18% before any chunk has saved anything (report 12 Â§2.6).

**Folding a chunk is promoting its entry, never moving its declarations.** Moving them breaks the DAG
property, because relocated code still references colours the destination does not contain and the
repair cascades â which is precisely why *"every fixup demotes the atom to leftovers"* in GWT. So: an
entry whose chunk does not repay a split is **added to the main entry's seed set and the colouring is
re-run**, to a fixpoint, candidates considered in canonical entry order. That is dart2js's
`ImportSetTransition` (report 12 Â§4.2) used as the merge mechanism, and it cannot produce a cycle.

**The threshold is provisional and says so.** A candidate chunk is kept iff its private content is at
least **4 096 raw bytes and 5% of the program's raw bytes**. Both numbers are inferred from report
12 Â§2.6's table and dart2js's 1 080-byte empty part, not measured here: report 12's open question 2
â *"the biggest unquantified risk in the chunking plan"* â is that nobody has measured what
declaration-granular colouring produces, and there is still no beni program large enough to say.
Re-derive from `bench/size.mjs` on the first one that is.

### Assembly, and what a chunk file contains

Lowering does not change. A module is lowered to `JsIr` exactly as today and a chunk is assembled
from the result: `JsIr.body` is *"the `import`s first, then one declaration per emitted value, then
one `export`"* (`src/js/JsIr.zig:57-62`), and `import_stmt` and `export_stmt` are their own tags
(`:117`, `:119`), so the assembler **drops them and writes its own**. `Print.print` gains an entry
point that prints a given list of statements into a caller's buffer; it prints `ir.body` today
(`src/js/Print.zig:73-78`).

- **Order within a chunk is module-topological, then `emissionOrder`.** In separate files ESM orders
  the modules; in one file nothing does, and a `const` read before its initialiser is a temporal-dead
  zone `ReferenceError` at load â the failure Â§9's own `run/` fixtures exist to catch. The module
  graph is acyclic and a cross-module reference only exists along an import edge, so the two orders
  compose. Emission order is otherwise unchanged: report 12 Â§2.1 measures up to 7% of compressed
  bytes for keeping related declarations adjacent, and Â§9's namer already spent that.
- **Nothing is renamed by chunk assignment, and that is the whole reason this is cheap.** Â§9's namer
  puts every name that can cross a file in one whole-program namespace, assigned before any chunk
  exists, so a declaration's name does not depend on where it lands. Rollup pays `deconflictChunk.ts`
  (266 lines) for this and Elm's LCI-plus-renaming is what report 12 Â§3.3 identifies as *"Elm's actual
  blocker"*. Confirmed on today's dev output too, where names are `Module$name` and already unique.
- **Cross-chunk bindings are synthesised by the assigner, inside the pass.** Closure is the only
  other system doing declaration-granular chunking with an ES-module mode and the combination is
  broken there because it relocates declarations without emitting the bindings
  (closure-compiler#4264, open); esbuild's `computeCrossChunkDependencies` is the model. By the DAG
  property, every such binding is a static `import` from a less-shared chunk into a more-shared one.

### Where everything else goes

| Thing | Chunk | Why |
|---|---|---|
| the main chunk | **`out/_main.mjs`**, with the platform's `run(main)` call last | it is already the file `Emit.emitEntry` writes, so the artifact path does not move â Â§2's rule 1 renamed it from `out/main.mjs` on 2026-09-21 and chunking inherits the new name, not a second one |
| a colour that is one entry | `out/chunk/<Module>.<name>.mjs` | input-derived and readable: it names the declaration the author marked |
| a colour of two or more | `out/chunk/shared.<i>.mjs`, `i` the colour's index in canonical colour order | input-derived; **no content hash**, so a golden is stable and rule 5 is met by construction |
| a derived `eq` / `compare` | coloured like any other node (`Reach.Kind.derived`) | Â§9 already makes it a node |
| a `$$order` table | its `compare`'s chunk | *"lives and dies with its `compare`"* (Â§9); not a node |
| `eq$prim`, `compare$prim`, `compare$char` | emitted per chunk that wants one | discovered by `Lowerer.needs` during lowering, not nodes (Â§9); three small functions, and duplicating beats a cross-chunk edge |
| an eta-expanded evidence closure | the chunk of the declaration whose site built it | not a node; *"an eta-expansion is built from a site's targets, and the targets are the edges"* (Â§9) |
| a `*.foreign.mjs` sibling | **its own file, unchunked**, at today's path; every chunk using one of its exports imports it | a sibling is copied whole and never parsed (`boundary.md` Â§4). ESM evaluates a module once, so duplicate imports cost specifiers and nothing else. Measured cost of not folding siblings into the bundle: 1 215 brotli bytes on `run/Dictionaries`, where the seven siblings are **54% of compressed output** â left on the table deliberately, because separating two siblings' scopes needs a JavaScript parser |
| `_platform/runtime.foreign.mjs` | its own file, imported by the main chunk | *"copied whole, so it needs no root of its own"* (Â§9) |
| *(amended 2026-09-30)* a sibling, the markup and program runtimes, the derived engine | **in the chunk whose pieces import them**, their top-level names in the whole-program table, unless one must keep a module of its own | the two rows above are superseded for the one-chunk case built in Â§9, *One scope-hoisted file under `--release`*: a lexical pass renames a hand-written file's top-level names without a parser, so separating two siblings' scopes no longer needs one; a file it declines keeps its own file, as those rows say |
| a `--library` build | **one chunk** | a library's callers are not in the build, so there is no entry set to colour by; Â§9 already measures that elimination barely shrinks a library |

### Determinism, M4 and M5

**Determinism needs no new machinery.** Entry order, node identity, colour order and chunk names are
all functions of the file index and source order (CLAUDE.md rule 5), and the colouring's output is a
*set*. `--jobs=1` against `--jobs=8` covers it exactly as it covers Â§9, with `--release` in the
matrix.

**M4 and chunking never meet.** Chunking is release-only and release is not the 15 ms warm path, so
"one edit rewrites one small file" (`src/js/Emit.zig:6-10`) remains true of the mode that promises
it. The cacheable unit is what Â§9 says â per-module edge lists, per-module `JsIr` â and a chunk file
is a concatenation of already-lowered statements. What a release build cannot cache is the name
table: Â§9 promises only that a name is a function of position in `emissionOrder`, so inserting a
declaration shifts every name after it. That is a stated non-guarantee and not a regression.

**M5 needs nothing new either.** Â§11's *"per-file chunks rebased once at join time"* is chunk
assembly: mappings are recorded at print time and rebased by the chunk's running line offset, one
`.map` per chunk file.

### Measurement, acceptance and fixtures

**`bench/size.mjs` cannot see chunking today and must be changed first.** `measureTree` concatenates
every `.mjs` under `out/` and compresses the concatenation (`bench/size.mjs:255-279`), so its
headline `brotli_bytes` is *already* the idealised single-file number. It gains **`split_brotli_bytes`
â the sum of per-file brotli â and `files`**, and chunking's win is the distance between them
closing. Measured today on dev builds: `run/Dictionaries` is 20 files, 11 908 brotli summed against
9 290 concatenated (**â22.0%**, â26.5% once module headers go); hello world is 5 files, 1 152 against
835 (**â27.5%**). Those are the numbers the single-chunk case has to reach.

Acceptance:

1. **A release build of a single-entry program writes one `.mjs` plus siblings and the runtime**, and
   its `split_brotli_bytes` equals its `brotli_bytes`.
2. **Every `run/` fixture passes under `--release` with no `.expected` change**, which Â§9's release
   testing already runs; a chunked build is a third pass over the same corpus, not a new one.
3. **Every `emit/` and dev golden is byte-identical**: chunking is release-only.
4. **The determinism test is green** at `--jobs=1` and `--jobs=8`, twice each, byte-compared, with
   `--release` in the matrix.
5. **Emit throughput stays above Â§13's 5 MB/s.** Assembly is a copy per statement and an interning
   pass over `|E| Ã nodes` bits; what would breach it is a fixpoint per declaration, and none is
   specified.

Fixtures, and the failure each one is about. `emit/release/ChunkSingleFile` â one file, no `import`
of a generated module, sibling imports hoisted, `run(main)` last. `emit/release/ChunkOrder` â a
three-module diamond that throws a temporal-dead-zone `ReferenceError` at load if assembly order is
not module-topological; it is `run/`-shaped rather than golden-shaped for the reason Â§12 gives.
`run/ChunkCrossBinding` and a two-entry `run/` project prove that a shared chunk is imported by both
entries and that both print â **PENDING the multi-entry decision**, which is what gives the colouring
a second seed at all; until then every fixture here exercises the one-colour case, and a pass whose
only test is the degenerate case is a pass that will be wrong the first time it has two.

## 11. Source maps

Fused into the print pass â a mapping recorded at each emit site, never a second traversal â
delta-encoded, per-file chunks rebased once at join time. On by default in dev, off in release.
Positions live in `JsIr` from the start even while maps are off. *Amended 2026-10-15:* "off in
release" is the default, not a limit: `--release --source-maps` writes release maps (Â§11.2).

### 11.1 Development maps (specified and built 2026-10-01)

Pulled forward from M5 by `plans/status-2026-10.md` Milestone 1, item 4: beni is a browser language
first, and debugging emitted JavaScript without a map is the first thing a user of `beni serve`
hits. This subsection is the contract for the **development** build; `--release` writes no map yet
(below). Code: `src/js/SourceMap.zig`, the printer's `mark`/`markName` (`src/js/Print.zig`), and
`Emitter.planMap` (`src/js/Emit.zig`). *Amended 2026-10-15:* Â§11.2 is the contract for a
`--release` build, and it extends this subsection; everything here that Â§11.2 does not change holds
for a release map too.

**One map per emitted module, beside it.** Every `.mjs` a development build lowers from a `.beni`
module â the app's, `_core/`'s and `_platform/`'s alike â gets `<path>.mjs.map` in the same
directory, and the module ends with one line, `//# sourceMappingURL=<basename>.mjs.map`. The URL is
relative, so the output tree is self-contained: `beni serve` serves it as it serves the modules
(`frontend.md` Â§10.4 already types `.map` as `application/json`), and the tree can be moved or
served under any `"base"`. **Not mapped**, each for a stated reason: a hand-written sibling
(`*.foreign.mjs`) and a lowering's runtime are copied byte for byte, so the file the debugger shows
IS the source and an identity map would add a file and say nothing; the entry file (`_main.mjs`)
and the derived-comparison runtime (`_core/_derived.mjs`) were written by no beni line; the page
shell is HTML. A `.mjs.map` is never an ES module, and Â§2's "every emitted file is `.mjs`" reads
"every emitted file a host loads"; a map is named for the module beside it and never stands alone.

**The format is Source Map v3** (ECMA-426): `version`, `file` (the module's base name), one entry in
`sources`, the same one in `sourcesContent`, `names`, `mappings`. No `sourceRoot`, no index maps, no
`ignoreList`. Columns on both sides are **UTF-16 code units**, which is what the format counts and
what a browser means by a column; a generated line ends at `\n`, `\r` and U+2028/U+2029, as a
JavaScript engine counts lines.

- **`sources`** names the `.beni` file relative to the map: for a file read from disk, the path
  from the map's directory to it, both made absolute against the working directory and normalised
  lexically (`../src/Main.beni` for `beni build src --out=out`), so Node's `--enable-source-maps`
  prints a path the developer can open; for a file embedded in the compiler (core, an embedded
  platform), `beni:///` and its store path (`beni:///core/List.beni`), a URL that names it
  honestly and that no server is asked for.
- **`sourcesContent`** always carries the module's text. The output tree is what a browser can
  reach â the source tree is not served, and core is not on disk at all â so without it DevTools
  would show an empty file.
- **`names`** gives a binding its beni name where the printed one differs: `Main$twice` is
  `twice`, `n$2` is `n`. A temporary the lowering invented (`$tâ¦`) has none. Two locals printed
  `x$2` and `x$5` are two entries. A **named function's first byte carries its name too** â the
  arrow after `const Main$twice = `, a `function` declaration's keyword â because an engine names a
  stack frame by the mapping at the start of the enclosing function (Node's does exactly that), so
  a crash in `describe` prints `at describe (â¦/Main.beni:17:13)` and not `at Main$describe`.

**Granularity: every statement and every expression whose `JsIr` node has a position.** `mark` runs
at the start of `statement`, `rawRecursive` and `expand` â the three places a node starts printing
â and records `(generated byte offset, source byte offset)`; a binding's name gets a second mark
at the name. A node the lowering invented (`Node.no_pos`) records nothing and is covered by the
mark before it. Where several nodes start at the same generated byte â a call and its callee, a
binary and its left operand â the **innermost** wins, since it is the token the reader sees first
there (`n * 2` maps to `n`, not to the `*` the binary is positioned on). The encoder drops a
segment that repeats the previous one's source position on the same generated line. What that
gives, by construction rather than by a list: a declaration maps to its name (its `const` and its
name to the definition's name token â `Lower.declarationAs` positions the binding there and the
value at its body); a call maps to its first token; a `case` arm's test maps to the arm's pattern
and its body to the arm's expression; `Debug.todo` and every other call maps to the call, which is
where a thrown error's frame points. **Markup** is lowered by the platform's lowering through the
interface (`boundary.md` Â§9.4), whose `at` positions each built node at the markup node it came
from: a hole's patch and mount code map to the hole (`{r.maybe}`), a template and its kind to the
element that opens it, and the walk the lowering invents between them to the mark before it.

*Amended 2026-10-17 (issue #94):* a **cached** module's marks are the ones its own printing
recorded. The printed text of every embedded module carries its marks in the checked core (Â§9, *The
embedded modules' printed text, in the pack*), each with the generated offset relative to its
unit's first byte and the identity of the name it carries; the join rebases the offsets and
rebuilds `names` in first-use order, one entry per identity, so the map is the one this subsection
describes, entry for entry. Nothing else moves: a build still writes one map per module with one
`SourceMap.write`, and `sources`, `sourcesContent` and the relative-URL rule are untouched.

**Determinism** (rule 5): the map is a function of the printed bytes, the marks (in print order)
and the source; `names` is numbered in first-use order; nothing reads thread timing. The only input
outside the build's arguments is the working directory, and it enters only as the common prefix
the relative URL cancels. That holds while the arguments are relative to it: an absolute one (a
`--platform=/â¦/page`) does not cancel, and a map names that file by its path from the output
tree, so moving the project relative to it changes the map â correctly, since the path is one the
developer can open. A test that hashes an output tree therefore keeps every disk source inside its
project (the `browser/` harness copies the `page` platform in, `tests/blackbox/browser.zig`).

**Cost**, measured 2026-10-01 on `zig build bench -- --generate=100000` (624 files, 100 159 lines,
one core, ReleaseFast): the `emit` line 34â37 ms without maps; the new `emit+maps` line, which
records the marks and writes every map, 10â14 ms more (â30%), of which `sourcesContent` is about
2.5 ms and the marks in the printer 2â4 ms. A whole cold `beni build --library` of the same tree:
182 â 208 ms at `--jobs=1`, 61 â 73 ms at `--jobs=8`, the difference including 627 more files
written. Size: 2.54 MB of maps beside 1.63 MB of JavaScript, 2.03 MB of it `sourcesContent`;
mappings average about 6 bytes a segment. A development build is not shipped, so this is disk and
write time, not page weight; `--no-source-maps` drops all of it.

**Tests.** `build_test`'s *a development build maps a crash in a case arm back to the beni line and
column* builds a program whose `case` arm calls `Debug.todo`, decodes `Main.mjs.map` with a VLQ
reader written in the test from the format alone, and pins where named spots of the module map â
the `Debug.todo` call, a call inside an arm, an arm's test, a declaration's name and its arrow,
both carrying `twice` â and then runs the program under Node's `--enable-source-maps` and pins the
crash's frames (`at describe (â¦Main.beni:17:13)`); it also checks a map beside every module and
none beside a sibling or the entry file. A neighbour pins `--no-source-maps` and the contradiction.
Every `emit/` development golden ends with its module's `//# sourceMappingURL=` line, and the
determinism test byte-compares the maps with everything else. Chrome is not in the gates:
`tests/browser/sourcemap-chrome.mjs <chrome> <out-dir>` (Chrome from `nix develop .#browser`)
serves a browser build, waits for its first uncaught exception over the DevTools protocol, and
resolves each frame through the `sourceMappingURL` Chrome reported in `Debugger.scriptParsed` â
run on 2026-10-01 against a page whose view calls `Debug.todo` from a hole, it printed
`Main$label /Main.mjs:17:41 -> /src/Main.beni:9:13` and `Main$view â¦ -> /src/Main.beni:17:9`, the
frames below them in `beni:///platforms/browser/Rt.beni`, and the sibling's and entry file's
frames `unmapped`. By hand: `beni serve`, open DevTools, and look for the `.beni` files in the
Sources panel under the page's origin (`src/`, where `../src/` lands at the server's root) and
under `beni://`; that half â the panel, breakpoints, stepping â has not been checked by a test.

**The flags.** A development build writes maps unless `--no-source-maps` is given; `--source-maps`
says so explicitly and is accepted; giving both is a usage error (exit 2). `--release` writes none,
and `--release --source-maps` is refused with exit 2 and a one-line message rather than accepted
while writing no `.map` â Â§2's original reason, kept for the half that is not built. *Amended
2026-10-15:* the refusal is gone; Â§11.2 gives what the pair writes.

**Deferred.** (1) **Release maps**: the one scope-hoisted file and the multi-file release layout
need the marks to survive Opt's dropped statements and inlined initialisers, compact printing's
inserted spaces, Rename's short names (whose `names` entry is then the long beni name â the point
of `names` in a minified build) and Â§9's per-module pieces joined into one file, which is the
"rebased once at join time" above; none of that is built. (2) **Hand-written JavaScript** is
unmapped in development (above) and, under `--release`, compacted by `Minify.zig`, which would then
owe a map of its own. (3) A crash screen (`Rt.crashScreen`, development only) shows the message and
points at the console, where DevTools already applies these maps to the stack; resolving frames on
the screen itself would need a map reader in the runtime and is not built. *Amended 2026-10-15:*
item (1) is Â§11.2, and item (2) is Â§11.2's *Hand-written JavaScript*, which states what this slice
maps and what it leaves unmapped.

### 11.2 Release maps (specified and built 2026-10-15)

*Issue #93, M5 (`fast-compiler.md` Â§13).* `beni build --release --source-maps` writes a Source Map
v3 file for each output file that the release build lowers from beni. `--release` alone writes no
map. **The flag does not change one byte of the code.** It adds the map files and one comment line
at the end of each mapped file, and nothing else. The `emit/release/` goldens and the run hashes
hold that for every build without the flag, and `build_test` holds it for the builds with it
(*Tests*, below). Code: `src/js/SourceMap.zig` (`writeJoined`), the printer's marks under compact
printing (`src/js/Print.zig`), and `Emitter.linkHoisted` (`src/js/Emit.zig`).

**What gets a map.** A release build has two layouts (Â§9), and each gets maps by its own rule.

- **The multi-file layout** (`--library`, and an application that Â§9 does not hoist): each `.mjs`
  lowered from a `.beni` module gets `<path>.mjs.map` beside it, exactly as Â§11.1 says. One source
  per map.
- **The one scope-hoisted file** (Â§9, *One scope-hoisted file under `--release`*): one map,
  `<entry>.map` beside the entry file (`_main.mjs.map`). Its `sources` has one entry for each
  emitted module that the file holds, in the order of the file. The modules that the file does not
  hold have no entry. A module that records no mark has no entry either, and its bytes are an
  unmapped stretch. Its text would only add to the map: a
  body copied out of `core/Debug` maps to its call, so `Debug.beni` often has nothing that maps to
  it.
- **No map:** the entry file of the multi-file layout and `_core/_derived.mjs`, for Â§11.1's reason
  (no beni line wrote them), and each hand-written file that the build writes as a file of its own
  (below).

*Amended 2026-10-17 (issue #94):* **a release build reads no emit row** (Â§9, *The embedded
modules' printed text, in the pack*). The release text is entangled with the specialiser, the
renamer and the hoist, so its marks are, and remain, the ones its own printing records â *What the
marks survive*, below, unchanged.

**Hand-written JavaScript.** Under `--release`, `Minify.zig` compacts a sibling and the runtimes
(Â§9, *Hand-written JavaScript under `--release`*). In development the file is copied, so the file
IS its source and needs no map (Â§11.1). The compacted file is not its source, but this slice does
not map it: `Minify` does not record token positions. So:

- A compacted hand-written file of its own (the multi-file layout, or a file Â§9 declines to hoist)
  gets no map, as in development. The debugger shows the compacted text.
- Inside the hoisted file, a hand-written piece and the bytes that the link step writes (the
  `const` aliases, `start(â¦)`, `run(main)`, `export{flush}`) are **unmapped**. Each such stretch
  starts with a one-field segment (ECMA-426: a segment with a generated column and nothing else).
  Without it, the last mapping of the module before the stretch would cover it, and a frame in the
  runtime would point at an unrelated beni line. An unmapped frame shows the compacted text.

A map from the compacted text back to the original `.js` file is deferred (item 1 below).

**What the marks survive.** The printer records the marks of Â§11.1 at the same sites, in the same
order. Each release pass changes the printed bytes, and each has a rule.

1. **Dropped bindings** (Â§9 item 1): the printer skips a dropped statement before it records a
   mark. So a dropped binding records nothing.
2. **Inlined initialisers** (Â§9 item 1, and *A function called once is written where it is
   called*): the initialiser prints at the use, and its nodes keep their own positions. So the
   inlined bytes map to the beni code that wrote them, not to the use. Â§11.1's innermost rule does
   this: the use's identifier and the initialiser start at the same byte, and the initialiser is
   marked last. A body that whole-program specialisation copies **into another module** cannot
   keep its positions, because a position is an offset into the source of one module. So each
   node of the copy takes the position of the call that the copy replaces (`Spec.Copy.site`).
   The copy maps to the call: `Debug.todo "â¦"`, written where it is called, maps its `throw` to
   that call, and the stack frame points at the line that the development build names (Â§11.1).
   Before this rule the copy had no position, and the mark before it covered it: the `throw`
   mapped to the `case` scrutinee. A map that names the other module's own line is item 2 of
   *Deferred*.
3. **Compact printing** (Â§9 item 3): the adjacency guard can put a space between a mark and the
   token that the mark is for. The guard moves the mark past the space, so the mark is on the
   token. A lookup of the token finds the same segment either way, but a tool that reads `names`
   reads it at the binding's own column. `closeBlock` removes the `;` before a `}`. It also
   removes a mark that it leaves past the end of the bytes, because such a mark was for a node
   that printed nothing (an `if` with empty arms and a test that only compares prints nothing
   under `--release`).
4. **Joined declarations** (Â§9 item 5, and the `for` head of *Compact statements*): each
   declarator in a run records what a `const` statement records in Â§11.1 â a mark on its name with
   the name's `names` entry, and, when its value is an arrow, the function's name on the arrow's
   mark. The run's keyword (`const`, `let`) maps where its first member does, as a `const`
   statement's keyword does in Â§11.1.
5. **Short names** (Â§9 item 2): under `--release` every binding prints a short name. So every
   binding that the printer marks at its declaration gets its beni name in `names`, a local as well
   as a module's top-level name. A temporary that the lowering invented (`$tâ¦`) still has no entry.
   A named function's first mapping carries its name, as in Â§11.1, so a stack frame under Node's
   `--enable-source-maps` names the beni function and not its short name.
6. **Decided branches** (Â§9, *Whole-program specialisation*): specialisation writes the operand
   that a decided `cond`, `&&` or `||` keeps in place of the node (`Spec.foldTo`). The node takes
   the kept operand's position too. The kept code is what runs, so it maps to where it was written
   and not to the test that decided it. A call kept this way is then the site of a copy into it
   (item 2). Before this rule, `if n > 100 then Aid.boom n` with `n` known to be 500 mapped the
   copied `Aid.boom` to the `>`, and the crash frame named the test's line. A node that an inline
   writes in place of a call keeps the call's position: the call is where the inlined code runs.

**The join.** The printer prints each module of the hoisted file on its own, with marks relative
to the module's own bytes (Â§9). The link step joins the pieces, and the map follows the join:

- each module piece is one stretch: its start in the file, the index of its source, its marks and
  its `names`;
- the encoder adds the stretch's start to each mark, and writes a source index delta when the
  source changes (ECMA-426: every field but the generated column is relative to its previous
  value across the whole map);
- the `names` of the stretches are joined in stretch order, and each mark's index moves by the
  count of names before its stretch. No name is shared between two stretches;
- a mark at or past the end of its stretch records nothing (the join removes a module's last
  newline, and nothing maps to it);
- when the last segment has fewer than five fields, `mappings` ends with `;`, in every release map
  of either layout (`SourceMap.Joined.end_line`). Node's reader (`node:module`'s `SourceMap`, which
  `--enable-source-maps` uses) ends a segment only at a `,` or a `;`. At the end of the string it
  reads the missing fields as zero deltas: a one-field segment repeats the one before it, so the
  link step's glue, the hoisted file's last stretch, mapped to the last beni line; and a four-field
  segment takes the name before it, which is the last segment of nearly every module map. The `;`
  closes the code's line, which the comment line follows. A development map ends as Â§11.1 has it;
  the same reading gives its last segment a name it does not have, which is a Â§11.1 defect and not
  this section's.

The encoder runs once, over the joined bytes. This is Â§11's "per-file chunks rebased once at join
time", and Â§10's chunks will use it for each chunk file.

**Format.** As Â§11.1, with two additions: more than one entry in `sources` (the hoisted file), and
the one-field segment. `sourcesContent` always carries each source's text, and `beni help` says so
on the `--source-maps` line. A release map is
written only when the user asks for it, and a map without the text shows an empty file. The user
who ships the map ships the source; the user who does not want that does not give the flag, or
does not deploy the `.map` files. The `sources` URLs follow Â§11.1: a disk source is relative to the
map, an embedded one is `beni:///` and its store path.

**The comment line.** Each mapped file ends with `//# sourceMappingURL=<basename>.map` and a
newline, after the file's own last newline. A browser fetches the map only when its developer tools
are open, so what a page pays is the comment line: about 35 bytes before compression.

**Determinism** (rule 5) as Â§11.1: the marks are in print order, the stretches in the order of the
file, and `names` in first-use order in each stretch. `--jobs` changes no byte of a map.

**Cost**, measured 2026-10-15. Instructions: user-space instructions (`perf_event_open`) of a
whole cold `beni build --no-cache --jobs=1` with the ReleaseSafe beni the gates run, the median of
5 runs, which differ by under 0.001%. Time: a ReleaseFast LLVM beni, the median of 11 and of 21
runs interleaved with the build without the flag; other builds ran on the machine (load 7â15), so
a time is Â± a few milliseconds, as large as the effect.

| Build | Instructions without â with maps | Time without â with maps | Code bytes | Map bytes | Of which `sourcesContent` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bench/corpus`, `--release --library`, 27 maps | 1 784.29 M â 1 832.99 M, **+2.73%** | 59.0 â 60.2 ms; `--jobs=1` 67.2 â 69.6 and 69.9 â 73.7 ms | 72 950 + 985 (the comment lines) | 305 483 | 234 180 (77%) |
| `examples/conduit`, `--release`, one map of 38 sources | 5 165.53 M â 5 273.57 M, **+2.09%** | 171.5 â 172.7 and 174.7 â 177.5 ms; `--jobs=1` 189.0 â 193.1 and 192.7 â 197.6 ms | 125 961 + 35 | 765 823 | 634 824 (83%) |
| `examples/sternhalma`, `--release`, one map of 19 sources | 1 270.52 M â 1 315.42 M, **+3.53%** | `--jobs=1` 51.4 â 52.6 ms | 24 154 + 35 | 455 904 | 411 256 (90%) |

So a release map costs about 1â5% of a build: +2.1% to +3.5% of its instructions, 1â5 ms of its
time. Most of its bytes are the sources' text. The mappings average 5.5 bytes a segment (conduit:
88 038 bytes for 15 747 segments; 1 933 `names` in 14 435 bytes). The page pays the comment line
only. The times were taken before a module with no mark lost its entry in `sources`; the
instructions and the bytes after it.

**Tests.** `build_test`:

- *a release build maps the one hoisted file back to each module's beni source* builds an
  application under `--release --source-maps` (with the hidden `--allow-debug`, for a crash),
  decodes `_main.mjs.map` with a VLQ reader written from the format, and pins where named spots of
  the one file map: calls, an inlined initialiser, a renamed local with its beni name, a run's
  keyword, each function's first byte with its name, the copied `Debug.todo`, a `for` head's
  keyword and its variables' beni names, and three unmapped stretches (the file's start, the
  runtime's and the link step's, the last one the map's last segment). A segment that starts
  before its spot fails it, and so does a spot that Node's own reader (`node:module`'s
  `SourceMap`) reads differently. It runs the program under Node's `--enable-source-maps` and pins
  the frames of the crash, and it pins the `sources`: a module with no mark is not one.
- *a branch that specialisation decides maps to the code it keeps* is item 6: `crash 500` keeps
  `Aid.boom n`, and the call and the crash frame map to 14:9, the line the development build
  names, and not to the test. A second program keeps `Aid.bad n` from `n > 100 && Aid.bad n`; it
  maps to 8:16 and not to the `&&`, which holds the `&&`/`||` fold site.
- *a release library build writes a map beside every module* builds `--release --library
  --source-maps` (the multi-file layout), pins named spots of `Lib.mjs`, and checks a map beside
  each module lowered from beni, core's included, and none beside the hand-written runtime.
- *--release writes a map only when asked, and asking changes no byte of the code* builds an
  application and a library with and without the flag, and with `--no-source-maps`. It checks that
  each file is the same but for the comment line, that the manifest is the only other file that
  differs, and that the maps are the same at `--jobs=1` and `--jobs=8`.

Unit tests hold the rules a program does not reach on purpose: `Print`'s *compact: a mark goes
past the guard's space, and with the `;` a block's end takes back*, and `SourceMap`'s join
tests. Each black-box claim above was checked red by a revert of its rule: the call site of a
copy, the guard's space, a run's keyword, a decided branch's position, the last `;` and a module
with no mark.

**The flags.** `--release --source-maps` writes the maps. `--release` alone writes none, and
`--release --no-source-maps` says so. `--source-maps` with `--no-source-maps` exits 2, with or
without `--release`, as in development.

**Deferred.**

1. **Maps for hand-written JavaScript under `--release`.** `Minify` would record the position of
   each token it keeps, as the printer does, and the hoisted map would get the `.js` file as one
   more source. The one-field segments of this slice mark where those stretches go.
2. **The other module's line for a body copied across modules.** `JsIr` positions are offsets
   into one source. A copy from another module maps to its call (item 2 above); to map it to the
   lines it came from, a position needs a source index with its offset.
3. **Parameter names.** A parameter is a `NameIndex` with no node in `JsIr`, so it has no position
   to mark, and `names` gives it no beni name. A debugger shows its short name.
4. **A map without the comment line** ("hidden" maps, for an error-reporting service that reads
   maps the page does not name). It needs a flag of its own.
5. **Â§10's chunks**: each chunk file gets a map by the join above.

## 12. Testing

The boundary that matters is the second one: **compile, run under Node, assert what it printed.**
This is what Elm's deleted suite never had and it is why `boundary.md` puts the Node platform before
the optimiser.

New corpus kinds:

```
tests/corpus/run/<Name>.beni + <Name>.expected     compile, run, stdout must match
tests/corpus/emit/<Name>.beni + <Name>.js          the extracted declaration, for shape claims
```

`run/` is the default for anything about behaviour. `emit/` is for claims running cannot observe â
that a self-recursive function became a loop, that a constructor emits a uniform shape, that a
saturated call emitted a direct call and not an adapter. Goldens are **extracted and normalised, not
whole-file**, which is the discipline Elm's suite lacked and resented.

The one deviation, recorded rather than hidden: an `emit/` golden is the fixture's **own module**
